message.content: <local-command-caveat>Caveat: The messages below were generated by the user while running local commands. DO NOT respond to these messages or otherwise consider them in your response unless the user explicitly asks you to.</local-command-caveat>

<local-command-stdout>Set effort level to max (this session only): Maximum capability with deepest reasoning. May use excessive tokens resulting in long response times or overthinking. Use sparingly for the hardest tasks.</local-command-stdout>

./build/andes-sim 
move doctor from developer to user

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- qemu-runner: Use this agent when you need to run a RISC-V ELF binary through Andes QEMU and get its output. Always use this agent instead of running QEMU directly, as it handles the semihosting fd 9 output capture quirk in Claude Code's sandbox.

Examples:

- assistant: *builds a test binary*
  assistant: "Let me use the qemu-runner agent to execute the binary and check the output"

- user: "Run this ELF at VLEN=512"
  assistant: "I'll use the qemu-runner agent to run it" (Tools: Bash, Read) (Tools: Bash)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.content:
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Release-surface contract: the andes-sim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
3	# user-facing commands (run, list) and never the third-party simulator name
4	# "verilator". Developer commands (build, test, doctor) appear only under
5	# ANDES_SIM_DEV=1; the unfinished ROADMAP commands (profile, cluster, archive,
6	# replay, estimate) appear in no help at all. The cycle-accurate engine is
7	# presented as "vsim" everywhere -- proven end to end with a fake engine that
8	# self-describes as "verilator" and must come back out as vsim:.
9	set -uo pipefail
10	
11	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
12	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
13	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
14	
15	BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
16	
17	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
18	
19	# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
20	has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
21	no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }
22	
23	# 1. release --help: run + list only, the dev hint, and no "verilator".
24	H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
25	has '^  run '  "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'run'"
26	has '^  list ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'list'"
27	for c in build test doctor state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
28	  has "^  $c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
29	done
30	no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
31	has 'ANDES_SIM_DEV' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing developer-commands hint"
32	ok "release --help: run/list only, dev hint, no verilator"
33	
34	# 2. ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 --help: adds build/test/doctor; hidden five stay hidden.
35	D=$(ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
36	for c in run list build test doctor state-diff; do
37	  has "^  $c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing '$c'"
38	done
39	for c in profile cluster archive replay estimate; do

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-surface contract: the andes-sim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
# user-facing commands (run, list) and never the third-party simulator name
# "verilator". Developer commands (build, test, doctor) appear only under
# ANDES_SIM_DEV=1; the unfinished ROADMAP commands (profile, cluster, archive,
# replay, estimate) appear in no help at all. The cycle-accurate engine is
# presented as "vsim" everywhere -- proven end to end with a fake engine that
# self-describes as "verilator" and must come back out as vsim:.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }

# 1. release --help: run + list only, the dev hint, and no "verilator".
H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
has '^  run '  "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'run'"
has '^  list ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'list'"
for c in build test doctor state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
done
no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'ANDES_SIM_DEV' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing developer-commands hint"
ok "release --help: run/list only, dev hint, no verilator"

# 2. ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 --help: adds build/test/doctor; hidden five stay hidden.
D=$(ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
for c in run list build test doctor state-diff; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing '$c'"
done
for c in profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" && fail "dev --help: leaked hidden command '$c'"
done
no_word "$D" || fail "dev --help: leaked 'verilator'"
ok "dev --help: adds build/test/doctor, hidden cmds stay hidden, no verilator"

# 3. run --help: the --engine example reads vsim:, never verilator:; the
# --trigger menu offers only implemented triggers (simpoint is unfinished).
RH=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
has 'vsim:' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing vsim: example"
no_word "$RH" || fail "run --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'simpoint' "$RH" && fail "run --help: leaked unfinished trigger 'simpoint':"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mem-size' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --mem-size:"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mmap-size' "$RH" && fail "run --help: retired --mmap-size alias should stay hidden:"$'\n'"$RH"
ok "run --help: vsim: example, no verilator/simpoint, --mem-size documented"

# 4. list models: composition cells read vsim (never verilator), and NOTES show
# user-facing model traits only -- no implementation detail, no unfinished trigger.
LM=$("$BIN" list models 2>&1)
has 'vsim' "$LM" || fail "list models: missing vsim"
no_word "$LM" || fail "list models: leaked 'verilator'"
for d in 'transparent passthrough' 'pure from reset' 'simpoint'; do
  has "$d" "$LM" && fail "list models: leaked implementation detail/unfinished trigger '$d':"$'\n'"$LM"
done
ok "list models: vsim, no verilator, no implementation detail, no simpoint"

# 5. list engines end to end: a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator"
# must surface as vsim: (the single normalization point), proving --engine /
# errors / list all speak the product name with no real sim_* needed.
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat >"$TMP/sim_fake" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"verilator:fakecfg","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc","icount"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
EOF
chmod +x "$TMP/sim_fake"
LE=$(ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" list engines 2>&1)
has 'vsim:fakecfg' "$LE" || fail "list engines: fake not renamed to vsim:fakecfg:"$'\n'"$LE"
no_word "$LE" || fail "list engines: leaked 'verilator':"$'\n'"$LE"
# Triggers are a hybrid-MODEL option, not an engine attribute: `list engines`
# carries no TRIGGERS column (and so never leaks the unfinished simpoint trigger
# that the built-in qemu row used to advertise).
has 'TRIGGERS' "$LE" && fail "list engines: TRIGGERS is a hybrid-model option, not an engine column:"$'\n'"$LE"
has 'simpoint'  "$LE" && fail "list engines: leaked unfinished trigger 'simpoint':"$'\n'"$LE"
ok "list engines: a verilator-self-describing engine is shown as vsim:, no TRIGGERS column"

# 6. `list fixtures` is a developer target (internal test ELFs, not user
# workloads): release hides it; ANDES_SIM_DEV reveals it.
printf '%s\n' "$H" | grep -qw fixtures && fail "release --help: leaked 'fixtures' target"
LH=$("$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$LH" | grep -qw fixtures && fail "release list --help: leaked 'fixtures':"$'\n'"$LH"
has 'models' "$LH" || fail "release list --help: missing 'models' target:"$'\n'"$LH"
expect 2 "unknown target 'fixtures'" "$BIN" list fixtures
DLH=$(ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$DLH" | grep -qw fixtures || fail "dev list --help: missing 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$DLH"
ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list fixtures >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "dev: list fixtures should succeed"
ok "list: fixtures is dev-only (release hides it; ANDES_SIM_DEV reveals it)"

ok "release surface (hide verilator + release/dev command split)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Differential parity harness: the closed-loop flywheel for the rewrite.
#
# Runs the same args through the Python golden (hsim) and the C++ driver
# (build/andes-sim), then diffs stdout+stderr and the exit code. As each
# later feature ports a subcommand, it adds its cases below; a green parity
# run is the evidence the C++ path matches the reference it replaces.
#
# F0 ships the harness skeleton with zero cases, so it exits 0 vacuously.
# Override the two binaries via the GOLDEN / NEW env vars if needed.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

GOLDEN="${GOLDEN:-$ROOT/hsim.py}"        # Python reference driver
NEW="${NEW:-$ROOT/build/andes-sim}"   # C++ driver under test

# Parity compares the full developer surface against the golden (which exposes
# everything), so run the C++ driver in dev mode -- e.g. so the dev-only
# `list fixtures` target resolves on both sides.
export ANDES_SIM_DEV=1

pass=0
fail=0

# compare <case-name> -- <args...>
# Invoke GOLDEN and NEW with identical args; require matching stdout+stderr
# and exit code. Records a pass/fail; never aborts so all cases report.
compare() {
  local name="$1"
  shift
  [ "${1:-}" = "--" ] && shift
  local g_out g_rc n_out n_rc
  g_out=$("$GOLDEN" "$@" 2>&1)
  g_rc=$?
  n_out=$("$NEW" "$@" 2>&1)
  n_rc=$?
  if [ "$g_rc" != "$n_rc" ] || [ "$g_out" != "$n_out" ]; then
    echo "[DIFF] $name (golden rc=$g_rc, new rc=$n_rc)"
    fail=$((fail + 1))
    return
  fi
  pass=$((pass + 1))
}

# compare_carried <case-name> -- <args...>
# Like compare, but the C++ driver appends sections the Python golden lacks
# (doctor's engines readout). Scope parity to the carried-over report by
# truncating NEW at (and including) the `Summary:` line before diffing.
compare_carried() {
  local name="$1"
  shift
  [ "${1:-}" = "--" ] && shift
  local g_out g_rc n_full n_rc n_out
  g_out=$("$GOLDEN" "$@" 2>&1)
  g_rc=$?
  n_full=$("$NEW" "$@" 2>&1)
  n_rc=$?
  n_out=$(printf '%s\n' "$n_full" | awk '{print} /^Summary:/{exit}')
  if [ "$g_rc" != "$n_rc" ] || [ "$g_out" != "$n_out" ]; then
    echo "[DIFF] $name (golden rc=$g_rc, new rc=$n_rc)"
    fail=$((fail + 1))
    return
  fi
  pass=$((pass + 1))
}

# --- parity cases (populated per feature) ---
compare "list fixtures" -- list fixtures      # F1
compare_carried "doctor" -- doctor            # F3
compare "build dry default" -- build --dry-run                  # F4
for w in all qemu vsim plugin simpoint fixtures; do
  compare "build dry $w" -- build --dry-run --what "$w"
done

echo "parity: $pass matched, $fail differed"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

```

Subcommand cheat sheet:

| Command                                                          | What it does                                                        |
|------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `./andes-sim list <models|engines>`                              | List the 3 models, or the discovered engines with their hardware params (XLEN/VLEN/DLEN/ELEN; `-` = not reported). |
| `./andes-sim build [--what TARGET] [--dry-run]`                  | Build artifacts; targets: `all`, `qemu`, `vsim`, `plugin`, `simpoint`, `fixtures`, `runtime`. |
| `./andes-sim run --model fast|cycle|hybrid [--trigger marker|pc|icount] [--engine ID] [--gdb [--gdb-port PORT]] <elf>` | Run one ELF on a model (hybrid = QEMU -> vsim handoff; --gdb pauses at startup for a debugger: fast opens QEMU's GDB stub on port 1234, cycle halts the hart and opens vsim's JTAG port (9104) then execs `$ICEMAN`, a GDB server (use a modern OpenOCD); --gdb not supported with hybrid). |
| `bash scripts/run_e2e.sh` (env: `FILTER`, `MODE`, `JOBS`)        | Run the e2e suite (the `test` subcommand is not yet ported to the C++ driver; see Section 6). |

Run `./andes-sim <cmd> -h` for the full flag list of a subcommand (set
`ANDES_SIM_DEV=1` to see the developer commands). The SimPoint pipeline
(`run --mode simpoint`, `estimate`, `profile`, `cluster`, `archive`,
`replay`) still lives in the Python reference driver `./hsim.py` until
the C++ port lands. The rest of this guide (Sections 1-7) documents the
underlying scripts and is useful when you need to bypass `./andes-sim`
(custom env vars, single-leg debugging, alternative CPU YAML, etc.).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-surface contract: the andes-sim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
# user-facing commands (run, list) and never the third-party simulator name
# "verilator". Developer commands (build, test, doctor) appear only under
# ANDES_SIM_DEV=1; the unfinished ROADMAP commands (profile, cluster, archive,
# replay, estimate) appear in no help at all. The cycle-accurate engine is
# presented as "vsim" everywhere -- proven end to end with a fake engine that
# self-describes as "verilator" and must come back out as vsim:.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }

# 1. release --help: run + list only, the dev hint, and no "verilator".
H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
has '^  run '  "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'run'"
has '^  list ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'list'"
for c in build test doctor state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
done
no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'ANDES_SIM_DEV' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing developer-commands hint"
ok "release --help: run/list only, dev hint, no verilator"

# 2. ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 --help: adds build/test/doctor; hidden five stay hidden.
D=$(ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
for c in run list build test doctor state-diff; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing '$c'"
done
for c in profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" && fail "dev --help: leaked hidden command '$c'"
done
no_word "$D" || fail "dev --help: leaked 'verilator'"
ok "dev --help: adds build/test/doctor, hidden cmds stay hidden, no verilator"

# 3. run --help: the --engine example reads vsim:, never verilator:; the
# --trigger menu offers only implemented triggers (simpoint is unfinished).
RH=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
has 'vsim:' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing vsim: example"
no_word "$RH" || fail "run --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'simpoint' "$RH" && fail "run --help: leaked unfinished trigger 'simpoint':"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mem-size' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --mem-size:"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mmap-size' "$RH" && fail "run --help: retired --mmap-size alias should stay hidden:"$'\n'"$RH"
ok "run --help: vsim: example, no verilator/simpoint, --mem-size documented"

# 4. list models: composition cells read vsim (never verilator), and NOTES show
# user-facing model traits only -- no implementation detail, no unfinished trigger.
LM=$("$BIN" list models 2>&1)
has 'vsim' "$LM" || fail "list models: missing vsim"
no_word "$LM" || fail "list models: leaked 'verilator'"
for d in 'transparent passthrough' 'pure from reset' 'simpoint'; do
  has "$d" "$LM" && fail "list models: leaked implementation detail/unfinished trigger '$d':"$'\n'"$LM"
done
ok "list models: vsim, no verilator, no implementation detail, no simpoint"

# 5. list engines end to end: a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator"
# must surface as vsim: (the single normalization point), proving --engine /
# errors / list all speak the product name with no real sim_* needed.
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat >"$TMP/sim_fake" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"verilator:fakecfg","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc","icount"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
EOF
chmod +x "$TMP/sim_fake"
LE=$(ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" list engines 2>&1)
has 'vsim:fakecfg' "$LE" || fail "list engines: fake not renamed to vsim:fakecfg:"$'\n'"$LE"
no_word "$LE" || fail "list engines: leaked 'verilator':"$'\n'"$LE"
# Triggers are a hybrid-MODEL option, not an engine attribute: `list engines`
# carries no TRIGGERS column (and so never leaks the unfinished simpoint trigger
# that the built-in qemu row used to advertise).
has 'TRIGGERS' "$LE" && fail "list engines: TRIGGERS is a hybrid-model option, not an engine column:"$'\n'"$LE"
has 'simpoint'  "$LE" && fail "list engines: leaked unfinished trigger 'simpoint':"$'\n'"$LE"
ok "list engines: a verilator-self-describing engine is shown as vsim:, no TRIGGERS column"

# 6. `list fixtures` is a developer target (internal test ELFs, not user
# workloads): release hides it; ANDES_SIM_DEV reveals it.
printf '%s\n' "$H" | grep -qw fixtures && fail "release --help: leaked 'fixtures' target"
LH=$("$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$LH" | grep -qw fixtures && fail "release list --help: leaked 'fixtures':"$'\n'"$LH"
has 'models' "$LH" || fail "release list --help: missing 'models' target:"$'\n'"$LH"
expect 2 "unknown target 'fixtures'" "$BIN" list fixtures
DLH=$(ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$DLH" | grep -qw fixtures || fail "dev list --help: missing 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$DLH"
ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list fixtures >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "dev: list fixtures should succeed"
ok "list: fixtures is dev-only (release hides it; ANDES_SIM_DEV reveals it)"

ok "release surface (hide verilator + release/dev command split)"

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(andes_sim CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release)

  hybrid.cpp

# Shared ABI header lives at <repo>/include/hybrid/state_abi.h, two levels up.

target_compile_options(andes-sim PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)

# bootstrap consumed by setup.sh and `andes-sim build --what driver` (wired in
# F14). Out-of-tree build under build/driver; the binary is redirected to
# build/andes-sim via CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
BUILD="$ROOT/build/driver"

cmake -S "$ROOT/driver" -B "$BUILD" \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY="$ROOT/build" \
  >/dev/null

cmake --build "$BUILD" -j"$(nproc)"

file.content:
# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andes-sim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andes-sim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andes-sim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andes-sim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode \
               rt_trap_ecall

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandes_sim_runtime.a) with the

toolUseResult.originalFile:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F7 contract: `run --mode fast` -- QEMU-only, transparent passthrough.
# Three layers:
#
#   1. run-test (unit, fast): passthrough_argv fills the qemu `standalone`
#      invoke template ({bin}/{elf}) and appends the post-`--` engine args
#      verbatim -- including a `-gdb tcp::N -S` gdbstub. Pure, no spawn.
#   2. CLI error paths (no engine needed): missing --mode, unknown model,
#      missing ELF, an extra positional, and engine!=qemu each exit 2 with a
#      clear message.
#   3. real passthrough (needs built qemu + a fixture): launch
#      `run --mode fast ELF -- -gdb tcp::PORT -S`; the gdbstub port opens and
#      qemu halts at reset -- the done-when "port opens, halts, debugger
#      connects". exec_passthrough's exit-code propagation is already covered
#      by the F5 infra test (and observed here only indirectly).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
RUNTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andes-sim-run-test"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit: the argv-assembly contract carries the passthrough behavior
[ -x "$RUNTEST" ] || fail "missing unit-test binary: $RUNTEST"
"$RUNTEST" || fail "run unit tests (passthrough_argv) failed"

# assert `$BIN run ...` exits with $1 and its combined output matches regex $2
expect_rc_match() {
  local want_rc="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want_rc" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want_rc for [$*]: $out"
  echo "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "output missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# 2. CLI error paths (deterministic; no qemu)
expect_rc_match 2 'model .* is required'    "$BIN" run
expect_rc_match 2 "unknown model 'bogus'"    "$BIN" run --mode bogus p.elf
expect_rc_match 2 'missing ELF'              "$BIN" run --mode fast
expect_rc_match 2 'engine args go after --'  "$BIN" run --mode fast a.elf b.elf
expect_rc_match 2 "engine must be 'qemu'"    "$BIN" run --mode fast --engine vsim:x p.elf

# 3. real passthrough: a frozen-at-reset gdbstub port opens (guarded on artifacts)
QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"
if [ -x "$QEMU" ] && [ -f "$ELF" ]; then
  PORT=$(( 40000 + (RANDOM % 20000) ))
  BG=""
  cleanup() { [ -n "${BG:-}" ] && kill "$BG" 2>/dev/null; pkill -f "tcp::$PORT" 2>/dev/null; true; }
  trap cleanup EXIT
  # -S halts the cpu at reset, so the stub listens regardless of the ELF body.
  "$BIN" run --mode fast "$ELF" -- -gdb "tcp::$PORT" -S </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
  BG=$!
  opened=0
  for _ in $(seq 1 40); do
    if timeout 1 bash -c ">/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/$PORT" 2>/dev/null; then opened=1; break; fi
    sleep 0.25
  done
  cleanup; trap - EXIT; wait "$BG" 2>/dev/null
  [ "$opened" -eq 1 ] || fail "fast passthrough: gdbstub port $PORT never opened"
  echo "[ok] real fast passthrough: qemu gdbstub halted + listening on :$PORT"
else
  echo "[skip] real fast run: qemu and/or fixture not built ($QEMU / $ELF)"
fi

ok "F7 run --mode fast"

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	* Always update docs/USER_GUIDE.md if something changed.
5	
6	## Repository Overview
7	
8	Andes hybrid RISC-V co-simulator: QEMU 9.x (functional, MHz-level) + vsim (SystemC + Verilator, cycle-accurate) share architectural state across a magic-CSR boundary. The system runs a two-phase handoff: **QEMU1** (drain on CSR/PC trigger) -> **vsim** (resume + execute + drain). The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta; there is no QEMU2 leg (the handback was removed).
9	
10	Two Git submodules:
11	- `QEMU/` - QEMU fork hosting the TCG plugin (branch: `hybrid`)
12	- `verilator/` - vsim sources; `hybrid/` subdirs hold the plugin and test fixtures
13	- `tools/simpoint/` - SimPoint 3.2 (UCSD) clustering binary; pinned to upstream `17783e5`
14	
15	Shared ABI lives at `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (not inside either submodule).
16	
17	## Build Commands
18	
19	**Primary path (`./andes-sim`)** -- the end-user driver (C++, self-builds on
20	first use), used in all user-facing docs. The retired Python driver is kept
21	as `hsim.py`, the byte-parity golden (`tests/andes_sim/parity.sh`); the
22	SimPoint pipeline (`run --mode simpoint`, `estimate`, `profile`, `cluster`,
23	`archive`, `replay`) still runs only there until the C++ port lands.
24	
25	```sh
26	./andes-sim build                  # builds qemu, vsim, plugin, simpoint, fixtures
27	./andes-sim test                   # full e2e suite (defaults: MODE=both, JOBS=8)
28	./andes-sim run --mode fast|cycle|hybrid [--trigger marker|pc|icount] [--engine ID] <elf>
29	./andes-sim list <models|engines>
30	```
31	
32	**Developer escape hatch** -- the underlying scripts. Use these when
33	working on the build system, the harness, or a single leg in isolation:
34	
35	```sh
36	# Build everything (qemu -> vsim -> plugin -> simpoint)
37	source ./setup.sh
38	
39	# Build individual components
40	./scripts/build_qemu.sh                              # QEMU (configure + make -j64)
41	./scripts/build_vsim.sh                              # vsim (Docker/podman, runs ./build.sh inside container)
42	make -C qemu_plugin QEMU_ROOT="$PWD/QEMU"  # TCG plugin (out-of-tree); QEMU_ROOT must be absolute (make -C chdirs first)
43	./scripts/build_simpoint.sh                          # SimPoint clustering binary (g++ on host)
44	
45	# Build RISC-V ELF test fixtures
46	make -C tests/fixtures              # all fixtures
47	make -C tests/fixtures rt_c_v_regs.elf  # single fixture
48	
49	# Clean
50	source ./setup.sh clean [qemu|vsim|plugin|simpoint|all]
51	```
52	
53	**Outputs:**
54	- `build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64`
55	- `verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium` (or other CPU variant)
56	- `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so`
57	- `tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint`
58	
59	`scripts/build_vsim.sh` is Docker-based (podman). It builds an image from `verilator/Dockerfile` (target `env`) then runs `./build.sh` inside it, mounting the repo at `/work` and `include/` as `/include:ro`.
60	
61	## Running Tests
62	
63	```sh
64	# All e2e tests in parallel (auto-detects job count from nproc + /dev/shm headroom)
65	bash scripts/run_e2e.sh
66	
67	# Run with specific options
68	JOBS=4 MODE=marker bash scripts/run_e2e.sh         # 4-way parallel, marker-mode only
69	JOBS=1 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh                  # sequential (debug)
70	FILTER=rt_c_v bash scripts/run_e2e.sh           # regex filter on fixture name
71	LOG_DIR=/tmp/my-logs bash scripts/run_e2e.sh    # custom log directory
72	
73	# Unit tests (inside vsim build container)
74	# The container build runs: cmake --build build -j
75	# To run ctest directly after build:
76	#   podman run ... ./build.sh && podman exec ... ctest --test-dir build -L hybrid-e2e
77	```
78	
79	**Important:** on a high-core-count machine (128+ cores) `default_jobs()` computes `min(nproc, /dev/shm_free/256MB)` which can reach 128+. Running that many vsim Verilator processes simultaneously saturates CPU and causes timeouts. Use `JOBS=8` (or lower) as a practical cap: `JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`.
80	
81	`scripts/run_e2e.sh` exits 0 only when all tests pass. Logs go to a `mktemp` directory under `/tmp`; path is printed at the start of each run. Each test's full output lands in `$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log`.
82	
83	**Manual driver tests**: `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh` cover the C++ driver (parity vs the golden + feature contracts); `tests/hsim/test_hsim_*.sh` are the retired golden's own per-feature smoke tests (they now invoke `hsim.py`). Both families run manually during driver development, not wired into `scripts/run_e2e.sh`. Each script is self-contained (sources `setup.sh` artifacts, runs one subcommand, asserts on stdout). The same convention applies to `tests/plugin/test_plugin_*.sh` (QEMU-plugin-only smoke tests).
84	
85	## Architecture
86	
87	### Two-Phase Handoff
88	
89	```
90	QEMU1 --(state file + shared mmap)--> vsim (resume + run ROI + drain)
91	```
92	
93	1. **QEMU plugin** (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`) - TCG plugin. On the marker trigger (`slti x0, x0, 0x5A0`) or PC-trigger, drains QEMU's architectural state into a binary `hybrid_state_v1` struct written to `--outfile`.
94	2. **vsim handoff controller** (`src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp`) - Detects the trigger inside vsim, pauses the hart via DMI, then calls `ResumeDriver` to restore state.
95	3. **ResumeDriver** (`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`) - Writes GPRs/FPRs/CSRs/V-state into the vsim hart via RISC-V Debug Module Abstract Commands and Program Buffer.
96	4. **StateDrain** (`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`) - On vsim exit trigger, reads back the full architectural state via DMI Abstract Commands into `hybrid_state_v1`. This is the end of the run: the cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` minus QEMU1's drained `mcycle`. The old QEMU2 resume leg was removed entirely.
97	
98	**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes the CSRs the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mscratch` (L23), `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie`/`mip` (L24), `mcycle`, `minstret`, `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags, gated on `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`; L20), and the Andes machine-setup CSRs `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA) + `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0) (L21). The cache pair matters for the cycle figure, not correctness: crt0 enables the L1 I/D caches via `mcache_ctl`, but that write runs on the cache-less functional engine, so without transporting it vsim resumes at the ROI with caches at their reset default (disabled) and the whole window runs uncached -- inflating the cycle count severalfold. All are tolerant writes: an engine without a given custom CSR mirrors the write as a no-op. In the trap-free ROI these writable M-mode CSRs are ordinary read/write state, so they round-trip fully: restored at resume, re-read at drain (`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough`), and compared by `--verify` (`state_diff`). Two verify-side exceptions: `mip` is restored + re-read but NOT compared -- its pending bits are hardware/platform-driven (the timer bit tracks elapsed time, which advances differently in QEMU's functional clock vs vsim's cycle clock), so comparing it would false-positive; and `mtvec` is restored but not re-drained. The QEMU plugin still drains `medeleg`/`mideleg`/`satp` into `hybrid_state_v1`, but those are S-mode CSRs the default M-only engine (`ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`) does not implement, so they are not restored -- they remain in `hybrid_state_v1` only as the drained record, deferred to the S/U-envelope work. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free, interrupt-free, and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.
99

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-surface contract: the andes-sim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
# user-facing commands (run, list, doctor) and never the third-party simulator
# name "verilator". Developer commands (build, test, state-diff) appear only under
# ANDES_SIM_DEV=1; the unfinished ROADMAP commands (profile, cluster, archive,
# replay, estimate) appear in no help at all. The cycle-accurate engine is
# presented as "vsim" everywhere -- proven end to end with a fake engine that
# self-describes as "verilator" and must come back out as vsim:.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }

# 1. release --help: run + list + doctor, the dev hint, and no "verilator".
H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
has '^  run '    "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'run'"
has '^  list '   "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'list'"
has '^  doctor ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'doctor'"
for c in build test state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
done
no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'ANDES_SIM_DEV' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing developer-commands hint"
ok "release --help: run/list/doctor, dev hint, no verilator"

# 2. ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 --help: adds build/test/state-diff; doctor still shows
# (now release-tier, always listed); the hidden five stay hidden.
D=$(ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
for c in run list doctor build test state-diff; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing '$c'"
done
for c in profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" && fail "dev --help: leaked hidden command '$c'"
done
no_word "$D" || fail "dev --help: leaked 'verilator'"
ok "dev --help: adds build/test/state-diff, doctor still shown, hidden cmds hidden, no verilator"

# 3. run --help: the --engine example reads vsim:, never verilator:; the
# --trigger menu offers only implemented triggers (simpoint is unfinished).
RH=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
has 'vsim:' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing vsim: example"
no_word "$RH" || fail "run --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'simpoint' "$RH" && fail "run --help: leaked unfinished trigger 'simpoint':"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mem-size' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --mem-size:"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mmap-size' "$RH" && fail "run --help: retired --mmap-size alias should stay hidden:"$'\n'"$RH"

# 4. list models: composition cells read vsim (never verilator), and NOTES show
# user-facing model traits only -- no implementation detail, no unfinished trigger.
LM=$("$BIN" list models 2>&1)
has 'vsim' "$LM" || fail "list models: missing vsim"
no_word "$LM" || fail "list models: leaked 'verilator'"
for d in 'transparent passthrough' 'pure from reset' 'simpoint'; do
  has "$d" "$LM" && fail "list models: leaked implementation detail/unfinished trigger '$d':"$'\n'"$LM"
done

# must surface as vsim: (the single normalization point), proving --engine /

TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat >"$TMP/sim_fake" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"verilator:fakecfg","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc","icount"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'

ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list fixtures >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "dev: list fixtures should succeed"

/* andes_sim/ROI.h - ROI markers for cycle measurement.
 *
 * andes_sim_ROI_begin()/andes_sim_ROI_end() delimit the region of
 * interest. On `--model hybrid --trigger marker` the simulator switches
 * QEMU -> vsim at begin and drains at end; the reported window_cycles
 * covers exactly the span between the two markers.
 *
 * The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1).
 * An rd=x0 instruction discards its result, so each marker is an
 * architectural NOP on every conforming core: the SAME binary runs
 * unmodified on --model fast, --model cycle, and real silicon.
 *
 * Cycle-attribution contract: the "memory" clobber pins memory accesses
 * across the marker but NOT register-only computation -- the compiler may
 * hoist a register-resident kernel out of the span. To keep a kernel
 * inside the measured window, anchor it through memory (read inputs /
 * write outputs inside the span) or call it as a noinline function
 * between the markers.
 */

#ifndef ANDES_SIM_ROI_H
#define ANDES_SIM_ROI_H

static inline void andes_sim_ROI_begin(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A0\n" ::: "memory");
}

static inline void andes_sim_ROI_end(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A1\n" ::: "memory");
}

#endif /* ANDES_SIM_ROI_H */

#
# pc uses handoff_roundtrip.elf's own markers as the boundaries (_start =
# the enter marker 0x100000, 0x10000c = the exit marker), so pc reproduces marker's
# switch points exactly -- and exercises BOTH symbol and 0x resolution.
set -uo pipefail

# 2. validation error paths -- real binary, but every case errors before a spawn

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F9 contract: `run --mode hybrid` -- orchestrate a QEMU1 -> vsim handoff (no
# QEMU2) and print the one-line window-cycle figure for the marker | pc | icount
# triggers. Three layers:
#
#   1. unit (fast, no spawn): the elf-syms boundary resolver, hybrid_trigger
#      (CLI -> Trigger, incl. pc symbol resolution + icount defaults), the
#      trigger->argv mapping (plan-test), and the new CLI flags (cli-test).
#   2. validation error paths via the real binary, all exiting BEFORE any spawn:
#      missing ELF, pc without boundaries, an undefined pc symbol, simpoint
#      (F11, not yet), and an unknown trigger.
#   3. real handoff + golden parity (guarded): run marker/pc/icount through both
#      ./hsim.py (the Python golden) and andes-sim and assert identical window
#      cycle numbers, plus the new output format. Skipped when the qemu/vsim/
#      plugin artifacts or the golden driver are not built.
#
# pc uses handoff_roundtrip.elf's own markers as the boundaries (_start =
# the enter marker 0x100000, 0x10000c = the exit marker), so pc reproduces marker's
# switch points exactly -- and exercises BOTH symbol and 0x resolution.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"  # asm fixture
CELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_matmul.elf"       # C fixture (needs shared mmap)
SPIN="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/icount_spin.elf"
ENG=vsim:ax45mpv_premium  # the engine ./hsim.py resolves by default

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit tests (the F9 pure cores)
for t in elf-syms hybrid plan cli; do
  "$ROOT/build/driver/andes-sim-$t-test" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || fail "unit test andes-sim-$t-test failed"
done
echo "[ok] unit: elf-syms, hybrid_trigger, trigger->argv (plan), CLI flags"

# 2. validation error paths -- real binary, but every case errors before a spawn
# (expect: assert rc + output regex; shared helper from tests/lib/log.sh)
expect 2 'ELF not found'        "$BIN" run --mode hybrid /no/such.elf
expect 2 'engine args go after' "$BIN" run --mode hybrid a.elf b.elf
expect 2 'requires --pc-start'  "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger pc "$ELF"
expect 2 'not defined' "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger pc \
  --pc-start nope_xyz --pc-end _start "$ELF"
expect 2 'F11'              "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger simpoint "$ELF"
expect 2 'unknown trigger'  "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger bogus "$ELF"
expect 2 'marker or pc'        "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger icount \
  --kanata /tmp/k "$SPIN"
expect 2 'requires --kanata' "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
  --objdump /tmp/o "$ELF"
echo "[ok] validation: missing ELF, pc boundaries, bad symbol, simpoint/unknown trigger, kanata/objdump"

# 3. real handoff + golden parity (guarded on built artifacts)
QEMU="$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64"
SIM="$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
PLUGIN="$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so"
if [ -x "$QEMU" ] && [ -x "$SIM" ] && [ -f "$PLUGIN" ] && [ -x "$ROOT/hsim.py" ]; then
  # Pull the window/kernel cycle integer from either driver's "] N  (vsim..."
  # line (golden marker/pc say "kernel_cycles", icount/andes say "window_cycles";
  # the number's position is identical).
  cyc() { grep -oE '\] [0-9]+  \(' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | head -1; }
  check_parity() {  # LABEL GOLDEN_NUM ANDES_NUM
    [ -n "$2" ] || fail "$1: golden produced no cycle number"
    [ -n "$3" ] || fail "$1: andes-sim produced no cycle number"
    [ "$2" = "$3" ] || fail "$1: cycle mismatch golden=$2 andes=$3"
    echo "[ok] $1 parity: $3 cycles (golden == andes-sim)"
  }

  # marker -- also assert the new output format (window_cycles + PASS line)
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim.py run --mode marker "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" "$ELF" 2>&1)
  printf '%s\n' "$AO" | grep -Eq '^\[marker window_cycles\] [0-9]+  \(vsim mcycle=' \
    || fail "marker: missing window_cycles line: $AO"
  printf '%s\n' "$AO" | grep -Eq '^PASS: --mode hybrid --trigger marker ' \
    || fail "marker: missing PASS line: $AO"
  check_parity marker "$GO" "$(printf '%s\n' "$AO" | cyc)"

  # marker on a C fixture -- the stack/heap + main()'s frame must survive the
  # handoff through the shared mmap (asm fixtures are self-contained; this is
  # the "+ C fixtures" half of the done-when).
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim.py run --mode marker "$CELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" "$CELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  check_parity marker-c "$GO" "$AO"

  # pc -- symbol start (_start) + 0x end (the exit marker)
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim.py run --mode pc \
        --pc-start _start --pc-end 0x10000c "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENG" \
        --pc-start _start --pc-end 0x10000c "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  check_parity pc "$GO" "$AO"

  # icount -- defaults (qemu 10000 / vsim 5000); andes keeps --shared-mem-* but
  # the cycle number is unchanged (this is the deliberate-divergence guard).
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim.py run --mode icount "$SPIN" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger icount --engine "$ENG" "$SPIN" 2>&1 | cyc)
  check_parity icount "$GO" "$AO"

# QEMU2) and print the one-line window-cycle figure for the marker | pc
# triggers. Three layers:
#
#   1. unit (fast, no spawn): the elf-syms boundary resolver, hybrid_trigger
#      (CLI -> Trigger, incl. pc symbol resolution), the trigger->argv mapping
#      (plan-test), and the new CLI flags (cli-test).
#   2. validation error paths via the real binary, all exiting BEFORE any spawn:
#      missing ELF, pc without boundaries, an undefined pc symbol, simpoint
#      (F11, not yet), and an unknown trigger.
#   3. real handoff + golden parity (guarded): run marker/pc/icount through both
#      ./hsim.py (the Python golden) and andes-sim and assert identical window
#      cycle numbers, plus the new output format. Skipped when the qemu/vsim/
#      plugin artifacts or the golden driver are not built.
#
# pc uses handoff_roundtrip.elf's own markers as the boundaries (_start =
# the enter marker 0x100000, 0x10000c = the exit marker), so pc reproduces marker's
# switch points exactly -- and exercises BOTH symbol and 0x resolution.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"  # asm fixture
CELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_matmul.elf"       # C fixture (needs shared mmap)
SPIN="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/icount_spin.elf"
ENG=vsim:ax45mpv_premium  # the engine ./hsim.py resolves by default

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit tests (the F9 pure cores)
for t in elf-syms hybrid plan cli; do
  "$ROOT/build/driver/andes-sim-$t-test" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || fail "unit test andes-sim-$t-test failed"
done
echo "[ok] unit: elf-syms, hybrid_trigger, trigger->argv (plan), CLI flags"

# 2. validation error paths -- real binary, but every case errors before a spawn
# (expect: assert rc + output regex; shared helper from tests/lib/log.sh)
expect 2 'ELF not found'        "$BIN" run --mode hybrid /no/such.elf
expect 2 'engine args go after' "$BIN" run --mode hybrid a.elf b.elf
expect 2 'requires --pc-start'  "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger pc "$ELF"
expect 2 'not defined' "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger pc \
  --pc-start nope_xyz --pc-end _start "$ELF"
expect 2 'F11'              "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger simpoint "$ELF"
expect 2 'unknown trigger'  "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger bogus "$ELF"
expect 2 'marker or pc'        "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger icount \
  --kanata /tmp/k "$SPIN"
expect 2 'requires --kanata' "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
  --objdump /tmp/o "$ELF"

SIM="$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"

  [ -s "$KAN" ] || fail "kanata: trace file empty/missing after marker run"
  echo "[ok] kanata: marker run wrote a non-empty ROI trace ($(wc -l <"$KAN") lines)"
  rm -f "$KAN"

  echo "[skip] real handoff parity: need built qemu+vsim+plugin and ./hsim"
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# run --cosim contract (cosim_roi F4): opt-in checkpoint co-simulation.
#   1. hybrid marker --cosim --cosim-interval 500 -> >=1 checkpoint,

#   2. hybrid pc --cosim                          -> same through cosim_pc
#   3. default (no --cosim)                       -> no cosim output
#   4. usage errors: model, trigger, interval, --verify exclusivity
#   5. dev-only help surface
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_v_matmul}"
hybrid_resolve_paths
ENGINE="${ENGINE:-vsim:ax45mpv_premium}"

# 1. marker mode with a sub-ROI interval -> real checkpoints.
OUT=$("$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" \
      --cosim --cosim-interval 500 "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "marker --cosim rc=$RC: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q '\[cosim\] PASS' || fail "marker: no [cosim] PASS: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -Eq '\[cosim\] PASS: [1-9][0-9]* checkpoint' \
  || fail "marker: expected at least one checkpoint: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'window_cycles' \
  && fail "marker: window_cycles printed under --cosim (the checkpoints pollute it; mutually exclusive): $OUT"

# 2. pc mode (boundaries = the fixture's own marker PCs, like docs 4.2).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-surface contract: the andes-sim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
# user-facing commands (run, list, doctor) and never the third-party simulator
# name "verilator". Developer commands (build, test, state-diff) appear only under
# ANDES_SIM_DEV=1; the unfinished ROADMAP commands (profile, cluster, archive,
# replay, estimate) appear in no help at all. The cycle-accurate engine is
# presented as "vsim" everywhere -- proven end to end with a fake engine that
# self-describes as "verilator" and must come back out as vsim:.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }

# 1. release --help: run + list + doctor, the dev hint, and no "verilator".
H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
has '^  run '    "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'run'"
has '^  list '   "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'list'"
has '^  doctor ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'doctor'"
for c in build test state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
done
no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'ANDES_SIM_DEV' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing developer-commands hint"
ok "release --help: run/list/doctor, dev hint, no verilator"

# 2. ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 --help: adds build/test/state-diff; doctor still shows
# (now release-tier, always listed); the hidden five stay hidden.
D=$(ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
for c in run list doctor build test state-diff; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing '$c'"
done
for c in profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" && fail "dev --help: leaked hidden command '$c'"
done
no_word "$D" || fail "dev --help: leaked 'verilator'"
ok "dev --help: adds build/test/state-diff, doctor still shown, hidden cmds hidden, no verilator"

# 3. run --help: the --engine example reads vsim:, never verilator:; the
# --trigger menu offers only implemented triggers (simpoint is unfinished).
RH=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
has 'vsim:' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing vsim: example"
no_word "$RH" || fail "run --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'simpoint' "$RH" && fail "run --help: leaked unfinished trigger 'simpoint':"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mem-size' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --mem-size:"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mmap-size' "$RH" && fail "run --help: retired --mmap-size alias should stay hidden:"$'\n'"$RH"
# Interactive-debug + oracle knobs are user-facing: documented in the release help.
has '^  --verify '   "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --verify:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb '      "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb-port ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb-port:"$'\n'"$RH"
ok "run --help: vsim: example, no verilator/simpoint, --mem-size/--verify/--gdb documented"

# 4. list models: composition cells read vsim (never verilator), and NOTES show
# user-facing model traits only -- no implementation detail, no unfinished trigger.
LM=$("$BIN" list models 2>&1)
has 'vsim' "$LM" || fail "list models: missing vsim"
no_word "$LM" || fail "list models: leaked 'verilator'"
for d in 'transparent passthrough' 'pure from reset' 'simpoint'; do
  has "$d" "$LM" && fail "list models: leaked implementation detail/unfinished trigger '$d':"$'\n'"$LM"
done
ok "list models: vsim, no verilator, no implementation detail, no simpoint"

# 5. list engines end to end: a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator"
# must surface as vsim: (the single normalization point), proving --engine /
# errors / list all speak the product name with no real sim_* needed.
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat >"$TMP/sim_fake" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"verilator:fakecfg","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc","icount"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
EOF
chmod +x "$TMP/sim_fake"
LE=$(ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" list engines 2>&1)
has 'vsim:fakecfg' "$LE" || fail "list engines: fake not renamed to vsim:fakecfg:"$'\n'"$LE"
no_word "$LE" || fail "list engines: leaked 'verilator':"$'\n'"$LE"
# Triggers are a hybrid-MODEL option, not an engine attribute: `list engines`
# carries no TRIGGERS column (and so never leaks the unfinished simpoint trigger
# that the built-in qemu row used to advertise).
has 'TRIGGERS' "$LE" && fail "list engines: TRIGGERS is a hybrid-model option, not an engine column:"$'\n'"$LE"
has 'simpoint'  "$LE" && fail "list engines: leaked unfinished trigger 'simpoint':"$'\n'"$LE"
ok "list engines: a verilator-self-describing engine is shown as vsim:, no TRIGGERS column"

# 6. `list fixtures` is a developer target (internal test ELFs, not user
# workloads): release hides it; ANDES_SIM_DEV reveals it.
printf '%s\n' "$H" | grep -qw fixtures && fail "release --help: leaked 'fixtures' target"
LH=$("$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$LH" | grep -qw fixtures && fail "release list --help: leaked 'fixtures':"$'\n'"$LH"
has 'models' "$LH" || fail "release list --help: missing 'models' target:"$'\n'"$LH"
expect 2 "unknown target 'fixtures'" "$BIN" list fixtures
DLH=$(ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$DLH" | grep -qw fixtures || fail "dev list --help: missing 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$DLH"
ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list fixtures >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "dev: list fixtures should succeed"
ok "list: fixtures is dev-only (release hides it; ANDES_SIM_DEV reveals it)"

ok "release surface (hide verilator + release/dev command split)"

#   [hsim mmap] 2.0 GiB at /home/u/.cache/andes-sim (free: 2.1 TiB) (fallback: /dev/shm too small (1.2 GiB free))

If you pin `HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/tmp` and `/tmp` is mounted as tmpfs (Arch

########## USER_GUIDE.md 485,495 ##########
session:
  mem_size: 134217728            # 128 MB shared mmap
  mmap_path: null                # null -> mktemp in /dev/shm
  elf: tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf

steps:
  - model: qemu
    trigger: { kind: marker }       # marker trigger; can also be { kind: pc, enter: 0x... } or { kind: icount, n: 5000 }
    on_exit: { archive_as: "snap/0" }
```

########## USER_GUIDE.md 520,527 ##########

Marker/PC delimit ONE kernel you choose; icount/SimPoint sample the whole
program by instruction count (SimPoint is icount repeated, weight-combined).
How each is driven: marker/pc/icount go through `./andes-sim run --mode
hybrid --trigger marker|pc|icount`; SimPoint still goes through the Python
reference (`./hsim.py run --mode simpoint`, also exposed as
`./hsim.py estimate`). The cycle figure is always
the vsim `mcycle` delta; SimPoint extrapolates many deltas
########## USER_GUIDE.md 705,725 ##########

For workloads you cannot edit. Both legs switch on a retired-insn count -
a **single boundary** on each side: QEMU fast-forwards `--qemu-icount` insns,
vsim measures `--vsim-icount` insns and drains. The cycle figure (window
cycles = vsim `mcycle` - QEMU `mcycle`) is the raw vsim-side
delta. Pair it with `--vsim-warmup-icount K` (see "Warmup window" below)
to exclude the first K cold-cache insns from the reported figure.

```sh
./andes-sim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf --mode hybrid --trigger icount --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
  --qemu-icount 2000 --vsim-icount 1000
```

Override the targets directly on the command line (defaults: 10000 / 5000):

```sh
./andes-sim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf --mode hybrid --trigger icount --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
  --qemu-icount 20000 --vsim-icount 8000
```

Use the markerless GEMM (`rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf`) - the twin of the marked
########## USER_GUIDE.md 985,997 ##########
snapshot lands on exactly the K-th retire, in icount mode it can be off
by a handful of insns, so treat the split as approximate there.

```sh
./andes-sim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf \
  --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --vsim-warmup-icount 1000

./andes-sim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
  --mode hybrid --trigger icount --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --qemu-icount 2000 --vsim-icount 5000 \
  --vsim-warmup-icount 1000     # require K < --vsim-icount
```

The snapshot - the (`mcycle`, `minstret`) pair at the K-th commit - is
########## USER_GUIDE.md 1043,1052 ##########
to view the pipeline.

Constraints:

- `--kanata` is only valid with `--mode hybrid --trigger marker` or `--mode hybrid --trigger pc`. icount and simpoint modes have no single ROI-exit PC and are rejected with rc=2.
- marker mode requires exactly one `slti x0,x0,0x5A1` (exit marker) in the
  ELF. If the binary has more than one, vsim errors out with
  `multiple ... markers in ELF -- use \`--mode hybrid --trigger pc\` with explicit \`--pc-end\``.
  Switch to pc mode and pick the desired exit explicitly.
- `--objdump` requires `--kanata`.

### 4.3 icount mode - a sampled window (no markers)

For workloads you cannot edit. Both legs switch on a retired-insn count -
a **single boundary** on each side: QEMU fast-forwards `--qemu-icount` insns,
vsim measures `--vsim-icount` insns and drains. The cycle figure (window
cycles = vsim `mcycle` - QEMU `mcycle`) is the raw vsim-side
delta. Pair it with `--vsim-warmup-icount K` (see "Warmup window" below)
to exclude the first K cold-cache insns from the reported figure.

  --qemu-icount 2000 --vsim-icount 1000
```

Override the targets directly on the command line (defaults: 10000 / 5000):

  --qemu-icount 20000 --vsim-icount 8000
```

Use the markerless GEMM (`rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf`) - the twin of the marked

the markers compiled out: the plugin's marker matcher stays live, so a

reached.

**Privilege (L6)**: the handoff carries the real privilege level. The plugin drains the gdbstub `priv` register, `ResumeDriver` read-modify-writes `dcsr.prv` before `dret` (and verifies the write took -- an M-mode-only RTL like the default `ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`, WARL-pins the field, and the resume aborts with a pick-an-S/U-capable-engine error), and `StateDrain` reads `dcsr.prv` back at the exit halt. For S/U handoffs the producer's PMP block (64 `pmpaddr` + the 8 even `pmpcfg`) is also mirrored into the hart, because with PMP implemented and no matching entry every S/U access faults; M-mode handoffs keep PMP pass-through-only (L2). The `rt_priv_smode`/`rt_priv_umode` fixtures run on the S/U-capable `ax66_makatau` engine paired with QEMU `-cpu andes-ax66` (see `scripts/run_e2e.sh`); the ROI itself must still be trap-free, single-privilege, and paging-off (S-mode CSRs are not transported).

### Trigger Modes

The repo ships 4 switching modes, split by what they profile.

Kernel modes (measure one region you choose):
- **marker mode** (default): Pattern-matches `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (entry) / `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (exit) at retire time. The markers are RISC-V HINTs (rd=x0 discards the result), i.e. architectural NOPs -- a marker binary also runs standalone on every engine and on silicon. Users get them from `<andes_sim/ROI.h>` (`andes_sim_ROI_begin()/end()`).
- **PC mode**: explicit boundary PCs passed as `--pc-start S --pc-end E` (symbol name or `0x` address) resolved at startup; marker insns are bypassed. Both args are required.

Whole-program modes (sample by instruction count):
- **icount mode**: single boundary on each leg - plugin `icount=N` fast-forwards QEMU1, vsim `--hybrid-icount M` measures the window and drains. No markers, no warmup; for marker-less workloads.
- **SimPoint-driven mode**: profile the run into slices (interval = insns per slice), cluster representative phases, measure each phase like icount, weight-combine into a whole-program cycle estimate. Drive via `./hsim.py run --mode simpoint` (or the equivalent `./hsim.py estimate`) -- Python golden only until the C++ port lands. The bbv-profile / archive / replay machinery are its stages, not separate modes.

`./andes-sim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker|pc|icount` is the unified orchestrator (`./hsim.py run --mode simpoint` for SimPoint); `tests/e2e.sh` drives marker/pc internally. Each yields a cycle figure: kernel/window cycles = the vsim `mcycle` delta (`hybrid_state_v1::mcycle`); SimPoint reports the weight-combined `estimated_cycles`.

## 4. icount mode - a sampled window (single boundary)

### What it does

Both legs switch on retired-instruction count alone. No markers, no PC symbol — suitable for marker-less workloads (an infinite spin loop, a benchmark you cannot edit, a raw blob).

- QEMU plugin: `icount=N` -> drain at the N-th retired insn (fast-forward).
- vsim: `--hybrid-icount M` -> drain M insns after resume (measure).

This is a **single boundary** on each side: fast-forward N in QEMU, measure
M in vsim. By default the cycle figure includes the cold-start cost at
vsim entry. Pair the run with `--vsim-warmup-icount K` (any K < M) to
crop the first K insns out of the reported window - see the "Warmup
window" section below for the mechanism.

### Inputs

- A marker-free ELF. The icount/simpoint examples use `rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf` - the markerless
  twin of the GEMM fixture, built `-DHYBRID_MARKERLESS` from the same
  `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.c`. The twin matters because the plugin's
  marker matcher stays live in icount mode: a workload containing
  `slti x0,x0,0x5A0` would drain AT that marker before reaching the icount
  target, so the count-driven modes need the markers compiled out. (The
  kernel modes use the marked build of the same source.)

2	// engines run and *how* they combine; the concrete engine(s) are resolved
3	// separately (built-in qemu, or a discovered verilator:<cfg>).
4	//

6	//   cycle     = one Verilator alone, pure from reset, transparent passthrough.
7	//   hybrid    = QEMU fast-forwards, Verilator measures the ROI (+ a trigger).
8	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_MODELS_HPP

17	  std::string_view engines;  // engine composition, for `list models`
18	  std::string_view notes;
19	};

22	    {"fast", "qemu", "functional"},
23	    {"cycle", "vsim:<cfg>", "cycle-accurate"},

26	     "pick --trigger marker|pc|icount"},

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-surface contract: the andes-sim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
# user-facing commands (run, list, doctor) and never the third-party simulator
# name "verilator". Developer commands (build, test, state-diff) appear only under
# ANDES_SIM_DEV=1; the unfinished ROADMAP commands (profile, cluster, archive,
# replay, estimate) appear in no help at all. The cycle-accurate engine is
# presented as "vsim" everywhere -- proven end to end with a fake engine that
# self-describes as "verilator" and must come back out as vsim:.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }

# 1. release --help: run + list + doctor, the dev hint, and no "verilator".
H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
has '^  run '    "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'run'"
has '^  list '   "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'list'"
has '^  doctor ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'doctor'"
for c in build test state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
done
no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'ANDES_SIM_DEV' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing developer-commands hint"
ok "release --help: run/list/doctor, dev hint, no verilator"

# 2. ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 --help: adds build/test/state-diff; doctor still shows
# (now release-tier, always listed); the hidden five stay hidden.
D=$(ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
for c in run list doctor build test state-diff; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing '$c'"
done
for c in profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" && fail "dev --help: leaked hidden command '$c'"
done
no_word "$D" || fail "dev --help: leaked 'verilator'"
ok "dev --help: adds build/test/state-diff, doctor still shown, hidden cmds hidden, no verilator"

# 3. run --help: the --engine example reads vsim:, never verilator:; the
# --trigger menu offers only the supported triggers (marker|pc -- icount was
# removed, simpoint is unfinished).
RH=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
has 'vsim:' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing vsim: example"
no_word "$RH" || fail "run --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'simpoint' "$RH" && fail "run --help: leaked unfinished trigger 'simpoint':"$'\n'"$RH"
has 'trigger.*icount' "$RH" && fail "run --help: --trigger should not list removed 'icount':"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mem-size' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --mem-size:"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mmap-size' "$RH" && fail "run --help: retired --mmap-size alias should stay hidden:"$'\n'"$RH"
# Interactive-debug + oracle knobs are user-facing: documented in the release help.
has '^  --verify '   "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --verify:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb '      "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb-port ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb-port:"$'\n'"$RH"
ok "run --help: vsim: example, no verilator/simpoint, --mem-size/--verify/--gdb documented"

# 4. list models: composition cells read vsim (never verilator), and NOTES show
# user-facing model traits only -- no implementation detail, no unfinished trigger.
LM=$("$BIN" list models 2>&1)
has 'vsim' "$LM" || fail "list models: missing vsim"
no_word "$LM" || fail "list models: leaked 'verilator'"
for d in 'transparent passthrough' 'pure from reset' 'simpoint'; do
  has "$d" "$LM" && fail "list models: leaked implementation detail/unfinished trigger '$d':"$'\n'"$LM"
done
ok "list models: vsim, no verilator, no implementation detail, no simpoint"

# 5. list engines end to end: a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator"
# must surface as vsim: (the single normalization point), proving --engine /
# errors / list all speak the product name with no real sim_* needed.
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat >"$TMP/sim_fake" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"verilator:fakecfg","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc","icount"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
EOF
chmod +x "$TMP/sim_fake"
LE=$(ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" list engines 2>&1)
has 'vsim:fakecfg' "$LE" || fail "list engines: fake not renamed to vsim:fakecfg:"$'\n'"$LE"
no_word "$LE" || fail "list engines: leaked 'verilator':"$'\n'"$LE"
# Triggers are a hybrid-MODEL option, not an engine attribute: `list engines`
# carries no TRIGGERS column (and so never leaks the unfinished simpoint trigger
# that the built-in qemu row used to advertise).
has 'TRIGGERS' "$LE" && fail "list engines: TRIGGERS is a hybrid-model option, not an engine column:"$'\n'"$LE"
has 'simpoint'  "$LE" && fail "list engines: leaked unfinished trigger 'simpoint':"$'\n'"$LE"
ok "list engines: a verilator-self-describing engine is shown as vsim:, no TRIGGERS column"

# 6. `list fixtures` is a developer target (internal test ELFs, not user
# workloads): release hides it; ANDES_SIM_DEV reveals it.
printf '%s\n' "$H" | grep -qw fixtures && fail "release --help: leaked 'fixtures' target"
LH=$("$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$LH" | grep -qw fixtures && fail "release list --help: leaked 'fixtures':"$'\n'"$LH"
has 'models' "$LH" || fail "release list --help: missing 'models' target:"$'\n'"$LH"
expect 2 "unknown target 'fixtures'" "$BIN" list fixtures
DLH=$(ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$DLH" | grep -qw fixtures || fail "dev list --help: missing 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$DLH"
ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list fixtures >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "dev: list fixtures should succeed"
ok "list: fixtures is dev-only (release hides it; ANDES_SIM_DEV reveals it)"

ok "release surface (hide verilator + release/dev command split)"
