1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Release-surface contract: the andesim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
3	# user-facing commands (run, list, doctor) and never the third-party simulator
4	# name "verilator". Developer commands (build, test, state-diff) appear only under
5	# ANDESIM_DEV=1; the unfinished ROADMAP commands (profile, cluster, archive,
6	# replay, estimate) appear in no help at all. The cycle-accurate engine is
7	# presented as "vsim" everywhere -- proven end to end with a fake engine that
8	# self-describes as "verilator" and must come back out as vsim:.
9	set -uo pipefail
10	
11	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
12	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
13	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
14	
15	BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
16	
17	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
18	
19	# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
20	has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
21	no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }
22	
23	# 1. release --help: run + list + doctor, the dev hint, and no "verilator".
24	H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
25	has '^  run '    "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'run'"
26	has '^  list '   "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'list'"
27	has '^  doctor ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'doctor'"
28	for c in build test state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
29	  has "^  $c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
30	done
31	no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
32	has 'ANDESIM_DEV' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing developer-commands hint"
33	ok "release --help: run/list/doctor, dev hint, no verilator"
34	
35	# 2. ANDESIM_DEV=1 --help: adds build/test/state-diff; doctor still shows
36	# (now release-tier, always listed); the hidden five stay hidden.
37	D=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
38	for c in run list doctor build test state-diff; do
39	  has "^  $c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing '$c'"
40	done
41	for c in profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
42	  has "^  $c " "$D" && fail "dev --help: leaked hidden command '$c'"
43	done
44	no_word "$D" || fail "dev --help: leaked 'verilator'"
45	ok "dev --help: adds build/test/state-diff, doctor still shown, hidden cmds hidden, no verilator"
46	
47	# 3. run --help: the --engine example reads vsim:, never verilator:; the
48	# --trigger menu offers only the supported triggers (marker|pc -- icount was
49	# removed, simpoint is unfinished).
50	RH=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
51	has 'vsim:' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing vsim: example"
52	no_word "$RH" || fail "run --help: leaked 'verilator'"
53	has 'simpoint' "$RH" && fail "run --help: leaked unfinished trigger 'simpoint':"$'\n'"$RH"
54	has 'trigger.*icount' "$RH" && fail "run --help: --trigger should not list removed 'icount':"$'\n'"$RH"
55	has ' --mem-size' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --mem-size:"$'\n'"$RH"
56	has ' --mmap-size' "$RH" && fail "run --help: retired --mmap-size alias should stay hidden:"$'\n'"$RH"
57	# Interactive-debug + oracle knobs are user-facing: documented in the release help.
58	has '^  --verify '   "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --verify:"$'\n'"$RH"
59	has '^  --gdb '      "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb:"$'\n'"$RH"
60	has '^  --gdb-port ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb-port:"$'\n'"$RH"
61	ok "run --help: vsim: example, no verilator/simpoint, --mem-size/--verify/--gdb documented"
62	
63	# 4. list models: composition cells read vsim (never verilator), and NOTES show
64	# user-facing model traits only -- no implementation detail, no unfinished trigger.
65	LM=$("$BIN" list models 2>&1)
66	has 'vsim' "$LM" || fail "list models: missing vsim"
67	no_word "$LM" || fail "list models: leaked 'verilator'"
68	for d in 'transparent passthrough' 'pure from reset' 'simpoint' 'icount'; do
69	  has "$d" "$LM" && fail "list models: leaked implementation detail/removed-or-unfinished trigger '$d':"$'\n'"$LM"
70	done
71	ok "list models: vsim, no verilator, no implementation detail, no simpoint/icount"
72	
73	# 5. list engines end to end: a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator"
74	# must surface as vsim: (the single normalization point), proving --engine /
75	# errors / list all speak the product name with no real sim_* needed.
76	TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
77	cat >"$TMP/sim_fake" <<'EOF'
78	#!/bin/sh
79	[ "$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"verilator:fakecfg","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc","icount"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
80	EOF
81	chmod +x "$TMP/sim_fake"
82	LE=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" list engines 2>&1)
83	has 'vsim:fakecfg' "$LE" || fail "list engines: fake not renamed to vsim:fakecfg:"$'\n'"$LE"
84	no_word "$LE" || fail "list engines: leaked 'verilator':"$'\n'"$LE"
85	# Triggers are a hybrid-MODEL option, not an engine attribute: `list engines`
86	# carries no TRIGGERS column (and so never leaks the unfinished simpoint trigger
87	# that the built-in qemu row used to advertise).
88	has 'TRIGGERS' "$LE" && fail "list engines: TRIGGERS is a hybrid-model option, not an engine column:"$'\n'"$LE"
89	has 'simpoint'  "$LE" && fail "list engines: leaked unfinished trigger 'simpoint':"$'\n'"$LE"
90	ok "list engines: a verilator-self-describing engine is shown as vsim:, no TRIGGERS column"
91	
92	# 6. `list fixtures` is a developer target (internal test ELFs, not user
93	# workloads): release hides it; ANDESIM_DEV reveals it.
94	printf '%s\n' "$H" | grep -qw fixtures && fail "release --help: leaked 'fixtures' target"
95	LH=$("$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
96	printf '%s\n' "$LH" | grep -qw fixtures && fail "release list --help: leaked 'fixtures':"$'\n'"$LH"
97	has 'models' "$LH" || fail "release list --help: missing 'models' target:"$'\n'"$LH"
98	expect 2 "unknown target 'fixtures'" "$BIN" list fixtures
99	DLH=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
100	printf '%s\n' "$DLH" | grep -qw fixtures || fail "dev list --help: missing 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$DLH"
101	ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list fixtures >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "dev: list fixtures should succeed"
102	ok "list: fixtures is dev-only (release hides it; ANDESIM_DEV reveals it)"
103	
104	ok "release surface (hide verilator + release/dev command split)"

1	# Switching-Mode Tutorial and Exercises
2	
3	Status: draft for review
4	Audience: engineer running the hybrid co-simulator for the first time
5	Scope: the 4 switching modes the repo ships, with copy-paste commands,
6	the cycle figure each one yields, and one exercise per mode.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## 0. What "switching mode" means
11	
12	The hybrid simulator runs a program across two phases:
13	
14	```
15	   QEMU1  --(state file + shared mmap)-->  vsim
16	   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate)
17	```
18	
19	A "switching mode" is the RULE that decides WHEN QEMU1 drains its
20	architectural state and hands the region of interest to vsim. vsim runs
21	that region cycle-accurately, then drains the final state. You pick
22	the rule with plugin args and vsim CLI flags; the fixture binary does not
23	have to change between modes.
24	
25	> **Two ways to invoke, one canonical.** `./andesim run` is the driver -
26	> the supported way to run a workload, and what the examples below lead
27	> with. `tests/e2e.sh` is the regression harness that wraps the same legs
28	> behind `FIXTURE=... TRIGGER_MODE=... bash tests/e2e.sh`; it adds test-only
29	> assertions (`CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC`, `EXPECT_RC`, ...) and is shown only
30	> where those diagnostics are the point. When in doubt, use `./andesim run`.
31	
32	The repo ships **4 modes**, split by WHAT you profile.
33	
34	### Quick map
35	
36	| # | Mode | Profiles | Switch boundary | Cycle figure it yields |
37	|---|------|----------|-----------------|------------------------|
38	| 1 | marker | a kernel | `slti x0,x0,0x5A0` (enter) / `slti x0,x0,0x5A1` (exit) | kernel cycles |
39	| 2 | PC | a kernel | a PC / symbol address (no source edit) | kernel cycles |
40	| 3 | icount | a sampled window | N retired insns (single boundary) | window cycles |
41	| 4 | SimPoint | the whole program | clustering picks representative slices | whole-program estimate |
42	
43	- **Kernel modes (marker, PC)** measure ONE region you choose.
44	- **Whole-program modes (icount, SimPoint)** sample by instruction count.
45	  icount measures one window you place by hand; SimPoint measures several
46	  representative windows that clustering picks for you, then weight-combines
47	  them into a whole-program estimate. **SimPoint is just icount repeated.**
48	
49	(Migration: the old M1-M8 list collapses to these 4. Old M4-M7 are now
50	SimPoint stages; old M8 - the QEMU2 semihosting exit - was removed with
51	the QEMU2 phase, so every run now ends at the vsim drain.)
52	
53	### Where the cycle figure comes from
54	
55	Every mode reads the same counter: `mcycle`, a little-endian `uint64` at
56	byte offset **624** in the state file (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`). vsim
57	restores `mcycle` from QEMU1's drained value, then the RTL counts real
58	clock cycles, so the measured cycles are always a subtraction:
59	
60	```
61	cycles = mcycle(vsim drain) - mcycle(QEMU1 drain)
62	```
63	
64	The QEMU baseline cancels; only vsim's cycle-accurate delta survives. That
65	is why QEMU being functional-only (not cycle-accurate) does not taint the
66	number. marker/pc/icount report this delta directly (kernel / window cycles);
67	SimPoint extrapolates many such deltas into a whole-program estimate
68	(Section 5).
69	
70	---
71	
72	## 1. One-time prerequisites
73	
74	Build everything once. Each command is idempotent.
75	
76	```sh
77	cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim
78	source ./setup.sh         # qemu + vsim + plugin + simpoint
79	```
80	
81	You should now have:
82	
83	| Artifact                                | Purpose                           |
84	|-----------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
85	| `build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64`        | QEMU binary (phase 1)             |
86	| `verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium`   | vsim binary (phase 2)             |
87	| `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so`      | TCG plugin (state drainer)        |
88	| `tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint`           | SimPoint clustering tool (mode 4) |
89	| `tests/fixtures/*.elf`                  | Test fixtures (e.g. rt_c_v_matmul) |
90	
91	Common env vars (auto-detected by `./andesim` and the e2e harness;
92	override only if you keep these elsewhere):
93	
94	```sh
95	export VSIM_QEMU=/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64
96	export VSIM_PLUGIN=/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
97	export VSIM_BIN=/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium
98	```
99	
100	---
101	
102	## 2. marker mode - the default (profiles a kernel)
103	
104	### What it does
105	
106	QEMU1's plugin pattern-matches the encoding `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` at retire
107	time. On hit it drains state to `outfile` and exits 200. vsim does the
108	same on `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1`. The markers are RISC-V HINT NOPs (rd=x0), safe on every
109	core, so the fixture binary embeds these two `slti` instructions at the
110	kernel boundaries. vsim's drain at the `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` marker is the
111	natural tail of the run.
112	
113	### Inputs
114	
115	- Fixture ELF with `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` and `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` in its source.
116	  Every C-level fixture (rt_c_v_matmul, rt_c_v_regs, rt_c_matmul, etc.) has these.
117	
118	### Cycle figure
119	
120	Kernel cycles = the vsim `mcycle` delta over the region between the two
121	markers. Run with `CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1` and the harness prints
122	`mcycle` at both ends:
123	
124	```sh
125	FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TRIGGER_MODE=marker CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1 TIMEOUT=120 \
126	  bash tests/e2e.sh
127	```
128	
129	Look for the two lines `qemu1: mcycle=...` and `vsim: mcycle=...`; the
130	kernel cycle count is `vsim - qemu1` (the GEMM kernel is ~22808 cycles).
131	
132	### Run it
133	
134	```sh
135	cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim
136	./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium
137	```
138	
139	`./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker` orchestrates the QEMU1 → vsim handoff directly (driver/cmd_run.cpp). Before the final PASS line it prints the cycle figure:
140	
141	```
142	[marker window_cycles] 22808  (vsim mcycle=... - qemu mcycle=...)
143	PASS: --mode hybrid --trigger marker (rt_c_v_matmul)
144	```
145	
146	The plugin gets `outfile=<state.bin>` and nothing else - that is the marker
147	default. vsim is launched without `--hybrid-exit-pc` and without
148	`--hybrid-icount`, so its ELF pre-scanner watches for `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` PCs
149	at retire.
150	
151	### Exercise 1
152	
153	The `./andesim run` examples default to the GEMM, but the harness is
154	fixture-parameterized - switch from `rt_c_v_matmul` to `rt_c_matmul`
155	(a scalar matmul) to confirm:
156

file.content:
# Build the user-facing andesim runtime library into build/runtime/:
#
#   libandesim_runtime.a   trap.o handler.o vplat_syscalls.o
#   crt0.o                   startfile; kept OUTSIDE the archive because
#                            nothing references _start, so the linker
#                            would never extract it from a .a (same
#                            reason toolchains ship crt0.o next to libc.a)
#   andesim.ld             linker script (load base 0x00100000)
#   include/andesim/ROI.h  ROI markers (HINT NOPs; same dir rides -B)
#
# Users link with:
#   gcc ... -B <repo>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs hello.c
# or, without the gcc driver:
#   gcc ... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T andesim.ld crt0.o hello.c \
#       -L <repo>/build/runtime \
#       -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
#
# Toolchain location comes from config.env (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN), same as
# tests/fixtures/Makefile.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
AR := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ar

OUT ?= ../build/runtime

# rv64gc objects link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the RISC-V
# arch attributes), so one build serves both -march variants.
CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

LIB_OBJS := $(OUT)/trap.o $(OUT)/handler.o $(OUT)/vplat_syscalls.o

.PHONY: all clean

all: $(OUT)/libandesim_runtime.a $(OUT)/crt0.o $(OUT)/andesim.ld \
     $(OUT)/andesim.specs $(OUT)/include/andesim/ROI.h

$(OUT):
	mkdir -p $@

$(OUT)/%.o: %.S | $(OUT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(OUT)/%.o: %.c | $(OUT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(OUT)/trap.o: core_v5.h

$(OUT)/libandesim_runtime.a: $(LIB_OBJS)
	$(AR) rcs $@ $^

$(OUT)/andesim.ld: andesim.ld | $(OUT)
	cp $< $@

$(OUT)/andesim.specs: andesim.specs | $(OUT)
	cp $< $@

# gcc adds <-B prefix>/include to the include path, so the two-flag user
# command resolves #include <andesim/ROI.h> with no extra -I.
$(OUT)/include/andesim/ROI.h: ROI.h | $(OUT)
	mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	cp $< $@

clean:
	rm -rf $(OUT)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# andesim: repo-root entry for the C++ driver (build/andesim).
# Self-bootstraps on first use so a fresh clone can run ./andesim
# directly; the build is host-only (no Verilator/SystemC/QEMU needed).
#
# macOS is run-only: both legs must share one Linux kernel, so the wrapper
# re-execs inside the prebuilt runtime image (podman machine VM); the shared
# mmap then lives in the VM, never on a virtiofs mount. ANDESIM_OS is a
# test hook to force the branch from Linux.
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

if [ "${ANDESIM_OS:-$(uname -s)}" = "Darwin" ]; then
  exec bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_in_container.sh" "$@"
fi

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >&2
exec "$BIN" "$@"

## Code-quality review (altitude angle) -- uncommitted diff in `driver/ runtime/ tests/`

Verdict up front: the substantive (non-rename) changes are almost all at the right altitude. The icount removal was done cleanly at the user-facing layer while preserving the internal `icount` plan mechanism, and `doctor`'s tier move uses the existing mechanism with no special-case. Two findings worth surfacing: one concrete bug (help-column misalignment caused by the rename), and a clear recommendation on the now-dead defensive guards.

---

### Finding 1 -- `driver/main.cpp:104` -- `--mode` help line is misaligned by one column
- Summary: the renamed `--mode fast|cycle|hybrid` line's description starts at column 36; every other flag in the same block (including the newly added `--gdb`/`--gdb-port`) starts at column 37.
- Why the depth is wrong: this is the rename leaking into output the task said should stay clean. `--model` was one char longer than `--mode`; when the author shortened the flag they did not add a compensating space, so the description column lost alignment for exactly that one row. The new `--gdb` lines were added at the correct col 37, which makes the stray row visibly crooked in `run --help`.
- Deeper fix: add one space after `--mode fast|cycle|hybrid` so its description aligns at col 37 with the rest. (Purely cosmetic, but it is user-facing release help and the diff itself introduced the inconsistency.)

### Finding 2 -- `driver/main.cpp:112-115` -- `--gdb`/`--gdb-port` placement is correct
- Summary: the two new help lines sit in the always-printed release `std::fputs` block (before the `if (is_dev_mode())` dev block), matching `Cli::gdb` being a release-tier flag valid on fast/cycle.
- Assessment: right altitude. `--gdb` is a user-facing debugging entry (it has its own release-surface test assertions in `test_andes_sim_release_surface.sh:622-623`), so documenting it in the release block - not the dev block - is consistent with how `--verify` and `--mem-size` are documented, and inconsistent placement (dev block) would have under-advertised a shipped feature. No change needed.

### Finding 3 -- `driver/cmd_run.cpp:444-445` and `:448-449` -- the `--verify`/`--cosim` "supports --trigger marker|pc" guards are now dead AND untested
- Summary: after `hybrid_trigger()` returns with `err.empty()`, `trig.kind` is provably `"marker"` or `"pc"` (every other branch in `hybrid.cpp` sets `err` and returns empty kind; simpoint errors at `hybrid.cpp:32`). So both `trig.kind != "marker" && trig.kind != "pc"` conditions are always false.
- Why this depth is now wrong: these were meaningful guards when `icount` was a valid trigger that the cosim/verify legs could not arm on. With `icount` gone they guard nothing reachable, and - critically - the one test that exercised them (the `expect 2 'cosim supports --trigger marker\|pc'` case with `--trigger icount` in `test_andes_sim_cosim.sh`) was deleted in this same diff. `cmd_run.cpp` is compiled only into the `andesim` binary, not into any unit-test target, so there is now no automated coverage of these two error strings at all. A "defensive invariant" that is both unreachable and untested is dead weight: it cannot regress-test anything, and a future reader has to re-derive that it is unreachable.
- Recommendation (clear): remove both guards (lines 444-445 and 448-449, with their comments). The invariant they protect - "a hybrid trigger is always marker or pc" - belongs at its source, `hybrid_trigger()`, which already enforces it by construction and IS unit-tested (`hybrid_test.cpp` checks the simpoint/icount/bogus error paths directly). If you want the invariant stated for future readers, a one-line comment or an `assert(trig.kind == "marker" || trig.kind == "pc")` documents it without pretending to be a tested user-facing error path. Keeping the current `return fail(...)` form is the worse altitude: it dresses up a structurally-impossible state as a recoverable CLI error.

### Finding 4 -- `driver/hybrid.cpp:55-58` -- the kanata "marker or pc" guard is also CLI-unreachable, but this one should STAY
- Summary: the live caller (`cmd_run.cpp:460`) passes `trig.kind`, again provably marker|pc, so the kanata error branch cannot fire from the CLI either.
- Why this is a different case from Finding 3: `vsim_extra_args()` is a small pure function that IS compiled into `andesim-hybrid-test` and is directly unit-tested with a non-marker/pc kind (`hybrid_test.cpp` now calls `vsim_extra_args(..., "simpoint", err)` and asserts the error). So unlike the cmd_run guards, this guard's behavior remains exercised and locked. Keeping it is the right altitude: it makes `vsim_extra_args` a self-contained, total function whose contract holds for any `kind` a future trigger might introduce, and the cost is one tested branch rather than an unverified dead one.
- Recommendation: keep as-is. (This is the consistent answer to the task's "is keeping unreachable guards worse than removing them" question: the discriminator is testability + locality, not reachability. The hybrid.cpp guard passes both; the cmd_run guards fail both.)

### Finding 5 -- user-facing `--trigger marker|pc` vs internal `icount` plan kind -- layering is coherent
- Summary: `hybrid.cpp` (the CLI->Trigger mapping) no longer emits an `icount` kind, while `plan.hpp`/`run_plan.cpp` retain the `icount` plan mechanism for SimPoint.
- Assessment: right altitude, and the split is well-marked. The seam is clean: `hybrid_trigger()` is the single chokepoint that decides which trigger kinds are user-selectable, and it simply stopped producing `icount`. The plan layer never knew about CLI surface - it consumes a `Trigger` with params - so leaving its icount path intact for the SimPoint pipeline does not leak any icount concept back to the user. The comment added at `hybrid_test.cpp` (the "measurement mechanism survives in the plan layer ... no longer CLI-selectable" note) documents exactly this boundary. No confusion; this is the textbook way to retire a user-facing option without ripping out infrastructure a sibling feature still needs.

### Finding 6 -- `Cli::model` field kept while flag is `--mode`; `tests/andes_sim/` + `namespace andes_sim` kept -- one minor concern
- Summary: the parse table maps `{"--mode", &c.model}` (`cli.cpp:76`); the struct field stays `model` with comment `// --mode fast|cycle|hybrid`.
- Assessment: the kept `model` field is fine and intentional - the "model" concept (`list models`, `find_model`, `models.hpp`, the `unknown model '...'` errors) is a real domain noun distinct from the `--mode` selector flag, so a flag-name change need not rename the concept. There are zero remaining user-facing `--model` literals in non-test driver source (verified), so nothing leaks. The internal-only `andes_sim` namespace and `tests/andes_sim/` dir are likewise invisible to users.
- The one concern: there is now a permanent flag-name/field-name mismatch (`--mode` -> `Cli::model`) plus a directory/namespace (`andes_sim`) that no longer matches the product name (`andesim`). This is a small, deliberate, documented inconsistency, not a defect - but it is exactly the kind of thing the next contributor will "helpfully" try to finish renaming. Recommendation: add a one-line note at the `Cli::model` declaration (e.g. `// field intentionally 'model': the --mode flag selects a *model*; concept name kept`) so the half-rename reads as a decision, not an oversight. No code change otherwise.

---

Out-of-scope note (not one of the 5 questions, flagging once): `cmd_run.cpp:run_cycle_gdb` also changed substantively beyond the rename - it drops vsim's `-S` and now execs ICEman with `-I virtual_dmi.cfg`. That cfg and the `interface/` dir it implies are present but untracked (`git status` shows `?? interface/`, `?? virtual_dmi.cfg`). If the `--gdb` cycle path is meant to work for other users, those need to be committed or generated; that is a provisioning concern separate from the rename review.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# run --verify contract (verify_oracle F4): opt-in oracle cross-check.
#   1. hybrid marker --verify  -> oracle leg + "[verify] PASS", rc 0
#   2. hybrid pc --verify      -> same through the exit_pc oracle path
#   3. default (no --verify)   -> no verify leg, no verify output
#   4. --verify with fast/cycle -> usage error (rc 2)
#   5. --verify with icount     -> usage error (rc 2)
#   6. run --help documents --verify
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/roi.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_hello}"
hybrid_resolve_paths
ENGINE="${ENGINE:-vsim:ax45mpv_premium}"

# 1. marker mode.
OUT=$("$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --verify \
      "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "marker --verify rc=$RC: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q '\[verify\] PASS' || fail "marker: no [verify] PASS: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q '\[state-diff\] PASS' || fail "marker: no state-diff detail: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'window_cycles' || fail "marker: cycle figure missing: $OUT"
ok "hybrid marker --verify: oracle cross-check PASS"

# 2. pc mode (boundaries = the fixture's own marker PCs, like docs 4.2).
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")") \
  || fail "no ROI markers in $VSIM_ELF"
OUT=$("$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENGINE" \
      --pc-start "0x${MARKERS%% *}" --pc-end "0x${MARKERS##* }" --verify \
      "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "pc --verify rc=$RC: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q '\[verify\] PASS' || fail "pc: no [verify] PASS: $OUT"
ok "hybrid pc --verify: oracle cross-check PASS"

# 3. default off: no oracle leg, no verify output.
OUT=$("$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" \
      "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "default hybrid rc=$RC: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -qi 'verify' && fail "default run leaked verify output: $OUT"
ok "default: verification stays off"

# 4 + 5. usage errors.
expect 2 'verify requires --mode hybrid' \
  "$BIN" run --mode fast --verify "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'verify requires --mode hybrid' \
  "$BIN" run --mode cycle --verify "$VSIM_ELF"
ok "--verify usage errors (fast/cycle)"

# 6. run --help documents the flag.
expect 0 ' --verify ' "$BIN" run --help
ok "run --help documents --verify"

ok "run --verify oracle cross-check"

skills.name: simplify
skills.content:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

77	  step "building test ELFs in $TEST_DIR"

79	fi

82	# e2e.sh harness (shared /dev/shm mmap). The TRIGGER_MODE env is
83	# injected per iteration based on $MODE. Negative drivers live in
84	# NEG_TESTS and run once regardless of mode.
85	RT_TESTS=(
86	  "handoff_roundtrip|FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip"
87	  "rt_pc_jump|FIXTURE=rt_pc_jump"
88	  "rt_sign_bits|FIXTURE=rt_sign_bits"
89	  "rt_abi_aliases|FIXTURE=rt_abi_aliases"
90	  "rt_long_roi|FIXTURE=rt_long_roi"
91	  "rt_all_gprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_gprs"
92	  "rt_mem_loadstore|FIXTURE=rt_mem_loadstore"
93	  "rt_unaligned_lh|FIXTURE=rt_unaligned_lh"
94	  "rt_csr_survival|FIXTURE=rt_csr_survival"
95	  "rt_shared_mem|FIXTURE=rt_shared_mem"
96	  "rt_c_hello|FIXTURE=rt_c_hello"
97	  "rt_c_printf|FIXTURE=rt_c_printf"
98	  "rt_c_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
99	  "rt_c_fcsr|FIXTURE=rt_c_fcsr"
100	  "rt_c_v_regs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs"
101	  "rt_c_v_csrs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_csrs"
102	  "rt_c_v_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
103	  "rt_c_v_fill|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_fill"
104	  "rt_c_static_buf|FIXTURE=rt_c_static_buf"
105	)
106	
107	NEG_TESTS=(
108	  "rt_corrupt_state|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh"
109	)
110	
111	# Heavyweight round-trip fixtures, run SEQUENTIALLY after the parallel
112	# pool drains. The L6 privilege fixtures need an S/U-capable engine pair
113	# (the default ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only,
114	# NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1), and the only built RV64 one is
115	# ax66_makatau -- whose Verilator binary runs 32 threads. Two of those in
116	# the parallel pool saturate the box and time out BOTH themselves and the
117	# lighter default-engine tests, so they get the machine to themselves.
118	# Same entry format as RT_TESTS; both trigger modes still apply.
119	SERIAL_RT_TESTS=(
120	  "rt_priv_smode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_smode CHECK_PRIV=1 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_DIR/build/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
121	  "rt_priv_umode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_umode CHECK_PRIV=0 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_DIR/build/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
122	)
123	
124	MODE="${MODE:-both}"
125	case "$MODE" in
126	  marker|pc|both) ;;
127	  *) fail "MODE must be one of marker|pc|both (got: $MODE)"; exit 1 ;;
128	esac
129	
130	default_jobs() {
131	  local n=1 shm_free shm_cap
132	  n=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
133	  if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
134	    shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
135	    if [[ "$shm_free" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$shm_free" -gt 0 ]]; then
136	      shm_cap=$((shm_free / 256))
137	      (( shm_cap < n && shm_cap >= 1 )) && n=$shm_cap
138	    fi
139	  fi
140	  (( n < 1 )) && n=1
141	  printf '%d\n' "$n"
142	}
143	JOBS="${JOBS:-$(default_jobs)}"
144	[[ "$JOBS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$JOBS" -ge 1 ]] \
145	  || { fail "JOBS must be a positive integer (got: $JOBS)"; exit 1; }
146	
147	FILTER="${FILTER:-}"
148	
149	LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-$(mktemp -d -t e2e-XXXXXX)}"
150	mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
151	RESULTS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/results.tsv"
152	LOCK_FILE="$LOG_DIR/lock"
153	: > "$RESULTS_FILE"
154	: > "$LOCK_FILE"
155	
156	# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
157	# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
158	# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
159	# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
160	# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
161	# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
162	# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
163	run_one() {
164	  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
165	  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
166	  local start end elapsed status rc
167	  start=$(date +%s)
168	  set +e
169	  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
170	  rc=$?
171	  set -e
172	  end=$(date +%s)
173	  elapsed=$((end - start))
174	  case $rc in
175	    0)  status=PASS ;;
176	    77) status=SKIP ;;
177	    *)  status=FAIL ;;
178	  esac
179	  (
180	    flock 9
181	    case "$status" in
182	      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
183	      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
184	      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
185	    esac
186	    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
187	      "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
188	  ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
189	}
190	
191	# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
192	# matters: marker-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
193	# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
194	declare -a WORKPLAN=()
195	for tm in marker pc; do
196	  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
197	  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
198	    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
199	    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
200	    # B3: anchor the regex so FILTER=rt_csr does not silently also match
201	    # rt_csr_survival. Users who want a substring match pass '.*marker.*'.
202	    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
203	    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
204	    WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
205	  done
206	done
207	for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
208	  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
209	  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
210	  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
211	  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
212	done
213	
214	# Serial phase: same (mode, name, cmd) tuples, executed one at a time
215	# after the parallel pool drains (see SERIAL_RT_TESTS above for why).
216	declare -a SERIAL_PLAN=()
217	for tm in marker pc; do
218	  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
219	  for entry in "${SERIAL_RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
220	    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
221	    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
222	    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
223	    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
224	    SERIAL_PLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
225	  done
226	done
227	
228	TOTAL=$(( ${#WORKPLAN[@]} + ${#SERIAL_PLAN[@]} ))
229	step "logs: $LOG_DIR  jobs: $JOBS  mode: $MODE  tests: $TOTAL"
230	
231	# FIFO-based bounded job pool. Each child reads one token from $SEM_FIFO
232	# before starting and writes one back on exit; only $JOBS tokens exist,
233	# so at most $JOBS children run concurrently. Opening the fifo in
234	# read-write mode (<>) means writes never block the parent. The fifo
235	# inode is unlinked immediately after fd 8 is bound -- the kernel keeps
236	# the pipe alive as long as fd 8 is open.
237	SEM_FIFO="$LOG_DIR/sem.fifo"

239	exec 8<>"$SEM_FIFO"
240	rm -f "$SEM_FIFO"
241	for ((sem_i=0; sem_i<JOBS; sem_i++)); do
242	  printf '.\n' >&8
243	done
244	
245	i=0
246	for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
247	  i=$((i+1))
248	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
249	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
250	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
251	  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"

254	    run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"

256	  ) &
257	done
258	wait
259	exec 8>&-
260	
261	# Serial phase: each heavyweight test gets the machine to itself.
262	for w in "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
263	  i=$((i+1))
264	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
265	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
266	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
267	  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
268	  run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
269	done
270	
271	declare -A MODE_PASS=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
272	declare -A MODE_FAIL=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
273	declare -A MODE_SKIP=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)

278	    SKIP) MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]=$((MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
279	    FAIL) MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]=$((MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]+1));
280	          FAILED_NAMES+=("${r_name}[${r_mode}]") ;;
281	  esac
282	done < "$RESULTS_FILE"

284	# Stream failed-test logs in workplan order so the user sees a
285	# deterministic post-run failure dump.
286	for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}" "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
287	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
288	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
289	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
290	  w_status=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$w_mode" -v n="$w_name" \
291	                 '$1==m&&$2==n{print $3; exit}' "$RESULTS_FILE")
292	  if [[ "$w_status" == "FAIL" ]]; then
293	    echo
294	    echo "=== FAIL log: ${w_name}[${w_mode}] ==="
295	    cat "$LOG_DIR/$w_mode--$w_name.log"
296	  fi
297	done
298	
299	echo
300	marker_p=${MODE_PASS[marker]} marker_f=${MODE_FAIL[marker]} marker_s=${MODE_SKIP[marker]}
301	pc_p=${MODE_PASS[pc]}   pc_f=${MODE_FAIL[pc]}   pc_s=${MODE_SKIP[pc]}
302	neg_p=${MODE_PASS[neg]} neg_f=${MODE_FAIL[neg]} neg_s=${MODE_SKIP[neg]}
303	total_pass=$((marker_p + pc_p + neg_p))
304	total_fail=$((marker_f + pc_f + neg_f))
305	total_skip=$((marker_s + pc_s + neg_s))

308	  fail "failures: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
309	  exit 1
310	fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the hybrid e2e tests directly, bypassing the VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID
# CTest gate. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts in this
# workspace.
#
# Env overrides:
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64)
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: first sim_* under verilator/build/)
#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
#   MODE         marker | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
#                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own
#                scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)

set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
VSIM_DIR="$ROOT/verilator"
HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"

VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
  # Default to the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine (the same one ./andesim
  # pins). The fixtures are single-hart programs: on a multicore build like
  # sim_ax45mpv_mp2 -- which sorts FIRST under verilator/build/ -- the
  # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and
  # stops the sim before hart 0 drains, failing every C fixture. Fall back
  # to the first sim_* only when the canonical engine is not built.
  VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_DIR/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
  if [[ ! -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]]; then
    VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_DIR"/build/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
  fi
fi

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

require() {
  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
    fail "$1 not found: $2"
    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
    exit 1
  fi
}
require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"

export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN

REQUIRED_ELFS=(
  handoff_roundtrip rt_pc_jump rt_sign_bits rt_abi_aliases rt_long_roi
  rt_all_gprs rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh rt_csr_survival rt_shared_mem
  rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode
  rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_fcsr rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs
  rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
  # CSR-less spin loop; used by `./andesim run --mode icount` and the BBV-emit
  # / SimPoint stages.
  icount_spin
)
need_build=0
for f in "${REQUIRED_ELFS[@]}"; do
  [[ -e "$TEST_DIR/$f.elf" ]] || need_build=1
done
if (( need_build )); then
  step "building test ELFs in $TEST_DIR"
  make -C "$TEST_DIR" -j
fi

# Round-trip fixtures: name|fixture-env-prefix. All run on the unified
# e2e.sh harness (shared /dev/shm mmap). The TRIGGER_MODE env is
# injected per iteration based on $MODE. Negative drivers live in
# NEG_TESTS and run once regardless of mode.
RT_TESTS=(
  "handoff_roundtrip|FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip"
  "rt_pc_jump|FIXTURE=rt_pc_jump"
  "rt_sign_bits|FIXTURE=rt_sign_bits"
  "rt_abi_aliases|FIXTURE=rt_abi_aliases"
  "rt_long_roi|FIXTURE=rt_long_roi"
  "rt_all_gprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_gprs"
  "rt_mem_loadstore|FIXTURE=rt_mem_loadstore"
  "rt_unaligned_lh|FIXTURE=rt_unaligned_lh"
  "rt_csr_survival|FIXTURE=rt_csr_survival"
  "rt_shared_mem|FIXTURE=rt_shared_mem"
  "rt_c_hello|FIXTURE=rt_c_hello"
  "rt_c_printf|FIXTURE=rt_c_printf"
  "rt_c_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_fcsr|FIXTURE=rt_c_fcsr"
  "rt_c_v_regs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs"
  "rt_c_v_csrs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_csrs"
  "rt_c_v_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_v_fill|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_fill"
  "rt_c_static_buf|FIXTURE=rt_c_static_buf"
)

NEG_TESTS=(
  "rt_corrupt_state|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh"
)

# Heavyweight round-trip fixtures, run SEQUENTIALLY after the parallel
# pool drains. The L6 privilege fixtures need an S/U-capable engine pair
# (the default ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only,
# NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1), and the only built RV64 one is
# ax66_makatau -- whose Verilator binary runs 32 threads. Two of those in
# the parallel pool saturate the box and time out BOTH themselves and the
# lighter default-engine tests, so they get the machine to themselves.
# Same entry format as RT_TESTS; both trigger modes still apply.
SERIAL_RT_TESTS=(
  "rt_priv_smode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_smode CHECK_PRIV=1 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_DIR/build/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
  "rt_priv_umode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_umode CHECK_PRIV=0 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_DIR/build/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
)

MODE="${MODE:-both}"
case "$MODE" in
  marker|pc|both) ;;
  *) fail "MODE must be one of marker|pc|both (got: $MODE)"; exit 1 ;;
esac

default_jobs() {
  local n=1 shm_free shm_cap
  n=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
  if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
    shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
    if [[ "$shm_free" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$shm_free" -gt 0 ]]; then
      shm_cap=$((shm_free / 256))
      (( shm_cap < n && shm_cap >= 1 )) && n=$shm_cap
    fi
  fi
  (( n < 1 )) && n=1
  printf '%d\n' "$n"
}
JOBS="${JOBS:-$(default_jobs)}"
[[ "$JOBS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$JOBS" -ge 1 ]] \
  || { fail "JOBS must be a positive integer (got: $JOBS)"; exit 1; }

FILTER="${FILTER:-}"

LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-$(mktemp -d -t e2e-XXXXXX)}"
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
RESULTS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/results.tsv"
LOCK_FILE="$LOG_DIR/lock"
: > "$RESULTS_FILE"
: > "$LOCK_FILE"

# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
run_one() {
  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
  local start end elapsed status rc
  start=$(date +%s)
  set +e
  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
  rc=$?
  set -e
  end=$(date +%s)
  elapsed=$((end - start))
  case $rc in
    0)  status=PASS ;;
    77) status=SKIP ;;
    *)  status=FAIL ;;
  esac
  (
    flock 9
    case "$status" in
      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
    esac
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
      "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
  ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
}

# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
# matters: marker-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
declare -a WORKPLAN=()
for tm in marker pc; do
  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
    # B3: anchor the regex so FILTER=rt_csr does not silently also match
    # rt_csr_survival. Users who want a substring match pass '.*marker.*'.
    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
    WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
  done
done
for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
done

# Serial phase: same (mode, name, cmd) tuples, executed one at a time
# after the parallel pool drains (see SERIAL_RT_TESTS above for why).
declare -a SERIAL_PLAN=()
for tm in marker pc; do
  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
  for entry in "${SERIAL_RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
    SERIAL_PLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
  done
done

TOTAL=$(( ${#WORKPLAN[@]} + ${#SERIAL_PLAN[@]} ))
step "logs: $LOG_DIR  jobs: $JOBS  mode: $MODE  tests: $TOTAL"

# FIFO-based bounded job pool. Each child reads one token from $SEM_FIFO
# before starting and writes one back on exit; only $JOBS tokens exist,
# so at most $JOBS children run concurrently. Opening the fifo in
# read-write mode (<>) means writes never block the parent. The fifo
# inode is unlinked immediately after fd 8 is bound -- the kernel keeps
# the pipe alive as long as fd 8 is open.
SEM_FIFO="$LOG_DIR/sem.fifo"
mkfifo "$SEM_FIFO"
exec 8<>"$SEM_FIFO"
rm -f "$SEM_FIFO"
for ((sem_i=0; sem_i<JOBS; sem_i++)); do
  printf '.\n' >&8
done

i=0
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
  i=$((i+1))
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
  read -r -u 8 _tok
  (
    run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
    printf '.\n' >&8
  ) &
done
wait
exec 8>&-

# Serial phase: each heavyweight test gets the machine to itself.
for w in "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
  i=$((i+1))
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
  run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
done

declare -A MODE_PASS=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -A MODE_FAIL=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -A MODE_SKIP=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
while IFS=$'\t' read -r r_mode r_name r_status _r_rc _r_el; do
  case "$r_status" in
    PASS) MODE_PASS[$r_mode]=$((MODE_PASS[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    SKIP) MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]=$((MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    FAIL) MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]=$((MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]+1));
          FAILED_NAMES+=("${r_name}[${r_mode}]") ;;
  esac
done < "$RESULTS_FILE"

# Stream failed-test logs in workplan order so the user sees a
# deterministic post-run failure dump.
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}" "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_status=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$w_mode" -v n="$w_name" \
                 '$1==m&&$2==n{print $3; exit}' "$RESULTS_FILE")
  if [[ "$w_status" == "FAIL" ]]; then
    echo
    echo "=== FAIL log: ${w_name}[${w_mode}] ==="
    cat "$LOG_DIR/$w_mode--$w_name.log"
  fi
done

echo
marker_p=${MODE_PASS[marker]} marker_f=${MODE_FAIL[marker]} marker_s=${MODE_SKIP[marker]}
pc_p=${MODE_PASS[pc]}   pc_f=${MODE_FAIL[pc]}   pc_s=${MODE_SKIP[pc]}
neg_p=${MODE_PASS[neg]} neg_f=${MODE_FAIL[neg]} neg_s=${MODE_SKIP[neg]}
total_pass=$((marker_p + pc_p + neg_p))
total_fail=$((marker_f + pc_f + neg_f))
total_skip=$((marker_s + pc_s + neg_s))
step "summary: marker ${marker_p}p/${marker_f}f/${marker_s}s  pc ${pc_p}p/${pc_f}f/${pc_s}s  neg ${neg_p}p/${neg_f}f/${neg_s}s  total ${total_pass} passed, ${total_fail} failed, ${total_skip} skipped"
if (( total_fail > 0 )); then
  fail "failures: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
  exit 1
fi

project(andes_sim CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release)

=== setup.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Driver: build qemu + vsim + plugin + simpoint, then add build dirs to PATH.
# Source this script to affect your current shell's PATH:
#   source ./setup.sh                       # build all
#   source ./setup.sh clean [target]        # clean qemu|vsim|plugin|simpoint|all (default: all)

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${(%):-%x}"
elif [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
else
  _SETUP_SRC="$0"
fi

# Wrap the body in a function so strict-mode options stay local and don't
# leak into the caller's interactive shell (which would break zsh prompts
# under nounset).
_hybrid_setup_main() {
  if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    emulate -L sh
    setopt err_exit no_unset pipe_fail
  else
    local -
    set -euo pipefail
  fi

  local ROOT QEMU_BIN_DIR VSIM_BIN_DIR PLUGIN_DIR QEMU_SRC PLUGIN_SO SIMPOINT_SRC SIMPOINT_BIN_PATH CONFIG_FILE CONFIG_TEMPLATE
  ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$_SETUP_SRC")" && pwd)"
  QEMU_BIN_DIR="$ROOT/build/qemu"
  VSIM_BIN_DIR="$ROOT/verilator/build"
  PLUGIN_DIR="$ROOT/qemu_plugin"
  QEMU_SRC="$ROOT/QEMU"
  PLUGIN_SO="$PLUGIN_DIR/libhybrid_handoff.so"
  SIMPOINT_SRC="$ROOT/tools/simpoint"
  SIMPOINT_BIN_PATH="$SIMPOINT_SRC/bin/simpoint"
  CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
  CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"

  step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m \033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
  ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
  err()  { printf '\033[1;31m[err]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

  clean_qemu()   { step "cleaning qemu build ($QEMU_BIN_DIR)";   rm -rf "$QEMU_BIN_DIR"; ok "qemu cleaned"; }
  clean_vsim()   { step "cleaning vsim build ($VSIM_BIN_DIR)";   rm -rf "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; ok "vsim cleaned"; }
  clean_plugin() {
    step "cleaning plugin build ($PLUGIN_DIR)"
    if [ -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
      make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR" clean
    else
      rm -f "$PLUGIN_SO" "$PLUGIN_DIR"/*.o
    fi
    ok "plugin cleaned"
  }
  clean_simpoint() {
    step "cleaning simpoint build ($SIMPOINT_SRC)"
    if [ -f "$SIMPOINT_SRC/Makefile" ]; then
      make -C "$SIMPOINT_SRC" clean
    else
      rm -f "$SIMPOINT_BIN_PATH"
    fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# andesim: repo-root entry for the C++ driver (build/andesim).
# Self-bootstraps on first use so a fresh clone can run ./andesim
# directly; the build is host-only (no Verilator/SystemC/QEMU needed).
#
# macOS is run-only: both legs must share one Linux kernel, so the wrapper
# re-execs inside the prebuilt runtime image (podman machine VM); the shared
# mmap then lives in the VM, never on a virtiofs mount. ANDESIM_OS is a
# test hook to force the branch from Linux.
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

if [ "${ANDESIM_OS:-$(uname -s)}" = "Darwin" ]; then
  exec bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_in_container.sh" "$@"
fi

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >&2
exec "$BIN" "$@"

=== release_surface test: what does it assert about dev cmds? ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-surface contract: the andesim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
# user-facing commands (run, list, doctor) and never the third-party simulator
# name "verilator". Developer commands (build, test, state-diff) appear only under
# ANDESIM_DEV=1; the unfinished ROADMAP commands (profile, cluster, archive,
# replay, estimate) appear in no help at all. The cycle-accurate engine is
# presented as "vsim" everywhere -- proven end to end with a fake engine that
# self-describes as "verilator" and must come back out as vsim:.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }

# 1. release --help: run + list + doctor, the dev hint, and no "verilator".
H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
has '^  run '    "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'run'"
has '^  list '   "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'list'"
has '^  doctor ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'doctor'"
for c in build test state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
done
no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'ANDESIM_DEV' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing developer-commands hint"
ok "release --help: run/list/doctor, dev hint, no verilator"

# 2. ANDESIM_DEV=1 --help: adds build/test/state-diff; doctor still shows
# (now release-tier, always listed); the hidden five stay hidden.
D=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
for c in run list doctor build test state-diff; do

# verify_oracle F3 (opt-in, default off): differential check against a
# pure-QEMU oracle. The same ELF re-runs on QEMU alone -- clean memory, so
# NO shared mmap (reusing it would leak the hybrid run's post-ROI bytes
# into the oracle's boot) -- with the plugin draining at the ROI exit
# boundary. state-diff then compares everything vsim freshly drains.
if [ "${VERIFY:-0}" = "1" ]; then
  ANDESIM_BIN="${ANDESIM_BIN:-$TOP_ROOT/build/andesim}"
  if [ ! -x "$ANDESIM_BIN" ]; then

  ORACLE_TRIG="exit_marker=1"
  [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ] && ORACLE_TRIG="exit_pc=0x$EXIT_PC"
  # Sample at vsim's ACTUAL halt point: the DMI halt lands a variable 0-3
  # insns past the trigger, so the oracle must drain at the pc vsim's state
  # file reports (offset 16, locked by state_abi_check.h), not at trigger+1.
  VSIM_PC=$(printf '0x%x' "$(read_u64_le 16 "$STATE_VSIM")")
  ORACLE_TRIG="$ORACLE_TRIG,drain_pc=$VSIM_PC"

  set +e
  "$VSIM_QEMU" \
    -machine andes_ae350 \
    -cpu "$QEMU_CPU" \
    -nographic \
    -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
    -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
    -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_ORACLE,$ORACLE_TRIG" \
    </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
  ORACLE_RC=$?
  set -e
  if [ "$ORACLE_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: oracle QEMU expected exit 200 on drain, got $ORACLE_RC"
    exit 1
  fi

  set +e
  DIFF_OUT=$("$ANDESIM_BIN" state-diff "$STATE_ORACLE" "$STATE_VSIM" 2>&1)
  DIFF_RC=$?
  set -e
  printf '%s\n' "$DIFF_OUT"
  if [ "$DIFF_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim drain diverges from the QEMU oracle"
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "[$FIXTURE verify] PASS: vsim drain matches the QEMU oracle"
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)"

I now have the complete picture. Here's the architecture, derived from your three answers:

## Plan: strip developer commands from the `andesim` binary

**Binary surface (one coherent change to `main.cpp` + friends):** the product exposes only `run`/`list`/`doctor` (+ the hidden ROADMAP stubs). Remove:
- `build` → delete `cmd_build.cpp`, table entry, dispatch, CMake source.
- `test` → delete table entry (it has no handler today; it just hit the "not implemented" stub).
- `state-diff` → delete the `cmd_state_diff` wrapper + dispatch + table entry. **Keep** `diff_states()`/`print_diff_report()` (core used by `run --verify`/`--cosim`).
- Drop the now-empty "developer commands" section + the `ANDESIM_DEV` command-hint from `print_usage`. (`ANDESIM_DEV` still gates the `run --cosim` flags and `list fixtures` — those are flags/targets, not commands.)
- Repoint the user-facing "run `./andesim build`" hints in `engine_registry.hpp` + `cmd_doctor.cpp` to `scripts/build_all.sh`.

**Decouple `e2e.sh` from `andesim`:** remove the `VERIFY=1` block (its only `andesim` use — calls the deleted `state-diff`). Differential verify already lives in `andesim run --verify`, covered by `test_andes_sim_verify.sh`. No automated coverage lost.

**New scripts (thin wrappers, no duplicated build logic):**
- `scripts/build_all.sh` → `setup.sh` + `make -C tests/fixtures` (= old `build --what all`); optional target arg preserves the old `--what` set.
- `scripts/test_all.sh` → unit (`build/driver/andesim-*-test`) + contract (`tests/andes_sim/*.sh`) + e2e (`run_e2e.sh`).

**Tests:** rewrite `test_andes_sim_release_surface.sh`; delete `test_andes_sim_state_diff.sh` + `test_andes_sim_verify_e2e.sh` (subsumed); add `DRY_RUN` contract tests for both scripts. **Docs:** `USER_GUIDE.md` + `CLAUDE.md` repoint `./andesim build`/`test` → the scripts.

Starting TDD now — **F1 RED**: rewrite the release-surface contract to the new surface, then run it against the current (unchanged) binary to confirm it fails for the right reason.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-surface contract: the andesim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
# user-facing commands (run, list, doctor) and never the third-party simulator
# name "verilator". Developer commands (build, test, state-diff) appear only under
# ANDESIM_DEV=1; the unfinished ROADMAP commands (profile, cluster, archive,
# replay, estimate) appear in no help at all. The cycle-accurate engine is
# presented as "vsim" everywhere -- proven end to end with a fake engine that
# self-describes as "verilator" and must come back out as vsim:.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }

# 1. release --help: run + list + doctor, the dev hint, and no "verilator".
H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
has '^  run '    "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'run'"
has '^  list '   "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'list'"
has '^  doctor ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'doctor'"
for c in build test state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
done
no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'ANDESIM_DEV' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing developer-commands hint"
ok "release --help: run/list/doctor, dev hint, no verilator"

# 2. ANDESIM_DEV=1 --help: adds build/test/state-diff; doctor still shows
# (now release-tier, always listed); the hidden five stay hidden.
D=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
for c in run list doctor build test state-diff; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing '$c'"
done
for c in profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" && fail "dev --help: leaked hidden command '$c'"
done
no_word "$D" || fail "dev --help: leaked 'verilator'"
ok "dev --help: adds build/test/state-diff, doctor still shown, hidden cmds hidden, no verilator"

# 3. run --help: the --engine example reads vsim:, never verilator:; the
# --trigger menu offers only the supported triggers (marker|pc -- icount was
# removed, simpoint is unfinished).
RH=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
has 'vsim:' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing vsim: example"
no_word "$RH" || fail "run --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'simpoint' "$RH" && fail "run --help: leaked unfinished trigger 'simpoint':"$'\n'"$RH"
has 'trigger.*icount' "$RH" && fail "run --help: --trigger should not list removed 'icount':"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mem-size' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --mem-size:"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mmap-size' "$RH" && fail "run --help: retired --mmap-size alias should stay hidden:"$'\n'"$RH"
# Interactive-debug + oracle knobs are user-facing: documented in the release help.
has '^  --verify '   "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --verify:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb '      "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb-port ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb-port:"$'\n'"$RH"
ok "run --help: vsim: example, no verilator/simpoint, --mem-size/--verify/--gdb documented"

# 4. list models: composition cells read vsim (never verilator), and NOTES show
# user-facing model traits only -- no implementation detail, no unfinished trigger.
LM=$("$BIN" list models 2>&1)
has 'vsim' "$LM" || fail "list models: missing vsim"
no_word "$LM" || fail "list models: leaked 'verilator'"
for d in 'transparent passthrough' 'pure from reset' 'simpoint' 'icount'; do
  has "$d" "$LM" && fail "list models: leaked implementation detail/removed-or-unfinished trigger '$d':"$'\n'"$LM"
done
ok "list models: vsim, no verilator, no implementation detail, no simpoint/icount"

# 5. list engines end to end: a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator"
# must surface as vsim: (the single normalization point), proving --engine /
# errors / list all speak the product name with no real sim_* needed.
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat >"$TMP/sim_fake" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"verilator:fakecfg","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc","icount"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
EOF
chmod +x "$TMP/sim_fake"
LE=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" list engines 2>&1)
has 'vsim:fakecfg' "$LE" || fail "list engines: fake not renamed to vsim:fakecfg:"$'\n'"$LE"
no_word "$LE" || fail "list engines: leaked 'verilator':"$'\n'"$LE"
# Triggers are a hybrid-MODEL option, not an engine attribute: `list engines`
# carries no TRIGGERS column (and so never leaks the unfinished simpoint trigger
# that the built-in qemu row used to advertise).
has 'TRIGGERS' "$LE" && fail "list engines: TRIGGERS is a hybrid-model option, not an engine column:"$'\n'"$LE"
has 'simpoint'  "$LE" && fail "list engines: leaked unfinished trigger 'simpoint':"$'\n'"$LE"
ok "list engines: a verilator-self-describing engine is shown as vsim:, no TRIGGERS column"

# 6. `list fixtures` is a developer target (internal test ELFs, not user
# workloads): release hides it; ANDESIM_DEV reveals it.
printf '%s\n' "$H" | grep -qw fixtures && fail "release --help: leaked 'fixtures' target"
LH=$("$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$LH" | grep -qw fixtures && fail "release list --help: leaked 'fixtures':"$'\n'"$LH"
has 'models' "$LH" || fail "release list --help: missing 'models' target:"$'\n'"$LH"
expect 2 "unknown target 'fixtures'" "$BIN" list fixtures
DLH=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$DLH" | grep -qw fixtures || fail "dev list --help: missing 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$DLH"
ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list fixtures >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "dev: list fixtures should succeed"
ok "list: fixtures is dev-only (release hides it; ANDESIM_DEV reveals it)"

ok "release surface (hide verilator + release/dev command split)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-surface contract: the andesim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
# user-facing commands (run, list, doctor) and never the third-party simulator
# name "verilator". The former developer commands build/test/state-diff have
# moved OUT of the binary (build -> scripts/build_all.sh, test ->
# scripts/test_all.sh, state-diff -> the diff_states core behind `run --verify`):
# they are not listed in any help and are not dispatchable. The unfinished
# ROADMAP commands (profile, cluster, archive, replay, estimate) appear in no
# help at all. The cycle-accurate engine is presented as "vsim" everywhere --
# proven end to end with a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator" and
# must come back out as vsim:.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }

# 1. release --help: run + list + doctor, the dev hint, and no "verilator".
H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
has '^  run '    "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'run'"
has '^  list '   "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'list'"
has '^  doctor ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'doctor'"
for c in build test state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
done
no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'ANDESIM_DEV' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing developer-commands hint"
ok "release --help: run/list/doctor, dev hint, no verilator"

# 2. ANDESIM_DEV=1 --help: adds build/test/state-diff; doctor still shows
# (now release-tier, always listed); the hidden five stay hidden.
D=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
for c in run list doctor build test state-diff; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing '$c'"
done
for c in profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" && fail "dev --help: leaked hidden command '$c'"
done
no_word "$D" || fail "dev --help: leaked 'verilator'"
ok "dev --help: adds build/test/state-diff, doctor still shown, hidden cmds hidden, no verilator"

# 3. run --help: the --engine example reads vsim:, never verilator:; the
# --trigger menu offers only the supported triggers (marker|pc -- icount was
# removed, simpoint is unfinished).
RH=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
has 'vsim:' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing vsim: example"
no_word "$RH" || fail "run --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'simpoint' "$RH" && fail "run --help: leaked unfinished trigger 'simpoint':"$'\n'"$RH"
has 'trigger.*icount' "$RH" && fail "run --help: --trigger should not list removed 'icount':"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mem-size' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --mem-size:"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mmap-size' "$RH" && fail "run --help: retired --mmap-size alias should stay hidden:"$'\n'"$RH"
# Interactive-debug + oracle knobs are user-facing: documented in the release help.
has '^  --verify '   "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --verify:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb '      "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb-port ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb-port:"$'\n'"$RH"
ok "run --help: vsim: example, no verilator/simpoint, --mem-size/--verify/--gdb documented"

# 4. list models: composition cells read vsim (never verilator), and NOTES show
# user-facing model traits only -- no implementation detail, no unfinished trigger.
LM=$("$BIN" list models 2>&1)
has 'vsim' "$LM" || fail "list models: missing vsim"
no_word "$LM" || fail "list models: leaked 'verilator'"
for d in 'transparent passthrough' 'pure from reset' 'simpoint' 'icount'; do
  has "$d" "$LM" && fail "list models: leaked implementation detail/removed-or-unfinished trigger '$d':"$'\n'"$LM"
done
ok "list models: vsim, no verilator, no implementation detail, no simpoint/icount"

# 5. list engines end to end: a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator"
# must surface as vsim: (the single normalization point), proving --engine /
# errors / list all speak the product name with no real sim_* needed.
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat >"$TMP/sim_fake" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"verilator:fakecfg","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc","icount"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
EOF
chmod +x "$TMP/sim_fake"
LE=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" list engines 2>&1)
has 'vsim:fakecfg' "$LE" || fail "list engines: fake not renamed to vsim:fakecfg:"$'\n'"$LE"
no_word "$LE" || fail "list engines: leaked 'verilator':"$'\n'"$LE"
# Triggers are a hybrid-MODEL option, not an engine attribute: `list engines`
# carries no TRIGGERS column (and so never leaks the unfinished simpoint trigger
# that the built-in qemu row used to advertise).
has 'TRIGGERS' "$LE" && fail "list engines: TRIGGERS is a hybrid-model option, not an engine column:"$'\n'"$LE"
has 'simpoint'  "$LE" && fail "list engines: leaked unfinished trigger 'simpoint':"$'\n'"$LE"
ok "list engines: a verilator-self-describing engine is shown as vsim:, no TRIGGERS column"

# 6. `list fixtures` is a developer target (internal test ELFs, not user
# workloads): release hides it; ANDESIM_DEV reveals it.

expect 2 "unknown target 'fixtures'" "$BIN" list fixtures
DLH=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$DLH" | grep -qw fixtures || fail "dev list --help: missing 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$DLH"
ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list fixtures >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "dev: list fixtures should succeed"
ok "list: fixtures is dev-only (release hides it; ANDESIM_DEV reveals it)"

# andesim driver: a standalone C++20 executable.
#
# Intentionally minimal -- no Verilator, no SystemC, no QEMU, no fmt/spdlog.
# It depends only on the host C++ toolchain and the shared ABI header at
# include/hybrid/state_abi.h (consumed from F5 on for state-file reads).
#
# Build out-of-tree via scripts/build_driver.sh, which points
# CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY at the repo's build/ so the binary lands at
# build/andesim.
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(andes_sim CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release)
endif()

add_executable(andesim
  main.cpp
  cli.cpp
  cmd_list.cpp
  cmd_doctor.cpp
  cmd_build.cpp
  cmd_run.cpp
  hybrid.cpp
  elf_syms.cpp
  process.cpp
  shm.cpp
  argv.cpp
  run_plan.cpp
  run_passthrough.cpp
  engine_registry.cpp
  state_diff.cpp
  cosim_lockstep.cpp
)

# Shared ABI header lives at <repo>/include/hybrid/state_abi.h, two levels up.
target_include_directories(andesim PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_compile_options(andesim PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)

# Unit tests. Kept in the build tree (build/driver), not redirected to build/,
# so build/ holds only the shipped binary.
add_executable(andesim-cli-test cli_test.cpp cli.cpp)
add_executable(andesim-json-test json_test.cpp)
add_executable(andesim-infra-test infra_test.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp)
add_executable(andesim-plan-test plan_test.cpp argv.cpp run_plan.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp)

add_executable(andesim-plan-itest plan_itest.cpp argv.cpp run_plan.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp engine_registry.cpp)
# F7 transparent-passthrough argv assembly (pure; no spawn).
add_executable(andesim-run-test run_test.cpp run_passthrough.cpp argv.cpp process.cpp)

# cosim_redesign F6: the lock-step stream comparison core (pure; synthetic).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Differential parity harness: the closed-loop flywheel for the rewrite.
#
# Runs the same args through the Python golden (hsim) and the C++ driver
# (build/andesim), then diffs stdout+stderr and the exit code. As each
# later feature ports a subcommand, it adds its cases below; a green parity
# run is the evidence the C++ path matches the reference it replaces.
#
# F0 ships the harness skeleton with zero cases, so it exits 0 vacuously.
# Override the two binaries via the GOLDEN / NEW env vars if needed.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

GOLDEN="${GOLDEN:-$ROOT/hsim.py}"        # Python reference driver
NEW="${NEW:-$ROOT/build/andesim}"   # C++ driver under test

# Parity compares the full developer surface against the golden (which exposes
# everything), so run the C++ driver in dev mode -- e.g. so the dev-only
# `list fixtures` target resolves on both sides.
export ANDESIM_DEV=1

pass=0
fail=0

# compare <case-name> -- <args...>
# Invoke GOLDEN and NEW with identical args; require matching stdout+stderr
# and exit code. Records a pass/fail; never aborts so all cases report.
compare() {
  local name="$1"
  shift
  [ "${1:-}" = "--" ] && shift
  local g_out g_rc n_out n_rc
  g_out=$("$GOLDEN" "$@" 2>&1)
  g_rc=$?
  n_out=$("$NEW" "$@" 2>&1)
  n_rc=$?
  if [ "$g_rc" != "$n_rc" ] || [ "$g_out" != "$n_out" ]; then
    echo "[DIFF] $name (golden rc=$g_rc, new rc=$n_rc)"
    fail=$((fail + 1))
    return
  fi
  pass=$((pass + 1))
}

# compare_carried <case-name> -- <args...>
# Like compare, but the C++ driver appends sections the Python golden lacks
# (doctor's engines readout). Scope parity to the carried-over report by
# truncating NEW at (and including) the `Summary:` line before diffing.
compare_carried() {
  local name="$1"
  shift
  [ "${1:-}" = "--" ] && shift
  local g_out g_rc n_full n_rc n_out
  g_out=$("$GOLDEN" "$@" 2>&1)
  g_rc=$?
  n_full=$("$NEW" "$@" 2>&1)
  n_rc=$?
  n_out=$(printf '%s\n' "$n_full" | awk '{print} /^Summary:/{exit}')
  if [ "$g_rc" != "$n_rc" ] || [ "$g_out" != "$n_out" ]; then
    echo "[DIFF] $name (golden rc=$g_rc, new rc=$n_rc)"
    fail=$((fail + 1))
    return
  fi
  pass=$((pass + 1))
}

# --- parity cases (populated per feature) ---
compare "list fixtures" -- list fixtures      # F1
compare_carried "doctor" -- doctor            # F3
compare "build dry default" -- build --dry-run                  # F4
for w in all qemu vsim plugin simpoint fixtures; do
  compare "build dry $w" -- build --dry-run --what "$w"
done

echo "parity: $pass matched, $fail differed"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]
