#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-surface contract: the andesim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
# user-facing commands (run, list, doctor) and never the third-party simulator
# name "verilator". The former developer commands build/test/state-diff have
# moved OUT of the binary (build -> scripts/build_all.sh, test ->
# scripts/test_all.sh, state-diff -> the diff_states core behind `run --verify`):
# they are not listed in any help and are not dispatchable. The unfinished
# ROADMAP commands (profile, cluster, archive, replay, estimate) appear in no
# help at all. The cycle-accurate engine is presented as "vsim" everywhere --
# proven end to end with a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator" and
# must come back out as vsim:.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }

# 1. release --help: run + list + doctor only. No developer-commands section
# (build/test/state-diff moved to scripts/), and no "verilator".
H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
has '^  run '    "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'run'"
has '^  list '   "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'list'"
has '^  doctor ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'doctor'"
for c in build test state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
done
no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'developer command' "$H" && fail "release --help: developer commands moved to scripts/; drop the section:"$'\n'"$H"
ok "release --help: run/list/doctor only, no developer-commands section, no verilator"

# 2. The developer commands left the binary entirely: ANDESIM_DEV=1 --help adds
# NO commands (run/list/doctor only), and build/test/state-diff are no longer
# dispatchable (unknown command, rc 2).
D=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
for c in run list doctor; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing release command '$c'"
done
for c in build test state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" && fail "dev --help: leaked removed/hidden command '$c'"
done
no_word "$D" || fail "dev --help: leaked 'verilator'"
for c in build test state-diff; do
  expect 2 "unknown command '$c'" "$BIN" "$c"
done
ok "dev --help: no developer commands; build/test/state-diff gone (rc 2)"

# 3. run --help: the --engine example reads vsim:, never verilator:; the
# --trigger menu offers only the supported triggers (marker|pc -- icount was
# removed, simpoint is unfinished).
RH=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
has 'vsim:' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing vsim: example"
no_word "$RH" || fail "run --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'simpoint' "$RH" && fail "run --help: leaked unfinished trigger 'simpoint':"$'\n'"$RH"
has 'trigger.*icount' "$RH" && fail "run --help: --trigger should not list removed 'icount':"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mem-size' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --mem-size:"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mmap-size' "$RH" && fail "run --help: retired --mmap-size alias should stay hidden:"$'\n'"$RH"
# Interactive-debug + oracle knobs are user-facing: documented in the release help.
has '^  --verify '   "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --verify:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb '      "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb-port ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb-port:"$'\n'"$RH"
ok "run --help: vsim: example, no verilator/simpoint, --mem-size/--verify/--gdb documented"

# 4. list models: composition cells read vsim (never verilator), and NOTES show
# user-facing model traits only -- no implementation detail, no unfinished trigger.
LM=$("$BIN" list models 2>&1)
has 'vsim' "$LM" || fail "list models: missing vsim"
no_word "$LM" || fail "list models: leaked 'verilator'"
for d in 'transparent passthrough' 'pure from reset' 'simpoint' 'icount'; do
  has "$d" "$LM" && fail "list models: leaked implementation detail/removed-or-unfinished trigger '$d':"$'\n'"$LM"
done
ok "list models: vsim, no verilator, no implementation detail, no simpoint/icount"

# 5. list engines end to end: a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator"
# must surface as vsim: (the single normalization point), proving --engine /
# errors / list all speak the product name with no real sim_* needed.
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat >"$TMP/sim_fake" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"verilator:fakecfg","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc","icount"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
EOF
chmod +x "$TMP/sim_fake"
LE=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" list engines 2>&1)
has 'vsim:fakecfg' "$LE" || fail "list engines: fake not renamed to vsim:fakecfg:"$'\n'"$LE"
no_word "$LE" || fail "list engines: leaked 'verilator':"$'\n'"$LE"
# Triggers are a hybrid-MODEL option, not an engine attribute: `list engines`
# carries no TRIGGERS column (and so never leaks the unfinished simpoint trigger
# that the built-in qemu row used to advertise).
has 'TRIGGERS' "$LE" && fail "list engines: TRIGGERS is a hybrid-model option, not an engine column:"$'\n'"$LE"
has 'simpoint'  "$LE" && fail "list engines: leaked unfinished trigger 'simpoint':"$'\n'"$LE"
ok "list engines: a verilator-self-describing engine is shown as vsim:, no TRIGGERS column"

# 6. `list fixtures` is a developer target (internal test ELFs, not user
# workloads): release hides it; ANDESIM_DEV reveals it.
printf '%s\n' "$H" | grep -qw fixtures && fail "release --help: leaked 'fixtures' target"
LH=$("$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$LH" | grep -qw fixtures && fail "release list --help: leaked 'fixtures':"$'\n'"$LH"
has 'models' "$LH" || fail "release list --help: missing 'models' target:"$'\n'"$LH"
expect 2 "unknown target 'fixtures'" "$BIN" list fixtures
DLH=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$DLH" | grep -qw fixtures || fail "dev list --help: missing 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$DLH"
ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list fixtures >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "dev: list fixtures should succeed"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Differential parity harness: the closed-loop flywheel for the rewrite.
#
# Runs the same args through the Python golden (hsim) and the C++ driver
# (build/andesim), then diffs stdout+stderr and the exit code. As each
# later feature ports a subcommand, it adds its cases below; a green parity
# run is the evidence the C++ path matches the reference it replaces.
#
# F0 ships the harness skeleton with zero cases, so it exits 0 vacuously.
# Override the two binaries via the GOLDEN / NEW env vars if needed.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

GOLDEN="${GOLDEN:-$ROOT/hsim.py}"        # Python reference driver
NEW="${NEW:-$ROOT/build/andesim}"   # C++ driver under test

# Parity compares the full developer surface against the golden (which exposes
# everything), so run the C++ driver in dev mode -- e.g. so the dev-only
# `list fixtures` target resolves on both sides.
export ANDESIM_DEV=1

pass=0
fail=0

# compare <case-name> -- <args...>
# Invoke GOLDEN and NEW with identical args; require matching stdout+stderr
# and exit code. Records a pass/fail; never aborts so all cases report.
compare() {
  local name="$1"
  shift
  [ "${1:-}" = "--" ] && shift
  local g_out g_rc n_out n_rc
  g_out=$("$GOLDEN" "$@" 2>&1)
  g_rc=$?
  n_out=$("$NEW" "$@" 2>&1)
  n_rc=$?
  if [ "$g_rc" != "$n_rc" ] || [ "$g_out" != "$n_out" ]; then
    echo "[DIFF] $name (golden rc=$g_rc, new rc=$n_rc)"
    fail=$((fail + 1))
    return
  fi
  pass=$((pass + 1))
}

# compare_carried <case-name> -- <args...>
# Like compare, but the C++ driver appends sections the Python golden lacks
# (doctor's engines readout). Scope parity to the carried-over report by
# truncating NEW at (and including) the `Summary:` line before diffing.
compare_carried() {
  local name="$1"
  shift
  [ "${1:-}" = "--" ] && shift
  local g_out g_rc n_full n_rc n_out
  g_out=$("$GOLDEN" "$@" 2>&1)
  g_rc=$?
  n_full=$("$NEW" "$@" 2>&1)
  n_rc=$?
  n_out=$(printf '%s\n' "$n_full" | awk '{print} /^Summary:/{exit}')
  if [ "$g_rc" != "$n_rc" ] || [ "$g_out" != "$n_out" ]; then
    echo "[DIFF] $name (golden rc=$g_rc, new rc=$n_rc)"
    fail=$((fail + 1))
    return
  fi
  pass=$((pass + 1))
}

# --- parity cases (populated per feature) ---
compare "list fixtures" -- list fixtures      # F1
compare_carried "doctor" -- doctor            # F3
compare "build dry default" -- build --dry-run                  # F4
for w in all qemu vsim plugin simpoint fixtures; do
  compare "build dry $w" -- build --dry-run --what "$w"
done

echo "parity: $pass matched, $fail differed"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

# pure-QEMU oracle. The same ELF re-runs on QEMU alone -- clean memory, so
# NO shared mmap (reusing it would leak the hybrid run's post-ROI bytes
# into the oracle's boot) -- with the plugin draining at the ROI exit
# boundary. state-diff then compares everything vsim freshly drains.
if [ "${VERIFY:-0}" = "1" ]; then

  if [ ! -x "$ANDESIM_BIN" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: VERIFY=1 needs $ANDESIM_BIN (run scripts/build_driver.sh)"
    exit 1
  fi
  ORACLE_TRIG="exit_marker=1"
  [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ] && ORACLE_TRIG="exit_pc=0x$EXIT_PC"
  # Sample at vsim's ACTUAL halt point: the DMI halt lands a variable 0-3
  # insns past the trigger, so the oracle must drain at the pc vsim's state
  # file reports (offset 16, locked by state_abi_check.h), not at trigger+1.
  VSIM_PC=$(printf '0x%x' "$(read_u64_le 16 "$STATE_VSIM")")
  ORACLE_TRIG="$ORACLE_TRIG,drain_pc=$VSIM_PC"

  echo "[$FIXTURE verify mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] oracle: pure QEMU drains at ROI exit (pc=$VSIM_PC)"
  set +e
  "$VSIM_QEMU" \
    -machine andes_ae350 \
    -cpu "$QEMU_CPU" \
    -nographic \
    -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
    -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
    -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_ORACLE,$ORACLE_TRIG" \

    exit 1

  DIFF_RC=$?
  set -e
  printf '%s\n' "$DIFF_OUT"
  if [ "$DIFF_RC" -ne 0 ]; then

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# build_all.sh -- build the andesim artifacts. This is the entry point that
# replaced the former `andesim build` subcommand (which moved out of the driver
# binary). It only orchestrates the existing build scripts / Makefiles; the
# build logic itself lives in setup.sh, scripts/build_*.sh, and the Makefiles.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/build_all.sh [TARGET] [--dry-run]
#
# TARGET (default: all):
#   all       setup.sh (qemu + vsim + plugin + simpoint) then fixtures
#             (the fixtures Makefile also builds the runtime lib transitively)
#   qemu      build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64
#   vsim      verilator/build/sim_*
#   plugin    qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
#   simpoint  tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint
#   fixtures  tests/fixtures/*.elf (+ runtime lib)
#   runtime   build/runtime/ (libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o, andesim.ld, andesim.specs)
#
# --dry-run prints the underlying commands without running them.
#
# The andesim driver itself is NOT built here: ./andesim self-bootstraps via
# scripts/build_driver.sh on first use.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

TARGET=all
DRY_RUN=0
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    all|qemu|vsim|plugin|simpoint|fixtures|runtime) TARGET="$arg" ;;
    *)
      echo "build_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
      echo "usage: build_all.sh [all|qemu|vsim|plugin|simpoint|fixtures|runtime] [--dry-run]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# test_all.sh -- run the full andesim test surface. This is the entry point that
# replaced the former `andesim test` subcommand (which moved out of the binary).
#
# Phases (all run, in order, unless named explicitly):
#   unit      build/driver/andesim-*-test   the C++ driver unit tests
#   contract  tests/andes_sim/*.sh          driver feature + parity contracts
#   e2e       scripts/run_e2e.sh            hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]
#
# --dry-run prints the plan without executing (and without building). The
# contract and e2e phases need built artifacts -- run scripts/build_all.sh
# first. FILTER / MODE / JOBS pass through to scripts/run_e2e.sh unchanged.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

DRY_RUN=0
PHASES=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    unit|contract|e2e) PHASES+=("$arg") ;;
    *)
      echo "test_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
      echo "usage: test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done
[ "${#PHASES[@]}" -eq 0 ] && PHASES=(unit contract e2e)

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

pass=0
failed=0
declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()

# run_case NAME CMD...  -- execute one case, tally it, dump its log on failure.
run_case() {
  local name="$1"; shift
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "$name"; return; fi
  local log rc; log=$(mktemp)
  "$@" >"$log" 2>&1; rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
    ok "$name"; pass=$((pass + 1))
  else
    fail "$name (rc=$rc)"; failed=$((failed + 1)); FAILED_NAMES+=("$name")
    cat "$log"
  fi
  rm -f "$log"
}

run_unit() {
  step "[unit] C++ driver unit tests"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
    printf '  %s\n' "scripts/build_driver.sh" "build/driver/andesim-*-test (each)"
    return
  fi
  if ! bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null; then
    fail "[unit] build_driver.sh failed"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
  fi
  shopt -s nullglob
  local bins=("$ROOT"/build/driver/andesim-*-test)
  shopt -u nullglob
  if [ "${#bins[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
    fail "[unit] no unit-test binaries under build/driver"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
  fi
  local t
  for t in "${bins[@]}"; do run_case "[unit] $(basename "$t")" "$t"; done
}

run_contract() {
  step "[contract] driver feature + parity contracts"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
    printf '  %s\n' "tests/andes_sim/parity.sh" "tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh (each)"
    return
  fi
  local s
  for s in "$ROOT"/tests/andes_sim/parity.sh "$ROOT"/tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh; do
    [ -f "$s" ] || continue
    run_case "[contract] $(basename "$s")" bash "$s"
  done
}

run_e2e() {
  step "[e2e] hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "scripts/run_e2e.sh"; return; fi
  run_case "[e2e] run_e2e.sh" bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_e2e.sh"
}

for p in "${PHASES[@]}"; do
  case "$p" in
    unit)     run_unit ;;
    contract) run_contract ;;
    e2e)      run_e2e ;;
  esac
done

if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
  echo
  echo "(dry-run: nothing executed)"
  exit 0
fi

echo
step "summary: $pass passed, $failed failed"
if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
  fail "failed: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
  exit 1
fi

=== USER_GUIDE.md 35-72 ===

`./andesim` is the canonical end-user entry point (the C++ driver; it
self-builds on first use). It orchestrates QEMU and vsim directly: `build`
delegates to the repo's build scripts (`setup.sh`, `scripts/build_*.sh`),
while `run` drives the legs itself. Sections 1-7 document those underlying
scripts (`tests/e2e.sh`, `scripts/run_e2e.sh`) for when you need to bypass
the driver.

Four-command worked example - cold checkout to passing suite:

```sh
./andesim build                                       # qemu, vsim, plugin, simpoint, fixtures
./andesim list engines                                # discover the built engines
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
  tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf                         # one marker-mode handoff
JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh                          # full e2e suite (test subcommand not yet ported to the C++ driver)
```

Expected last line of `scripts/run_e2e.sh`:

```
summary: marker <N>p/0f/<S>s  pc <N>p/0f/<S>s  neg <N>p/0f/0s  total <N> passed, 0 failed, <S> skipped
```

Subcommand cheat sheet:

| Command                                                          | What it does                                                        |
|------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `./andesim list <models|engines>`                              | List the 3 models, or the discovered engines with their hardware params (XLEN/VLEN/DLEN/ELEN; `-` = not reported). |
| `./andesim build [--what TARGET] [--dry-run]`                  | Build artifacts; targets: `all`, `qemu`, `vsim`, `plugin`, `simpoint`, `fixtures`, `runtime`. |
| `./andesim doctor`                                             | Read-only environment health check: artifacts, submodules, toolchain, runtime, discovered engines, and `/dev/shm` mmap tiers (with WSL2 advice). |
| `./andesim run --mode fast|cycle|hybrid [--trigger marker|pc] [--engine ID] [--gdb [--gdb-port PORT]] <elf>` | Run one ELF on a model (hybrid = QEMU -> vsim handoff; --gdb pauses at startup for a debugger: fast opens QEMU's GDB stub on port 1234, cycle halts the hart and opens vsim's JTAG port (9104) then execs `$ICEMAN`, a GDB server (use a modern OpenOCD); --gdb not supported with hybrid). |
| `bash scripts/run_e2e.sh` (env: `FILTER`, `MODE`, `JOBS`)        | Run the e2e suite (the `test` subcommand is not yet ported to the C++ driver; see Section 6). |

<cell id="f52ecb9d"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># Co-simulation with andesim: catching where the RTL diverges

Co-simulation (**cosim**) runs the same program on a fast functional model
(QEMU) *and* the cycle-accurate RTL (vsim) and compares their architectural
state. QEMU is the **golden model**; vsim is the **device under test**. When
they disagree, the first mismatch points at the instruction the RTL got wrong.

There are **two ways to use it**, for two different situations:

| Usage | Command | When |
|-------|---------|------|
| **1. Lock-step DV** | `run --model cycle --cosim` | A small test program (e.g. from a constraint-based generator). Compare **every instruction** from reset. |
| **2. ROI narrowing** | `run --model hybrid --cosim [--cosim-refine]` | A long program. Fast-forward to a region of interest, then localize the bad instruction inside it. |

This notebook walks through both. It is a **developer** tool, so the flags
are hidden unless `ANDESIM_DEV=1` is set.</cell id="f52ecb9d">
<cell id="1ce59d77"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Setup

Point the shell at the repo's `build/` so `andesim` is on `PATH`. (Run
`./andesim build` once beforehand if `build/andesim` does not exist.)</cell id="1ce59d77">
<cell id="4ce3d48f">import os
from pathlib import Path
root = next(str(d) for d in (Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents)
            if (d / "build" / "andesim").exists())
os.chdir(root)
os.environ["PATH"] = f"{root}/build:" + os.environ["PATH"]
os.environ["ANDESIM_DEV"] = "1"   # show the cosim flags in --help (they work without it; this just un-hides them)
print("working dir:", root)</cell id="4ce3d48f">

working dir: /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim
<cell id="34d90c6d"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>The three models. `cosim` attaches to **cycle** (lock-step from reset) and
to **hybrid** (ROI window); `fast` is QEMU itself, so there is nothing to
cross-check.</cell id="34d90c6d">
<cell id="d4aedb2e">!andesim list models</cell id="d4aedb2e">

MODEL   ENGINES       NOTES
fast    qemu          functional
cycle   vsim:<cfg>    cycle-accurate
hybrid  qemu -> vsim  QEMU fast-forwards, vsim measures the ROI; pick --trigger marker|pc|icount
<cell id="7addf270"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>---
## Mode 1 -- Lock-step DV (`run --model cycle --cosim`)

Both engines boot the **same ELF from reset**. From an *arm pc* onward the
tool drains the full architectural state **before every instruction** on
each side and compares the two streams record-by-record. The first record
that differs is the exact instruction the RTL executed wrong.

Key properties:

- **No halt slack.** The RTL side single-steps over the Debug Module
  (`dcsr.step`), so each record boundary is an exact instruction boundary.
- **Aligned by attempt index**, not by a counter. Record *k* is the state
  before execution attempt *k+1* on both sides.
- **Traps are in scope.** An `ecall`/exception lands the next record at the
  handler entry on both sides; `mepc` and `mcause` are compared, so a
  mishandled trap diverges loudly.
- The QEMU oracle runs **first** (MHz-fast) and defines the record count
  *K*; the RTL is then bounded to *K* so a diverged hart cannot run away.</cell id="7addf270">
<cell id="d8d55d0a"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### The test program must establish its own state

Lock-step compares from the arm pc, so the program must have a **deterministic
architectural state by then**. This matters because QEMU and the RTL do not
agree on *reset* state: QEMU seeds the boot-argument registers (`a0`, `a1`,
...) while the RTL resets all GPRs to 0. A constraint-generated DV testbench
handles this the standard way -- it writes **every** register in a prologue,
then begins the region to compare.

The fixture `tests/fixtures/rt_trap_ecall.S` does exactly that: it `li`s all
of `x1..x31`, then exposes a `roi_start` label, then runs two trapping
`ecall`s. We arm at `roi_start` so the prologue runs on both engines but is
not recorded; record 0 is the ROI's first instruction with identical state
on both sides.</cell id="d8d55d0a">
<cell id="d34685f4">%%bash
# Build the self-initializing trap fixture (one-time).
. ./config.env 2>/dev/null
make -C tests/fixtures TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN" rt_trap_ecall.elf >/dev/null
echo "built tests/fixtures/rt_trap_ecall.elf"

# The ROI: arithmetic + two ecalls that trap to a handler and mret back.
"$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump" -d tests/fixtures/rt_trap_ecall.elf \
  | sed -n '/<roi_start>:/,/<hang>/p'</cell id="d34685f4">

built tests/fixtures/rt_trap_ecall.elf
00000000001000b6 <roi_start>:
  1000b6:	0505                	c.addi	a0,1
  1000b8:	00000073          	ecall
  1000bc:	0589                	c.addi	a1,2
  1000be:	00000073          	ecall
  1000c2:	00b50633          	add	a2,a0,a1
  1000c6:	6e09                	c.lui	t3,0x2
  1000c8:	c01e0e1b          	addiw	t3,t3,-1023
  1000cc:	0e4e                	c.slli	t3,0x13
  1000ce:	000e2023          	sw	zero,0(t3)
<cell id="38be2179"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### Run it

Arm at `roi_start` and bound the run to a handful of records (`--cosim-max-records 6`). Each RTL record is a DMI single-step + full drain — see the cost note below. Six records cross the first `ecall` and its handler.</cell id="38be2179">
<cell id="7cd30f7b">!andesim run --model cycle --cosim --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
    --pc-start roi_start --cosim-max-records 6 \
    tests/fixtures/rt_trap_ecall.elf</cell id="7cd30f7b">

[andesim] cosim lock-step: oracle (QEMU) boots from reset, arms at 0x1000b6
[andesim] cosim lock-step: oracle drained 6 record(s); DUT (vsim) bounded to the same

[cosim] PASS: 6 records match (lock-step, 1 attempt/record)
<cell id="cae1da68"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>`PASS` means the RTL matched QEMU on all six attempts, **including the trap**:
the record at the handler entry carried `mcause=11` (ecall-from-M) and the
right `mepc` on both engines. Drop `--cosim-max-records` to compare the whole
program (it runs until the program exits).</cell id="cae1da68">
<cell id="a292f1d5"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### Localizing a divergence

When the streams differ, the report names the **exact attempt** and both PCs.
To see the FAIL shape without a buggy RTL, run a *non*-DV program: `rt_c_hello`
is a normal C binary that reads the boot-argument registers QEMU seeds at
reset. The RTL reset those to 0, so the very first recorded instruction
already disagrees -- and the tool says so:</cell id="a292f1d5">

# Co-simulation with andesim: catching where the RTL diverges

Co-simulation (**cosim**) runs the same program on a fast functional model
(QEMU) *and* the cycle-accurate RTL (vsim) and compares their architectural
state. QEMU is the **golden model**; vsim is the **device under test**. When
they disagree, the first mismatch points at the instruction the RTL got wrong.

There are **two ways to use it**, for two different situations:

| Usage | Command | When |
|-------|---------|------|
| **1. Lock-step DV** | `run --model cycle --cosim` | A small test program (e.g. from a constraint-based generator). Compare **every instruction** from reset. |
| **2. ROI narrowing** | `run --model hybrid --cosim [--cosim-refine]` | A long program. Fast-forward to a region of interest, then localize the bad instruction inside it. |

This notebook walks through both. It is a **developer** tool, so the flags
are hidden unless `ANDESIM_DEV=1` is set.

## Setup

Point the shell at the repo's `build/` so `andesim` is on `PATH`. (Run
`./andesim build` once beforehand if `build/andesim` does not exist.)

import os
from pathlib import Path
root = next(str(d) for d in (Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents)
            if (d / "build" / "andesim").exists())
os.chdir(root)
os.environ["PATH"] = f"{root}/build:" + os.environ["PATH"]
os.environ["ANDESIM_DEV"] = "1"   # show the cosim flags in --help (they work without it; this just un-hides them)
print("working dir:", root)

to **hybrid** (ROI window); `fast` is QEMU itself, so there is nothing to

!andesim list models

MODEL   ENGINES       NOTES
fast    qemu          functional
cycle   vsim:<cfg>    cycle-accurate
hybrid  qemu -> vsim  QEMU fast-forwards, vsim measures the ROI; pick --trigger marker|pc|icount

---
## Mode 1 -- Lock-step DV (`run --model cycle --cosim`)

Both engines boot the **same ELF from reset**. From an *arm pc* onward the
tool drains the full architectural state **before every instruction** on
each side and compares the two streams record-by-record. The first record
that differs is the exact instruction the RTL executed wrong.

Key properties:

- **No halt slack.** The RTL side single-steps over the Debug Module
  (`dcsr.step`), so each record boundary is an exact instruction boundary.
- **Aligned by attempt index**, not by a counter. Record *k* is the state
  before execution attempt *k+1* on both sides.
- **Traps are in scope.** An `ecall`/exception lands the next record at the
  handler entry on both sides; `mepc` and `mcause` are compared, so a
  mishandled trap diverges loudly.
- The QEMU oracle runs **first** (MHz-fast) and defines the record count
  *K*; the RTL is then bounded to *K* so a diverged hart cannot run away.

### The test program must establish its own state

Lock-step compares from the arm pc, so the program must have a **deterministic
architectural state by then**. This matters because QEMU and the RTL do not
agree on *reset* state: QEMU seeds the boot-argument registers (`a0`, `a1`,
...) while the RTL resets all GPRs to 0. A constraint-generated DV testbench
handles this the standard way -- it writes **every** register in a prologue,
then begins the region to compare.

The fixture `tests/fixtures/rt_trap_ecall.S` does exactly that: it `li`s all
of `x1..x31`, then exposes a `roi_start` label, then runs two trapping
`ecall`s. We arm at `roi_start` so the prologue runs on both engines but is
not recorded; record 0 is the ROI's first instruction with identical state
on both sides.

# Build the self-initializing trap fixture (one-time).
. ./config.env 2>/dev/null
make -C tests/fixtures TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN" rt_trap_ecall.elf >/dev/null
echo "built tests/fixtures/rt_trap_ecall.elf"

# The ROI: arithmetic + two ecalls that trap to a handler and mret back.
"$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump" -d tests/fixtures/rt_trap_ecall.elf \
  | sed -n '/<roi_start>:/,/<hang>/p'

  1000b8:	00000073          	ecall
  1000bc:	0589                	c.addi	a1,2
  1000be:	00000073          	ecall
  1000c2:	00b50633          	add	a2,a0,a1
  1000c6:	6e09                	c.lui	t3,0x2
  1000c8:	c01e0e1b          	addiw	t3,t3,-1023
  1000cc:	0e4e                	c.slli	t3,0x13
  1000ce:	000e2023          	sw	zero,0(t3)

!andesim run --model cycle --cosim --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
    --pc-start roi_start --cosim-max-records 6 \
    tests/fixtures/rt_trap_ecall.elf

[cosim] PASS: 6 records match (lock-step, 1 attempt/record)

    "  before execution attempt *k+1* on both sides.\n",

    "  handler entry on both sides; `mepc` and `mcause` are compared, so a\n",
    "  mishandled trap diverges loudly.\n",

<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># andesim: a hands-on tutorial

`andesim` is one command that drives the Andes RISC-V simulators. This
notebook teaches it by running **real commands** against the binary built in
this repo. Each code cell is a plain shell command - the `!` prefix (or a `%%bash`
block) tells Jupyter to run it in the shell - so everything here is exactly what
you would type in a terminal.

## The mental model: one run = MODEL x ENGINE ( x TRIGGER )

To run something you pick up to three things:

| Axis | Question it answers | Choices |
|------|---------------------|---------|
| **model**   | which simulators run, and how they combine | `fast`, `cycle`, `hybrid` |
| **engine**  | which concrete simulator binary            | `qemu` (built in) or `vsim:<cpu>` (discovered) |
| **trigger** | (hybrid only) where the measured region starts and ends | `marker`, `pc`, `icount` |

The three models in one picture:

```
fast    QEMU only        fast (MHz speed), functional only, NO cycle count
cycle   one vsim only    cycle-accurate, but runs the WHOLE program in RTL (slow)
hybrid  QEMU  ->  vsim    QEMU fast-forwards; vsim measures only the region you pick
```

`hybrid` is the reason the tool exists: QEMU runs the boring parts quickly,
and the cycle-accurate vsim measures only the small region of interest (ROI).

> Note: `andesim` uses `--model` / `--engine` / `--trigger`. The retired
> Python reference driver (`./hsim.py`, kept as the parity golden) uses
> `--mode`; this tutorial is about `andesim`.</cell id="cell-0">
<cell id="cell-1"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Setup

Prerequisites: the driver, the simulators, and the test fixtures are already
built (`build/andesim`, `verilator/build/sim_*`, `build/qemu/...`, the QEMU
plugin, and `tests/fixtures/*.elf`). If any are missing:

```sh
bash scripts/build_driver.sh      # the driver only
# or, everything:
source ./setup.sh                 # qemu + vsim + plugin + simpoint
make -C tests/fixtures -j         # the .elf fixtures
```

The single cell below is the only Python in this notebook: it finds the repo
root, switches to it, and puts `build/` on `PATH`, so every later cell can call
`!andesim` directly. (It walks up to the `build/andesim` binary, so there
is no hardcoded path - it works wherever the repo lives.)</cell id="cell-1">
<cell id="cell-2">import os
from pathlib import Path
root = next(str(d) for d in (Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents)
            if (d / "build" / "andesim").exists())
os.chdir(root)
os.environ["PATH"] = f"{root}/build:" + os.environ["PATH"]
print("working dir:", root)</cell id="cell-2">

working dir: /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim

<cell id="cell-3"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## 1. Discover what is available

Start with `--help`. The release surface is deliberately small: just `run` and
`list`.</cell id="cell-3">
<cell id="cell-4">!andesim --help</cell id="cell-4">

usage: andesim <cmd> [args...]

Multi-engine driver for the Andes simulators (QEMU + vsim).

commands:
  run        run one simulation (--model fast|cycle|hybrid)
  list       list models|engines

(set ANDESIM_DEV=1 to show developer commands)

<cell id="cell-5"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>Developer commands (`build`, `test`, `doctor`) are hidden by default and
appear only when `ANDESIM_DEV=1` is set. They are for working on the repo,
not for running simulations. You can set the variable inline for one command:</cell id="cell-5">
<cell id="cell-6">!ANDESIM_DEV=1 andesim --help</cell id="cell-6">

usage: andesim <cmd> [args...]

Multi-engine driver for the Andes simulators (QEMU + vsim).

commands:
  run        run one simulation (--model fast|cycle|hybrid)
  list       list models|engines

developer commands:
  build      build artifacts (qemu, vsim, plugin, simpoint, fixtures, driver)
  test       run the end-to-end suite
  doctor     check environment health

<cell id="cell-7"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>`list models` shows the three compositions and what each is for.</cell id="cell-7">
<cell id="cell-8">!andesim list models</cell id="cell-8">

MODEL   ENGINES       NOTES
fast    qemu          functional
cycle   vsim:<cfg>    cycle-accurate
hybrid  qemu -> vsim  QEMU fast-forwards, vsim measures the ROI; pick --trigger marker|pc|icount

<cell id="cell-9"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>`list engines` shows the concrete simulators. `qemu` is built in. The
`vsim:<cpu>` rows are discovered at runtime by scanning `verilator/build/` for
binaries that describe themselves, so building a new CPU config makes it appear
here with no code change.

- **KIND** is what the selector keys on: `functional` (QEMU) vs
  `cycle-accurate` (vsim). `cycle` and `hybrid` need a `cycle-accurate` engine.
- **VLEN** is the vector register width in bits (`-` means not reported).</cell id="cell-9">
<cell id="cell-10">!andesim list engines</cell id="cell-10">

ENGINE                 TYPE  KIND            VLEN
qemu                   qemu  functional      -
vsim:ax45mpv_mp2       vsim  cycle-accurate  512
vsim:ax45mpv_premium   vsim  cycle-accurate  512
vsim:ax46mpv_advanced  vsim  cycle-accurate  512
vsim:ax66_makatau      vsim  cycle-accurate  128
vsim:d23               vsim  cycle-accurate  -

<cell id="cell-11"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>> This repo has **five** cycle-accurate engines built. When more than one
> exists, `cycle` and `hybrid` cannot guess which to use, so you must name one
> with `--engine` (shown below). If only one were built, it would be picked
> automatically.</cell id="cell-11">
<cell id="cell-12"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## 2. Build ONE program for every engine

`fast` runs an ELF on QEMU alone - a **transparent passthrough**: the program's
own input/output flows straight through and QEMU's exit code is propagated.

Historically you needed a different build per engine: QEMU wanted `-mvh`
(semihosting), which vsim cannot service. This repo now ships a portable
runtime - the **vplat runtime** (`runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`) -
that talks only to devices BOTH engines model at the same addresses:

| Channel | Device | QEMU ae350 | vsim |
|---------|--------|------------|------|
| stdio (fd 0-2)   | UART2 16550 @ `0xf0300000`  | yes | yes |
| exit code        | SimControl @ `0xe0080000`   | yes | yes |
| file io (fd > 2) | HTIF command @ `0xe0080010` | yes | yes |

No semihosting and no "which engine am I on" probe (a hybrid run migrates the
process between engines mid-run, so any boot-time detection would go stale) -
one binary therefore runs on `fast`, on `cycle`, and across a `hybrid`
handoff.

The runtime ships prebuilt as `build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a`
(build it with `./andesim build --what runtime`). The compile command
then needs just two extra flags: `-B build/runtime` and
`-specs=andesim.specs`, which together pull in the runtime's startup
code, linker script, and libraries so the binary runs on every engine.
The `say_hello` function and the `roi_end` label delimit the region
section 4d will measure.</cell id="cell-12">
<cell id="cell-13">%%bash
. ./config.env 2>/dev/null     # sets HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN (also done by `source ./setup.sh`)
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"
[ -x "$GCC" ] || { echo "toolchain missing - run: source ./setup.sh"; exit 1; }

cat > hello.c <<'EOF'
#include <stdio.h>

__attribute__((noinline)) void say_hello(void)
{
  printf("hello\n");
}

int main(void)
{
  say_hello();
  /* ROI end marker for hybrid --pc-end: the return point after the call. */
  __asm__ __volatile__(".globl roi_end\nroi_end:" ::: "memory");
  return 0;
}
EOF

make -C runtime TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN" >/dev/null   # build the runtime library (once)

# vplat runtime: UART stdio + SimControl exit + HTIF file io; no -mvh.
"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
  -B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs hello.c -o hello.elf

echo "built hello.elf:"; file hello.elf</cell id="cell-13">

built hello.elf:
hello.elf: ELF 64-bit LSB executable, UCB RISC-V, RVC, double-float ABI, version 1 (SYSV), statically linked, not stripped

<cell id="cell-14"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>On `fast` (pure QEMU) it prints `hello` and exits cleanly - QEMU services
the UART and the SimControl exit device:</cell id="cell-14">
<cell id="cell-15">!andesim run --model fast hello.elf</cell id="cell-15">

hello

<cell id="cell-16"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## 3. The SAME binary on pure verilator (`cycle`) - no rebuild

`cycle` runs an ELF on a single verilator (vsim) engine **from reset**, in
RTL — cycle-accurate but slow, because it simulates the whole program cycle-by-cycle in the RTL model. With the vplat build there is nothing to rebuild: the binary from
section 2 runs as-is.

This repo built several cycle-accurate engines, so `cycle` refuses to guess
and asks you to pick one with `--engine`:</cell id="cell-16">
<cell id="cell-17">!andesim run --model cycle hello.elf</cell id="cell-17">

andesim run --model cycle: model cycle: multiple cycle-accurate engines; select one with --engine (have: vsim:ax45mpv_mp2, vsim:ax45mpv_premium, vsim:ax46mpv_advanced, vsim:ax66_makatau, vsim:d23)

<cell id="cell-18"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>Name an engine and run the same `hello.elf`. It prints `hello` and **exits
0** - exactly the leg an `-mvh` (semihosting) build can never run (see
`docs/archive/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md`):</cell id="cell-18">
<cell id="cell-19">!andesim run --model cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium hello.elf</cell id="cell-19">

<cell id="cell-20"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>**Why this works.** The portable runtime talks only to a UART, an exit
device, and a file-I/O channel that BOTH engines model at the same
addresses (the table in section 2), so stdout, the exit code, and file
I/O behave identically on QEMU and vsim. The `[info]` lines are vsim's
own log on stderr; your program's output goes to stdout. (Device
addresses and the source files that model them are in
`docs/USER_GUIDE.md`.)

> The ROI markers are RISC-V HINT NOPs (`slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1`), so a
> marker binary also runs standalone on every engine -- include
> `<andesim/ROI.h>` and wrap the kernel in
> `andesim_ROI_begin()/andesim_ROI_end()`. PC symbols (here
> `say_hello` / `roi_end`) remain the way to delimit binaries you cannot
> edit, as section 4d shows.</cell id="cell-20">
<cell id="cell-21"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## 4. Model `hybrid` - the headline

`hybrid` runs two legs in one command:

```
QEMU1  -- drained state + shared memory -->  vsim
(fast-forward to the ROI)                    (measure the ROI, then drain)
```

The result is **window_cycles**: the vsim cycle count for the region, measured
as `vsim mcycle - qemu mcycle`. The result lines go to **stdout** (an
`[hsim mmap]` line, the `[... window_cycles] N` line, and a `PASS:` line); the
`[andesim] model=... engine=... trigger=...` banner goes to **stderr**. With
`!` you see both in the cell.

The **trigger** decides where the measured region begins and ends:

| Trigger | Profiles          | How the region is delimited |
|---------|-------------------|------------------------------|
| `marker`   | a kernel you mark | two HINT-NOP markers (`slti x0,x0,0x5A0/1`) compiled into the source |
| `pc`    | a kernel          | two explicit PCs you pass (`--pc-start`, `--pc-end`); a symbol or `0x` address |
| `icount`| a sampled window  | instruction counts: fast-forward N, then measure M (no markers) |

> The absolute `mcycle=...` numbers are a free-running counter and differ on
> every run. The bracketed `window_cycles` value is the figure you care about,
> and it is deterministic for a given ELF + engine + trigger.</cell id="cell-21">
<cell id="cell-22"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>The first three examples use the RVV GEMM fixtures - hybrid earns its keep
measuring a compute *region of interest*. Section 4d then closes the loop by
running the section-2 `hello.elf` through the handoff too.

### 4a. trigger `marker` - measure a marked kernel

`rt_c_v_matmul.elf` wraps its kernel in the two HINT-NOP markers (`slti x0,x0,0x5A0/1`), so
the trigger needs no parameters. This is the canonical example.</cell id="cell-22">
<cell id="cell-23">!andesim run --model hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf</cell id="cell-23">

[andesim] model=hybrid engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium vlen=512 trigger=marker fixture=rt_c_v_matmul
[hsim mmap] 128.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 251.9 GiB)




[marker window_cycles] 22808  (vsim mcycle=695138073055008 - qemu mcycle=695138073032200)
PASS: --model hybrid --trigger marker (rt_c_v_matmul)

<cell id="cell-24"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### 4b. trigger `pc` - measure between two PCs

When the binary has no markers, pass the boundary PCs yourself. `--pc-start`
accepts a **symbol name** (andesim resolves it from the ELF) or a `0x` address;
`--pc-end` is the same. Both are required.

`rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf` is the markerless twin of the kernel above. We start at
the `vmatmul_kernel` symbol and end at the return point after its call in `main`
(`0x1002c4`). To find that address yourself, disassemble and read the
instruction right after `jal ... <vmatmul_kernel>`:

```sh
$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump -d \
  tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf | grep -A1 'jal.*vmatmul_kernel'
```</cell id="cell-24">
<cell id="cell-25">!andesim run --model hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x1002c4 tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf</cell id="cell-25">

[andesim] model=hybrid engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium vlen=512 trigger=pc fixture=rt_c_v_matmul_free
[hsim mmap] 128.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 251.9 GiB)


[pc window_cycles] 22769  (vsim mcycle=695196736797057 - qemu mcycle=695196736774288)
PASS: --model hybrid --trigger pc (rt_c_v_matmul_free)

<cell id="cell-26"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>`pc` and `marker` should report nearly the same cycle count here - both wrap
the same single `vmatmul_kernel` call. The small difference is where each
boundary lands relative to the marker instructions.</cell id="cell-26">
<cell id="cell-27"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### 4c. trigger `icount` - sample a window by instruction count

For workloads you cannot edit and do not want to mark. QEMU fast-forwards
`--qemu-icount` instructions, then vsim measures `--vsim-icount` instructions and
drains. No markers needed. Defaults are `10000` / `5000`.</cell id="cell-27">
<cell id="cell-28">!andesim run --model hybrid --trigger icount --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --qemu-icount 2000 --vsim-icount 1000 tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf</cell id="cell-28">

[andesim] model=hybrid engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium vlen=512 trigger=icount fixture=rt_c_v_matmul_free
[hsim mmap] 128.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 251.9 GiB)


[icount window_cycles] 13182  (vsim mcycle=695261073781814 - qemu mcycle=695261073768632)
PASS: --model hybrid --trigger icount (rt_c_v_matmul_free)

<cell id="cell-29"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### 4d. One binary, three engines: `hello.elf` on hybrid

The same `hello.elf` already ran on `fast` (section 2) and `cycle`
(section 3). It runs the handoff too: the `pc` trigger uses the two symbols
compiled into it. QEMU fast-forwards the newlib boot and drains at
`say_hello`; vsim resumes there and the `hello` bytes go out the **modeled
UART, cycle-accurately**, before the drain at `roi_end`:</cell id="cell-29">
<cell id="cell-30">!andesim run --model hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --pc-start say_hello --pc-end roi_end hello.elf</cell id="cell-30">

[andesim] model=hybrid engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium vlen=512 trigger=pc fixture=hello
[hsim mmap] 128.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 251.9 GiB)
Copyright (C) 2013-2026 Andes Technology Corporation. All rights reserved.
Version : unknown

hello
[pc window_cycles] 14668  (vsim mcycle=742658855598908 - qemu mcycle=742658855584240)
PASS: --model hybrid --trigger pc (hello)

<cell id="cell-31"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### 4e. Cross-check the run against a QEMU oracle (`--verify`)

There is no handback leg, so nothing after your ROI ever runs - what proves
the RTL executed the ROI *correctly*? `--verify` (default OFF) answers it
with a differential check: the same ELF re-runs on pure QEMU (the oracle),
the plugin drains the full architectural state at the ROI exit - sampled at
the exact pc where vsim halted - and the driver diffs the two drains field
by field:

- **compared**: pc, all 32 GPRs, the FPRs, the V CSRs and full vector
  registers;
- **excluded**: `mcycle`/`minstret` (the engines count differently by
  design) and the passthrough M-CSRs/PMP (vsim copies those from the entry
  snapshot, so there is nothing fresh to compare).

Any divergence prints a `[state-diff] field: ref=... got=...` line per
mismatching field and the run exits non-zero. A clean run costs one extra
MHz-class QEMU pass - cheap next to the vsim leg. **Trigger constraint**: `--verify` requires `--trigger marker|pc`; it is rejected for `--trigger icount` (the icount window boundary differs between legs and has no single oracle arm point).</cell id="cell-31">
<cell id="cell-32">!andesim run --model hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --verify tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf</cell id="cell-32">

[andesim] model=hybrid engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium vlen=512 trigger=marker fixture=rt_c_v_matmul
[hsim mmap] 128.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 251.9 GiB)
[andesim] verify: oracle leg (pure QEMU drains at the ROI exit, pc=0x1002d0)
Copyright (C) 2013-2026 Andes Technology Corporation. All rights reserved.
Version : unknown

[marker window_cycles] 22821  (vsim mcycle=974634114459685 - qemu mcycle=974634114436864)
[hsim mmap] 128.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 251.9 GiB)
[state-diff] PASS: 109 fields match (counters and passthrough CSRs excluded)
[verify] PASS: vsim drain matches the QEMU oracle
PASS: --model hybrid --trigger marker (rt_c_v_matmul)

<cell id="cell-33"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>The usual `window_cycles` figure as in 4a, plus the two verification
lines:
`[state-diff] PASS: 109 fields match` is the field-by-field compare,
`[verify] PASS` the verdict. The oracle's stderr banner shows the sample
point (`pc=...` - vsim's actual halt pc).

For regression testing, the whole e2e suite takes the same check with
`VERIFY=1 JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`. Details (and the failure
anatomy) in `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` section 4.7.</cell id="cell-33">
<cell id="cell-34"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### 4f. Localize a divergence with checkpoint co-sim (`--cosim`)

`--verify` (4e) tells you THAT the vsim leg diverged; `--cosim` tells you
roughly WHERE. It is a developer tool (hidden from the release help, like
`state-diff` - set `ANDESIM_DEV=1` to see it in `run --help`):

```
hybrid run:  QEMU1 -> vsim: ..N insns..|..N insns..|.. exit
                              ckpt 1      ckpt 2      final drain
oracle run:  pure QEMU, drains at the SAME retire counts
diff ckpt k vs ckpt k -> first mismatch = the bad N-instruction window
```

Every N retired instructions (default 10000, `--cosim-interval` overrides)
the vsim leg halts the hart over DMI, drains a full architectural
checkpoint, and resumes. The driver reads each checkpoint's
`minstret - entry.minstret` (the exact post-entry retire count), re-runs
the ELF on pure QEMU with the plugin draining at those same counts, and
diffs checkpoint against checkpoint with the `state-diff` policy. The two
runs never share memory: the oracle replays the same deterministic program
from boot on its own RAM, so the shared mmap needs no change.</cell id="cell-34">
<cell id="cell-35">!andesim run --model hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --cosim --cosim-interval 500 tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf</cell id="cell-35">

[andesim] model=hybrid engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium vlen=512 trigger=marker fixture=rt_c_v_matmul
[hsim mmap] 128.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 251.7 GiB)
[andesim] cosim: oracle leg (pure QEMU, 3 checkpoint(s) + final at retire deltas 499:982:1462:1692)
Copyright (C) 2013-2026 Andes Technology Corporation. All rights reserved.
Version : unknown

[hsim mmap] 128.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 251.7 GiB)
[cosim] PASS: 3 checkpoint(s) + final state match the QEMU oracle (interval 500, 1692 ROI retires)
PASS: --model hybrid --trigger marker (rt_c_v_matmul)

<cell id="cell-36"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>The GEMM ROI retires 1692 instructions, so interval 500 gives three
checkpoints; `[cosim] PASS` means all three AND the final state match the
oracle. On a divergence you instead get the mismatching fields and the
window that contains the first bad instruction:

```
[state-diff] x12: ref=0x2a got=0x2b
[cosim] FAIL: divergence in window 2 (retires 500..1000 after entry)
```

Re-run with a smaller `--cosim-interval` to shrink the window.

**Limitations of this co-sim design**

- **Window granularity, not instruction granularity.** A divergence is
  bracketed to one N-instruction window; finding the exact instruction
  means re-running with a smaller N. Intervals near the DMI halt overshoot
  (tens of instructions) are not meaningful.
- **Registers only - memory is not compared.** Each checkpoint covers pc,
  GPRs, FPRs, V CSRs and vector registers. A wrong store is caught only
  later, when the bad value is loaded back into a register.
- **No cycle figure.** Every checkpoint adds a DMI halt + drain + resume
  on the vsim leg, which pollutes the vsim `mcycle` delta, so `--cosim`
  suppresses `window_cycles` entirely. Re-run without `--cosim` to
  measure.
- **`--trigger marker|pc` only, `--model hybrid` only.** The oracle must
  arm on a code boundary; the icount trigger's window semantics differ
  between the legs. Exclusive with `--verify` (the final-state check is
  already included).
- **Single-shot, deterministic runs only.** The oracle replays the program
  from boot, so the pre-ROI path must be deterministic, and the ROI is
  assumed to be entered once (same assumptions as the hybrid run itself).
- **Counters are excluded from the compare** (`mcycle`/`minstret` differ
  between engines by design), as are the passthrough M-CSRs/PMP - same
  policy as `state-diff`.

Details in `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` section 4.8.</cell id="cell-36">
<cell id="cell-37"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## 5. Picking an engine with `--engine`

`--engine <id>` selects which simulator to use. For `fast` it must be `qemu`
(the only functional engine). For `cycle` and `hybrid` it names one of the
`vsim:<cpu>` rows from `list engines`. Different CPU configs have different
microarchitectures and VLEN, so the same workload reports different cycles.

Try it yourself - rerun the marker example (section 4a) on a different core and
compare the number:

```sh
andesim run --model hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_mp2 \
  tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf
```

A heavier core simulates more slowly. If a leg exceeds the built-in 90 s per-leg
timeout, andesim stops it with `plan step 1: timed out after 90000 ms`; in that
case measure a smaller window (e.g. `--trigger icount` with small counts) or pick
a lighter core.</cell id="cell-37">
<cell id="cell-38"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## 6. Forwarding native engine flags with `--`

Everything after a lone `--` is passed to the engine **verbatim**; andesim does
not interpret it. For simple cases, use the dedicated `--gdb` flag instead:

```sh
# fast: QEMU gdbstub on port 1234 (default); pauses at startup for a debugger to attach.
andesim run --model fast --gdb tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf
# custom port:
andesim run --model fast --gdb --gdb-port 2345 tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf

# cycle: vsim JTAG on port 9104 (default) + ICEman in foreground (requires $ICEMAN).
andesim run --model cycle --gdb --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf
```

`--gdb` is not supported with `--model hybrid` (the two-leg pipeline cannot pause mid-handoff for a debugger).

For flags that have no dedicated wrapper — waveform capture, monitor console, or any engine-specific argument not exposed by andesim — use `--` passthrough:

```sh
andesim run --model fast tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf -- -gdb tcp::1234 -S
```

(Not run here — it blocks waiting for a debugger.)</cell id="cell-38">
<cell id="cell-39"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## 7. Developer commands (optional)

Set `ANDESIM_DEV=1` to reveal `build`, `test`, and `doctor` (section 1). They
build the artifacts, run the end-to-end suite, and check environment health -
useful when working on the repo, not when just running simulations. For most
build/test work the documented entry points are `bash scripts/build_driver.sh`,
`source ./setup.sh`, and `bash scripts/run_e2e.sh` (use `JOBS=8`).</cell id="cell-39">
<cell id="cell-40"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## 8. Cheat sheet and where to go next

```sh
andesim list models                        # the 3 compositions
andesim list engines                        # the concrete simulators
andesim run --model fast  ELF                            # QEMU only, functional
andesim run --model fast  --gdb [--gdb-port PORT] ELF    # QEMU gdbstub (default port 1234)
andesim run --model cycle --engine vsim:<cpu> ELF        # one vsim, from reset
andesim run --model cycle --engine vsim:<cpu> --gdb ELF  # vsim JTAG + ICEman (requires $ICEMAN; default port 9104)
andesim run --model hybrid --trigger marker    --engine vsim:<cpu> ELF
andesim run --model hybrid --trigger pc     --engine vsim:<cpu> --pc-start S --pc-end E ELF
andesim run --model hybrid --trigger icount --engine vsim:<cpu> --qemu-icount N --vsim-icount M ELF
andesim run --model hybrid --trigger marker    --engine vsim:<cpu> --verify ELF   # + QEMU-oracle cross-check
andesim run --model hybrid --trigger marker    --engine vsim:<cpu> --cosim ELF    # localize a divergence (dev)

# one vplat-built ELF runs on all three models (sections 2, 3, 4d):
andesim run --model hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:<cpu> \
  --pc-start say_hello --pc-end roi_end hello.elf
```

Next:

- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` - the full guide (build, configure, every mode).
- `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md` - one deep-dive exercise per trigger.
- `CLAUDE.md` - key files and the architecture summary.
- `runtime/` - the engine-portable runtime library; link it with
  `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs` (one build for fast / cycle /
  hybrid; sections 2-3).</cell id="cell-40">

cells.source:
# andesim: a hands-on tutorial

`andesim` is one command that drives the Andes RISC-V simulators. This
notebook teaches it by running **real commands** against the binary built in
this repo. Each code cell is a plain shell command - the `!` prefix (or a `%%bash`
block) tells Jupyter to run it in the shell - so everything here is exactly what
you would type in a terminal.

## The mental model: one run = MODEL x ENGINE ( x TRIGGER )

To run something you pick up to three things:

| Axis | Question it answers | Choices |
|------|---------------------|---------|
| **model**   | which simulators run, and how they combine | `fast`, `cycle`, `hybrid` |
| **engine**  | which concrete simulator binary            | `qemu` (built in) or `vsim:<cpu>` (discovered) |
| **trigger** | (hybrid only) where the measured region starts and ends | `marker`, `pc`, `icount` |

The three models in one picture:

```
fast    QEMU only        fast (MHz speed), functional only, NO cycle count
cycle   one vsim only    cycle-accurate, but runs the WHOLE program in RTL (slow)
hybrid  QEMU  ->  vsim    QEMU fast-forwards; vsim measures only the region you pick
```

`hybrid` is the reason the tool exists: QEMU runs the boring parts quickly,
and the cycle-accurate vsim measures only the small region of interest (ROI).

> Note: `andesim` uses `--model` / `--engine` / `--trigger`. The retired
> Python reference driver (`./hsim.py`, kept as the parity golden) uses
> `--mode`; this tutorial is about `andesim`.

## Setup

Prerequisites: the driver, the simulators, and the test fixtures are already
built (`build/andesim`, `verilator/build/sim_*`, `build/qemu/...`, the QEMU
plugin, and `tests/fixtures/*.elf`). If any are missing:

```sh
bash scripts/build_driver.sh      # the driver only
# or, everything:
source ./setup.sh                 # qemu + vsim + plugin + simpoint
make -C tests/fixtures -j         # the .elf fixtures
```

The single cell below is the only Python in this notebook: it finds the repo
root, switches to it, and puts `build/` on `PATH`, so every later cell can call
`!andesim` directly. (It walks up to the `build/andesim` binary, so there
is no hardcoded path - it works wherever the repo lives.)

import os
from pathlib import Path
root = next(str(d) for d in (Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents)
            if (d / "build" / "andesim").exists())
os.chdir(root)
os.environ["PATH"] = f"{root}/build:" + os.environ["PATH"]
print("working dir:", root)

outputs.text: working dir: /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim

`list engines` shows the concrete simulators. `qemu` is built in. The

here with no code change.

- **KIND** is what the selector keys on: `functional` (QEMU) vs
  `cycle-accurate` (vsim). `cycle` and `hybrid` need a `cycle-accurate` engine.
- **VLEN** is the vector register width in bits (`-` means not reported).
!andesim list engines

outputs.text:

qemu                   qemu  functional      -
vsim:ax45mpv_mp2       vsim  cycle-accurate  512
vsim:ax45mpv_premium   vsim  cycle-accurate  512

cells.source:
> This repo has **five** cycle-accurate engines built. When more than one
> exists, `cycle` and `hybrid` cannot guess which to use, so you must name one
> with `--engine` (shown below). If only one were built, it would be picked
> automatically.

## 2. Build ONE program for every engine

`fast` runs an ELF on QEMU alone - a **transparent passthrough**: the program's
own input/output flows straight through and QEMU's exit code is propagated.

Historically you needed a different build per engine: QEMU wanted `-mvh`
(semihosting), which vsim cannot service. This repo now ships a portable
runtime - the **vplat runtime** (`runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`) -
that talks only to devices BOTH engines model at the same addresses:

| Channel | Device | QEMU ae350 | vsim |
|---------|--------|------------|------|
| stdio (fd 0-2)   | UART2 16550 @ `0xf0300000`  | yes | yes |
| exit code        | SimControl @ `0xe0080000`   | yes | yes |
| file io (fd > 2) | HTIF command @ `0xe0080010` | yes | yes |

No semihosting and no "which engine am I on" probe (a hybrid run migrates the
process between engines mid-run, so any boot-time detection would go stale) -
one binary therefore runs on `fast`, on `cycle`, and across a `hybrid`
handoff.

The runtime ships prebuilt as `build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a`
(build it with `./andesim build --what runtime`). The compile command
then needs just two extra flags: `-B build/runtime` and
`-specs=andesim.specs`, which together pull in the runtime's startup
code, linker script, and libraries so the binary runs on every engine.
The `say_hello` function and the `roi_end` label delimit the region
section 4d will measure.

outputs.text:
built hello.elf:
hello.elf: ELF 64-bit LSB executable, UCB RISC-V, RVC, double-float ABI, version 1 (SYSV), statically linked, not stripped

cells.source:
On `fast` (pure QEMU) it prints `hello` and exits cleanly - QEMU services
the UART and the SimControl exit device:
!andesim run --model fast hello.elf

outputs.text: hello

cells.source:
## 3. The SAME binary on pure verilator (`cycle`) - no rebuild

`cycle` runs an ELF on a single verilator (vsim) engine **from reset**, in
RTL — cycle-accurate but slow, because it simulates the whole program cycle-by-cycle in the RTL model. With the vplat build there is nothing to rebuild: the binary from
section 2 runs as-is.

This repo built several cycle-accurate engines, so `cycle` refuses to guess
and asks you to pick one with `--engine`:
!andesim run --model cycle hello.elf

**Why this works.** The portable runtime talks only to a UART, an exit
device, and a file-I/O channel that BOTH engines model at the same
addresses (the table in section 2), so stdout, the exit code, and file
I/O behave identically on QEMU and vsim. The `[info]` lines are vsim's
own log on stderr; your program's output goes to stdout. (Device
addresses and the source files that model them are in
`docs/USER_GUIDE.md`.)

> The ROI markers are RISC-V HINT NOPs (`slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1`), so a
> marker binary also runs standalone on every engine -- include
> `<andesim/ROI.h>` and wrap the kernel in
> `andesim_ROI_begin()/andesim_ROI_end()`. PC symbols (here
> `say_hello` / `roi_end`) remain the way to delimit binaries you cannot
> edit, as section 4d shows.

## 4. Model `hybrid` - the headline

`hybrid` runs two legs in one command:

```
QEMU1  -- drained state + shared memory -->  vsim
(fast-forward to the ROI)                    (measure the ROI, then drain)
```

The result is **window_cycles**: the vsim cycle count for the region, measured
as `vsim mcycle - qemu mcycle`. The result lines go to **stdout** (an
`[hsim mmap]` line, the `[... window_cycles] N` line, and a `PASS:` line); the
`[andesim] model=... engine=... trigger=...` banner goes to **stderr**. With
`!` you see both in the cell.

The **trigger** decides where the measured region begins and ends:

| Trigger | Profiles          | How the region is delimited |
|---------|-------------------|------------------------------|
| `marker`   | a kernel you mark | two HINT-NOP markers (`slti x0,x0,0x5A0/1`) compiled into the source |
| `pc`    | a kernel          | two explicit PCs you pass (`--pc-start`, `--pc-end`); a symbol or `0x` address |
| `icount`| a sampled window  | instruction counts: fast-forward N, then measure M (no markers) |

> The absolute `mcycle=...` numbers are a free-running counter and differ on
> every run. The bracketed `window_cycles` value is the figure you care about,
> and it is deterministic for a given ELF + engine + trigger.

The first three examples use the RVV GEMM fixtures - hybrid earns its keep
measuring a compute *region of interest*. Section 4d then closes the loop by
running the section-2 `hello.elf` through the handoff too.

### 4a. trigger `marker` - measure a marked kernel

`rt_c_v_matmul.elf` wraps its kernel in the two HINT-NOP markers (`slti x0,x0,0x5A0/1`), so
the trigger needs no parameters. This is the canonical example.
!andesim run --model hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf

outputs.text:
[andesim] model=hybrid engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium vlen=512 trigger=marker fixture=rt_c_v_matmul
[hsim mmap] 128.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 251.9 GiB)

[marker window_cycles] 22808  (vsim mcycle=695138073055008 - qemu mcycle=695138073032200)
PASS: --model hybrid --trigger marker (rt_c_v_matmul)

cells.source:
### 4b. trigger `pc` - measure between two PCs

When the binary has no markers, pass the boundary PCs yourself. `--pc-start`
accepts a **symbol name** (andesim resolves it from the ELF) or a `0x` address;
`--pc-end` is the same. Both are required.

`rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf` is the markerless twin of the kernel above. We start at
the `vmatmul_kernel` symbol and end at the return point after its call in `main`
(`0x1002c4`). To find that address yourself, disassemble and read the
instruction right after `jal ... <vmatmul_kernel>`:

```sh
$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump -d \
  tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf | grep -A1 'jal.*vmatmul_kernel'
```
!andesim run --model hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x1002c4 tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf

outputs.text:
[andesim] model=hybrid engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium vlen=512 trigger=pc fixture=rt_c_v_matmul_free
[hsim mmap] 128.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 251.9 GiB)

[pc window_cycles] 22769  (vsim mcycle=695196736797057 - qemu mcycle=695196736774288)
PASS: --model hybrid --trigger pc (rt_c_v_matmul_free)

cells.source:
`pc` and `marker` should report nearly the same cycle count here - both wrap
the same single `vmatmul_kernel` call. The small difference is where each
boundary lands relative to the marker instructions.

### 4c. trigger `icount` - sample a window by instruction count

For workloads you cannot edit and do not want to mark. QEMU fast-forwards
`--qemu-icount` instructions, then vsim measures `--vsim-icount` instructions and
drains. No markers needed. Defaults are `10000` / `5000`.
!andesim run --model hybrid --trigger icount --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --qemu-icount 2000 --vsim-icount 1000 tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf

outputs.text:
[andesim] model=hybrid engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium vlen=512 trigger=icount fixture=rt_c_v_matmul_free
[hsim mmap] 128.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 251.9 GiB)

[icount window_cycles] 13182  (vsim mcycle=695261073781814 - qemu mcycle=695261073768632)
PASS: --model hybrid --trigger icount (rt_c_v_matmul_free)

cells.source:
### 4d. One binary, three engines: `hello.elf` on hybrid

The same `hello.elf` already ran on `fast` (section 2) and `cycle`
(section 3). It runs the handoff too: the `pc` trigger uses the two symbols
compiled into it. QEMU fast-forwards the newlib boot and drains at
`say_hello`; vsim resumes there and the `hello` bytes go out the **modeled
UART, cycle-accurately**, before the drain at `roi_end`:
!andesim run --model hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --pc-start say_hello --pc-end roi_end hello.elf

outputs.text:
[andesim] model=hybrid engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium vlen=512 trigger=pc fixture=hello
[hsim mmap] 128.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 251.9 GiB)
Copyright (C) 2013-2026 Andes Technology Corporation. All rights reserved.
Version : unknown

hello
[pc window_cycles] 14668  (vsim mcycle=742658855598908 - qemu mcycle=742658855584240)
PASS: --model hybrid --trigger pc (hello)

cells.source:
### 4e. Cross-check the run against a QEMU oracle (`--verify`)

There is no handback leg, so nothing after your ROI ever runs - what proves
the RTL executed the ROI *correctly*? `--verify` (default OFF) answers it
with a differential check: the same ELF re-runs on pure QEMU (the oracle),
the plugin drains the full architectural state at the ROI exit - sampled at
the exact pc where vsim halted - and the driver diffs the two drains field
by field:

- **compared**: pc, all 32 GPRs, the FPRs, the V CSRs and full vector
  registers;
- **excluded**: `mcycle`/`minstret` (the engines count differently by
  design) and the passthrough M-CSRs/PMP (vsim copies those from the entry
  snapshot, so there is nothing fresh to compare).

Any divergence prints a `[state-diff] field: ref=... got=...` line per
mismatching field and the run exits non-zero. A clean run costs one extra
MHz-class QEMU pass - cheap next to the vsim leg. **Trigger constraint**: `--verify` requires `--trigger marker|pc`; it is rejected for `--trigger icount` (the icount window boundary differs between legs and has no single oracle arm point).
!andesim run --model hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --verify tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf

outputs.text:
[andesim] model=hybrid engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium vlen=512 trigger=marker fixture=rt_c_v_matmul
[hsim mmap] 128.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 251.9 GiB)
[andesim] verify: oracle leg (pure QEMU drains at the ROI exit, pc=0x1002d0)
Copyright (C) 2013-2026 Andes Technology Corporation. All rights reserved.
Version : unknown

[marker window_cycles] 22821  (vsim mcycle=974634114459685 - qemu mcycle=974634114436864)
[hsim mmap] 128.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 251.9 GiB)
[state-diff] PASS: 109 fields match (counters and passthrough CSRs excluded)
[verify] PASS: vsim drain matches the QEMU oracle
PASS: --model hybrid --trigger marker (rt_c_v_matmul)

cells.source:
The usual `window_cycles` figure as in 4a, plus the two verification
lines:
`[state-diff] PASS: 109 fields match` is the field-by-field compare,
`[verify] PASS` the verdict. The oracle's stderr banner shows the sample
point (`pc=...` - vsim's actual halt pc).

For regression testing, the whole e2e suite takes the same check with
`VERIFY=1 JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`. Details (and the failure
anatomy) in `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` section 4.7.

### 4f. Localize a divergence with checkpoint co-sim (`--cosim`)

`--verify` (4e) tells you THAT the vsim leg diverged; `--cosim` tells you
roughly WHERE. It is a developer tool (hidden from the release help, like
`state-diff` - set `ANDESIM_DEV=1` to see it in `run --help`):

```
hybrid run:  QEMU1 -> vsim: ..N insns..|..N insns..|.. exit
                              ckpt 1      ckpt 2      final drain
oracle run:  pure QEMU, drains at the SAME retire counts
diff ckpt k vs ckpt k -> first mismatch = the bad N-instruction window
```

Every N retired instructions (default 10000, `--cosim-interval` overrides)
the vsim leg halts the hart over DMI, drains a full architectural
checkpoint, and resumes. The driver reads each checkpoint's
`minstret - entry.minstret` (the exact post-entry retire count), re-runs
the ELF on pure QEMU with the plugin draining at those same counts, and
diffs checkpoint against checkpoint with the `state-diff` policy. The two
runs never share memory: the oracle replays the same deterministic program
from boot on its own RAM, so the shared mmap needs no change.
!andesim run --model hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --cosim --cosim-interval 500 tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf

outputs.text:
[andesim] model=hybrid engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium vlen=512 trigger=marker fixture=rt_c_v_matmul
[hsim mmap] 128.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 251.7 GiB)
[andesim] cosim: oracle leg (pure QEMU, 3 checkpoint(s) + final at retire deltas 499:982:1462:1692)
Copyright (C) 2013-2026 Andes Technology Corporation. All rights reserved.
Version : unknown

[hsim mmap] 128.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 251.7 GiB)
[cosim] PASS: 3 checkpoint(s) + final state match the QEMU oracle (interval 500, 1692 ROI retires)
PASS: --model hybrid --trigger marker (rt_c_v_matmul)

cells.source:
The GEMM ROI retires 1692 instructions, so interval 500 gives three
checkpoints; `[cosim] PASS` means all three AND the final state match the
oracle. On a divergence you instead get the mismatching fields and the
window that contains the first bad instruction:

```
[state-diff] x12: ref=0x2a got=0x2b
[cosim] FAIL: divergence in window 2 (retires 500..1000 after entry)
```

Re-run with a smaller `--cosim-interval` to shrink the window.

**Limitations of this co-sim design**

- **Window granularity, not instruction granularity.** A divergence is
  bracketed to one N-instruction window; finding the exact instruction
  means re-running with a smaller N. Intervals near the DMI halt overshoot
  (tens of instructions) are not meaningful.
- **Registers only - memory is not compared.** Each checkpoint covers pc,
  GPRs, FPRs, V CSRs and vector registers. A wrong store is caught only
  later, when the bad value is loaded back into a register.
- **No cycle figure.** Every checkpoint adds a DMI halt + drain + resume
  on the vsim leg, which pollutes the vsim `mcycle` delta, so `--cosim`
  suppresses `window_cycles` entirely. Re-run without `--cosim` to
  measure.
- **`--trigger marker|pc` only, `--model hybrid` only.** The oracle must
  arm on a code boundary; the icount trigger's window semantics differ
  between the legs. Exclusive with `--verify` (the final-state check is
  already included).
- **Single-shot, deterministic runs only.** The oracle replays the program
  from boot, so the pre-ROI path must be deterministic, and the ROI is
  assumed to be entered once (same assumptions as the hybrid run itself).
- **Counters are excluded from the compare** (`mcycle`/`minstret` differ
  between engines by design), as are the passthrough M-CSRs/PMP - same
  policy as `state-diff`.

Details in `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` section 4.8.

## 5. Picking an engine with `--engine`

`--engine <id>` selects which simulator to use. For `fast` it must be `qemu`
(the only functional engine). For `cycle` and `hybrid` it names one of the
`vsim:<cpu>` rows from `list engines`. Different CPU configs have different
microarchitectures and VLEN, so the same workload reports different cycles.

Try it yourself - rerun the marker example (section 4a) on a different core and
compare the number:

```sh
andesim run --model hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_mp2 \
  tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf
```

A heavier core simulates more slowly. If a leg exceeds the built-in 90 s per-leg
timeout, andesim stops it with `plan step 1: timed out after 90000 ms`; in that
case measure a smaller window (e.g. `--trigger icount` with small counts) or pick
a lighter core.

## 6. Forwarding native engine flags with `--`

Everything after a lone `--` is passed to the engine **verbatim**; andesim does
not interpret it. For simple cases, use the dedicated `--gdb` flag instead:

```sh
# fast: QEMU gdbstub on port 1234 (default); pauses at startup for a debugger to attach.
andesim run --model fast --gdb tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf
# custom port:
andesim run --model fast --gdb --gdb-port 2345 tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf

# cycle: vsim JTAG on port 9104 (default) + ICEman in foreground (requires $ICEMAN).
andesim run --model cycle --gdb --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf
```

`--gdb` is not supported with `--model hybrid` (the two-leg pipeline cannot pause mid-handoff for a debugger).

For flags that have no dedicated wrapper — waveform capture, monitor console, or any engine-specific argument not exposed by andesim — use `--` passthrough:

```sh
andesim run --model fast tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf -- -gdb tcp::1234 -S
```

(Not run here — it blocks waiting for a debugger.)

## 7. Developer commands (optional)

Set `ANDESIM_DEV=1` to reveal `build`, `test`, and `doctor` (section 1). They
build the artifacts, run the end-to-end suite, and check environment health -
useful when working on the repo, not when just running simulations. For most
build/test work the documented entry points are `bash scripts/build_driver.sh`,
`source ./setup.sh`, and `bash scripts/run_e2e.sh` (use `JOBS=8`).

## 8. Cheat sheet and where to go next

```sh
andesim list models                        # the 3 compositions
andesim list engines                        # the concrete simulators
andesim run --model fast  ELF                            # QEMU only, functional
andesim run --model fast  --gdb [--gdb-port PORT] ELF    # QEMU gdbstub (default port 1234)
andesim run --model cycle --engine vsim:<cpu> ELF        # one vsim, from reset
andesim run --model cycle --engine vsim:<cpu> --gdb ELF  # vsim JTAG + ICEman (requires $ICEMAN; default port 9104)
andesim run --model hybrid --trigger marker    --engine vsim:<cpu> ELF
andesim run --model hybrid --trigger pc     --engine vsim:<cpu> --pc-start S --pc-end E ELF
andesim run --model hybrid --trigger icount --engine vsim:<cpu> --qemu-icount N --vsim-icount M ELF
andesim run --model hybrid --trigger marker    --engine vsim:<cpu> --verify ELF   # + QEMU-oracle cross-check
andesim run --model hybrid --trigger marker    --engine vsim:<cpu> --cosim ELF    # localize a divergence (dev)

# one vplat-built ELF runs on all three models (sections 2, 3, 4d):
andesim run --model hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:<cpu> \
  --pc-start say_hello --pc-end roi_end hello.elf
```

Next:

- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` - the full guide (build, configure, every mode).
- `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md` - one deep-dive exercise per trigger.
- `CLAUDE.md` - key files and the architecture summary.
- `runtime/` - the engine-portable runtime library; link it with
  `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs` (one build for fast / cycle /
  hybrid; sections 2-3).
