=============== idx 0 ===============
'# andesim: a hands-on tutorial

`andesim` is one command that drives the Andes RISC-V simulators. This
notebook teaches it by running **real commands** against the binary built in
this repo. Each code cell is a plain shell command - the `!` prefix (or a `%%bash`
block) tells Jupyter to run it in the shell - so everything here is exactly what
you would type in a terminal.

## The mental model: one run = MODEL x ENGINE ( x TRIGGER )

To run something you pick up to three things:

| Axis | Question it answers | Choices |
|------|---------------------|---------|
| **model**   | which simulators run, and how they combine | `fast`, `cycle`, `hybrid` |
| **engine**  | which concrete simulator binary            | `qemu` (built in) or `vsim:<cpu>` (discovered) |
| **trigger** | (hybrid only) where the measured region starts and ends | `marker`, `pc`, `icount` |

The three models in one picture:

```
fast    QEMU only        fast (MHz speed), functional only, NO cycle count
cycle   one vsim only    cycle-accurate, but runs the WHOLE program in RTL (slow)
hybrid  QEMU  ->  vsim    QEMU fast-forwards; vsim measures only the region you pick
```

`hybrid` is the reason the tool exists: QEMU runs the boring parts quickly,
and the cycle-accurate vsim measures only the small region of interest (ROI).

> Note: `andesim` uses `--mode` / `--engine` / `--trigger`. The retired
> Python reference driver (`./hsim.py`, kept as the parity golden) uses
> `--mode`; this tutorial is about `andesim`.'

=============== idx 5 ===============
'Developer commands (`build`, `test`, `doctor`) are hidden by default and
appear only when `ANDESIM_DEV=1` is set. They are for working on the repo,
not for running simulations. You can set the variable inline for one command:'

=============== idx 6 ===============
'!ANDESIM_DEV=1 andesim --help'

=============== idx 12 ===============
'## 2. Build ONE program for every engine

`fast` runs an ELF on QEMU alone - a **transparent passthrough**: the program's
own input/output flows straight through and QEMU's exit code is propagated.

Historically you needed a different build per engine: QEMU wanted `-mvh`
(semihosting), which vsim cannot service. This repo now ships a portable
runtime - the **vplat runtime** (`runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`) -
that talks only to devices BOTH engines model at the same addresses:

| Channel | Device | QEMU ae350 | vsim |
|---------|--------|------------|------|
| stdio (fd 0-2)   | UART2 16550 @ `0xf0300000`  | yes | yes |
| exit code        | SimControl @ `0xe0080000`   | yes | yes |
| file io (fd > 2) | HTIF command @ `0xe0080010` | yes | yes |

No semihosting and no "which engine am I on" probe (a hybrid run migrates the
process between engines mid-run, so any boot-time detection would go stale) -
one binary therefore runs on `fast`, on `cycle`, and across a `hybrid`
handoff.

The runtime ships prebuilt as `build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a`
(build it with `./andesim build --what runtime`). The compile command
then needs just two extra flags: `-B build/runtime` and
`-specs=andesim.specs`, which together pull in the runtime's startup
code, linker script, and libraries so the binary runs on every engine.
The `say_hello` function and the `roi_end` label delimit the region
section 4d will measure.'

=============== idx 21 ===============
'## 4. Model `hybrid` - the headline

`hybrid` runs two legs in one command:

```
QEMU1  -- drained state + shared memory -->  vsim
(fast-forward to the ROI)                    (measure the ROI, then drain)
```

The result is **window_cycles**: the vsim cycle count for the region, measured
as `vsim mcycle - qemu mcycle`. The result lines go to **stdout** (an
`[hsim mmap]` line, the `[... window_cycles] N` line, and a `PASS:` line); the
`[andesim] model=... engine=... trigger=...` banner goes to **stderr**. With
`!` you see both in the cell.

The **trigger** decides where the measured region begins and ends:

| Trigger | Profiles          | How the region is delimited |
|---------|-------------------|------------------------------|
| `marker`   | a kernel you mark | two HINT-NOP markers (`slti x0,x0,0x5A0/1`) compiled into the source |
| `pc`    | a kernel          | two explicit PCs you pass (`--pc-start`, `--pc-end`); a symbol or `0x` address |
| `icount`| a sampled window  | instruction counts: fast-forward N, then measure M (no markers) |

> The absolute `mcycle=...` numbers are a free-running counter and differ on
> every run. The bracketed `window_cycles` value is the figure you care about,
> and it is deterministic for a given ELF + engine + trigger.'

=============== idx 31 ===============
'### 4e. Cross-check the run against a QEMU oracle (`--verify`)

There is no handback leg, so nothing after your ROI ever runs - what proves
the RTL executed the ROI *correctly*? `--verify` (default OFF) answers it
with a differential check: the same ELF re-runs on pure QEMU (the oracle),
the plugin drains the full architectural state at the ROI exit - sampled at
the exact pc where vsim halted - and the driver diffs the two drains field
by field:

- **compared**: pc, all 32 GPRs, the FPRs, the V CSRs and full vector
  registers;
- **excluded**: `mcycle`/`minstret` (the engines count differently by
  design) and the passthrough M-CSRs/PMP (vsim copies those from the entry
  snapshot, so there is nothing fresh to compare).

Any divergence prints a `[state-diff] field: ref=... got=...` line per
mismatching field and the run exits non-zero. A clean run costs one extra
MHz-class QEMU pass - cheap next to the vsim leg. **Trigger constraint**: `--verify` requires `--trigger marker|pc`; it is rejected for `--trigger icount` (the icount window boundary differs between legs and has no single oracle arm point).'

=============== idx 33 ===============
"The usual `window_cycles` figure as in 4a, plus the two verification
lines:
`[state-diff] PASS: 109 fields match` is the field-by-field compare,
`[verify] PASS` the verdict. The oracle's stderr banner shows the sample
point (`pc=...` - vsim's actual halt pc).

For regression testing, the whole e2e suite takes the same check with
`VERIFY=1 JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`. Details (and the failure
anatomy) in `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` section 4.7."

=============== idx 34 ===============
"### 4f. Localize a divergence with checkpoint co-sim (`--cosim`)

`--verify` (4e) tells you THAT the vsim leg diverged; `--cosim` tells you
roughly WHERE. It is a developer tool (hidden from the release help, like
`state-diff` - set `ANDESIM_DEV=1` to see it in `run --help`):

```
hybrid run:  QEMU1 -> vsim: ..N insns..|..N insns..|.. exit
                              ckpt 1      ckpt 2      final drain
oracle run:  pure QEMU, drains at the SAME retire counts
diff ckpt k vs ckpt k -> first mismatch = the bad N-instruction window
```

Every N retired instructions (default 10000, `--cosim-interval` overrides)
the vsim leg halts the hart over DMI, drains a full architectural
checkpoint, and resumes. The driver reads each checkpoint's
`minstret - entry.minstret` (the exact post-entry retire count), re-runs
the ELF on pure QEMU with the plugin draining at those same counts, and
diffs checkpoint against checkpoint with the `state-diff` policy. The two
runs never share memory: the oracle replays the same deterministic program
from boot on its own RAM, so the shared mmap needs no change."

=============== idx 37 ===============
'## 5. Picking an engine with `--engine`

`--engine <id>` selects which simulator to use. For `fast` it must be `qemu`
(the only functional engine). For `cycle` and `hybrid` it names one of the
`vsim:<cpu>` rows from `list engines`. Different CPU configs have different
microarchitectures and VLEN, so the same workload reports different cycles.

Try it yourself - rerun the marker example (section 4a) on a different core and
compare the number:

```sh
andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_mp2 \
  tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf
```

A heavier core simulates more slowly. If a leg exceeds the built-in 90 s per-leg
timeout, andesim stops it with `plan step 1: timed out after 90000 ms`; in that
case measure a smaller window (e.g. `--trigger icount` with small counts) or pick
a lighter core.'

=============== idx 39 ===============
'## 7. Developer commands (optional)

Set `ANDESIM_DEV=1` to reveal `build`, `test`, and `doctor` (section 1). They
build the artifacts, run the end-to-end suite, and check environment health -
useful when working on the repo, not when just running simulations. For most
build/test work the documented entry points are `bash scripts/build_driver.sh`,
`source ./setup.sh`, and `bash scripts/run_e2e.sh` (use `JOBS=8`).'

=============== idx 40 ===============
'## 8. Cheat sheet and where to go next

```sh
andesim list models                        # the 3 compositions
andesim list engines                        # the concrete simulators
andesim run --mode fast  ELF                            # QEMU only, functional
andesim run --mode fast  --gdb [--gdb-port PORT] ELF    # QEMU gdbstub (default port 1234)
andesim run --mode cycle --engine vsim:<cpu> ELF        # one vsim, from reset
andesim run --mode cycle --engine vsim:<cpu> --gdb ELF  # vsim JTAG + ICEman (requires $ICEMAN; default port 9104)
andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker    --engine vsim:<cpu> ELF
andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc     --engine vsim:<cpu> --pc-start S --pc-end E ELF
andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger icount --engine vsim:<cpu> --qemu-icount N --vsim-icount M ELF
andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker    --engine vsim:<cpu> --verify ELF   # + QEMU-oracle cross-check
andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker    --engine vsim:<cpu> --cosim ELF    # localize a divergence (dev)

# one vplat-built ELF runs on all three models (sections 2, 3, 4d):
andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:<cpu> \
  --pc-start say_hello --pc-end roi_end hello.elf
```

Next:

- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` - the full guide (build, configure, every mode).
- `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md` - one deep-dive exercise per trigger.
- `CLAUDE.md` - key files and the architecture summary.
- `runtime/` - the engine-portable runtime library; link it with
  `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs` (one build for fast / cycle /
  hybrid; sections 2-3).'

"The usual `window_cycles` figure as in 4a, plus the two verification
lines:
`[state-diff] PASS: 109 fields match` is the field-by-field compare,
`[verify] PASS` the verdict. The oracle's stderr banner shows the sample
point (`pc=...` - vsim's actual halt pc).

For regression testing, the whole e2e suite takes the same check with
`VERIFY=1 JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`. Details (and the failure
anatomy) in `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` section 4.7."

=============== idx 34 ===============
"### 4f. Localize a divergence with checkpoint co-sim (`--cosim`)

`--verify` (4e) tells you THAT the vsim leg diverged; `--cosim` tells you
roughly WHERE. It is a developer tool (hidden from the release help, like
`state-diff` - set `ANDESIM_DEV=1` to see it in `run --help`):

```
hybrid run:  QEMU1 -> vsim: ..N insns..|..N insns..|.. exit
                              ckpt 1      ckpt 2      final drain
oracle run:  pure QEMU, drains at the SAME retire counts
diff ckpt k vs ckpt k -> first mismatch = the bad N-instruction window
```

Every N retired instructions (default 10000, `--cosim-interval` overrides)
the vsim leg halts the hart over DMI, drains a full architectural
checkpoint, and resumes. The driver reads each checkpoint's
`minstret - entry.minstret` (the exact post-entry retire count), re-runs
the ELF on pure QEMU with the plugin draining at those same counts, and
diffs checkpoint against checkpoint with the `state-diff` policy. The two
runs never share memory: the oracle replays the same deterministic program
from boot on its own RAM, so the shared mmap needs no change."

=============== idx 37 ===============
'## 5. Picking an engine with `--engine`

`--engine <id>` selects which simulator to use. For `fast` it must be `qemu`
(the only functional engine). For `cycle` and `hybrid` it names one of the
`vsim:<cpu>` rows from `list engines`. Different CPU configs have different
microarchitectures and VLEN, so the same workload reports different cycles.

Try it yourself - rerun the marker example (section 4a) on a different core and
compare the number:

```sh
andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_mp2 \
  tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf
```

A heavier core simulates more slowly. If a leg exceeds the built-in 90 s per-leg
timeout, andesim stops it with `plan step 1: timed out after 90000 ms`; in that
case measure a smaller window (e.g. `--trigger icount` with small counts) or pick
a lighter core.'

=============== idx 39 ===============
'## 7. Developer commands (optional)

Set `ANDESIM_DEV=1` to reveal `build`, `test`, and `doctor` (section 1). They
build the artifacts, run the end-to-end suite, and check environment health -
useful when working on the repo, not when just running simulations. For most
build/test work the documented entry points are `bash scripts/build_driver.sh`,
`source ./setup.sh`, and `bash scripts/run_e2e.sh` (use `JOBS=8`).'

=============== idx 40 ===============
'## 8. Cheat sheet and where to go next

```sh
andesim list models                        # the 3 compositions
andesim list engines                        # the concrete simulators
andesim run --mode fast  ELF                            # QEMU only, functional
andesim run --mode fast  --gdb [--gdb-port PORT] ELF    # QEMU gdbstub (default port 1234)
andesim run --mode cycle --engine vsim:<cpu> ELF        # one vsim, from reset
andesim run --mode cycle --engine vsim:<cpu> --gdb ELF  # vsim JTAG + ICEman (requires $ICEMAN; default port 9104)
andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker    --engine vsim:<cpu> ELF
andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc     --engine vsim:<cpu> --pc-start S --pc-end E ELF
andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger icount --engine vsim:<cpu> --qemu-icount N --vsim-icount M ELF
andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker    --engine vsim:<cpu> --verify ELF   # + QEMU-oracle cross-check
andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker    --engine vsim:<cpu> --cosim ELF    # localize a divergence (dev)

# one vplat-built ELF runs on all three models (sections 2, 3, 4d):
andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:<cpu> \
  --pc-start say_hello --pc-end roi_end hello.elf
```

Next:

- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` - the full guide (build, configure, every mode).
- `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md` - one deep-dive exercise per trigger.
- `CLAUDE.md` - key files and the architecture summary.
- `runtime/` - the engine-portable runtime library; link it with
  `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs` (one build for fast / cycle /
  hybrid; sections 2-3).'

**Debugging tip — attach GDB to a running binary**

```sh
# fast model: starts QEMU's built-in GDB stub on port 1234 and pauses at startup.
andesim run --model fast --gdb /tmp/hello.elf
# Then in a second terminal: riscv64-unknown-elf-gdb /tmp/hello.elf
#   (gdb) target remote :1234
#   (gdb) continue

# cycle model: resets + halts the hart, opens vsim's JTAG port (9104), then runs
# $ICEMAN -- a GDB server. Use a modern OpenOCD (0.12+); Andes ICEman's bundled
# 0.10 has a remote_bitbang bug vs vsim. Connect GDB to the server's gdb port
# (OpenOCD default 1111). Full example: docs/andes_sim_demo.ipynb.
export ICEMAN=/path/to/openocd-jtag-server
andesim run --model cycle --gdb --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium /tmp/hello.elf

# Override the port for either model:
andesim run --model fast --gdb --gdb-port 2345 /tmp/hello.elf
```

`--gdb` is not available with `--model hybrid` (the two-leg pipeline cannot pause for a debugger).

   (`scripts/build_all.sh plugin`) and fixtures (`make -C tests/fixtures`) often
   are not -- a missing plugin makes every hybrid cell fail.

   `python3 -m nbconvert --to notebook --execute --inplace
    --ExecutePreprocessor.kernel_name=andesim-nb
    --ExecutePreprocessor.timeout=900 docs/<nb>.ipynb`

To regenerate the `docs/*.ipynb` tutorial outputs against the freshly-built
`andesim` (e.g. after a CLI change), the notebooks' declared `python3` kernel is
usually unregistered. Recipe that worked:

1. `python3 -m pip install ipykernel nbconvert matplotlib` (matplotlib only for

   are not -- a missing plugin makes every hybrid cell fail.
4. Execute from the repo root with PATH including `build/`:
   `python3 -m nbconvert --to notebook --execute --inplace
    --ExecutePreprocessor.kernel_name=andesim-nb
    --ExecutePreprocessor.timeout=900 docs/<nb>.ipynb`

Gotchas: `andes_sim_demo.ipynb` has gdb/ICEman `%%bash` cells that block headless
-- tag them `skip-execution` in cell `metadata.tags` (nbclient honors it) to keep
their human-generated outputs. The runtime tutorial wrote throwaway sources to

`/tmp/andesim_*`. See [[zsh-noclobber-overwrite]] for the `>|` shell gotcha.

name: zsh-noclobber-overwrite
description: "This zsh has noclobber set; `>` to an existing file fails, use `>|`"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: ae5483e5-a453-4fa7-9aee-2e7fac3a20e4

The interactive zsh in this environment has `noclobber` set. Redirecting with
`>` to a path that already exists fails with `zsh: file exists: <path>` and the
command does NOT run. Use `>|` to force-overwrite (e.g. `cmd >| /tmp/out.log`),
or `rm -f` the file first. This bit me repeatedly when reusing `/tmp/*.log` and
heredoc target files across Bash tool calls.

Also: `mapfile` / `readarray` are unavailable in this zsh, and `for x in $var`
does NOT word-split on newlines (use `while IFS= read -r x` to iterate lines).

skills.name: simplify
skills.content:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

1	// The phase-plan grammar driven by run_plan (F6) -- the C++ analog of
2	// orchestrator/plan.py's Session/Step model, minus the dropped QEMU2 step.
3	//
4	// A Plan is a list of Steps; each Step names an engine (by id, resolved against
5	// the F2 registry), the role to invoke it in (its `invoke` template key, e.g.
6	// "fast-leg" / "accurate-leg"), and a Trigger. run_plan spawns each leg in
7	// order, threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward, and returns each
8	// leg's mcycle/minstret. Under the no-QEMU2-handback design every F6 step
9	// drains, so the hybrid cycle figure is the vsim-leg mcycle minus the qemu-leg
10	// mcycle.
11	#ifndef ANDESIM_PLAN_HPP
12	#define ANDESIM_PLAN_HPP
13	
14	#include <map>
15	#include <string>
16	#include <vector>
17	
18	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
19	
20	namespace andes_sim {
21	
22	// The ROI delimiter for a step. `kind` is marker|pc|icount|simpoint; `params`
23	// carries kind-specific values (e.g. icount=N, enter_pc, exit_pc) that F9 maps
24	// onto trigger args. F6 only exercises the default marker case (no params).
25	struct Trigger {
26	  std::string kind;
27	  std::map<std::string, std::string> params;
28	};
29	
30	// One leg of a plan: which engine, which invoke role, under which trigger.
31	// `extra_args` are verbatim tokens appended after the filled template and the
32	// trigger args -- the seam for user-forwarded per-leg flags (e.g. the vsim
33	// leg's --vsim-warmup-icount / --kanata), which are orthogonal to the trigger.
34	struct Step {
35	  std::string engine_id;  // "qemu" | "verilator:ax45mpv_premium"
36	  std::string role;       // invoke-template key: "fast-leg" | "accurate-leg"
37	  Trigger trigger;
38	  std::vector<std::string> extra_args{};  // default-init: keeps 3-field Step{} literals warning-free
39	};
40	
41	// A whole hybrid run. Every step loads `elf`; the shared mmap (`mem_size`
42	// bytes, at `mmap_path` or allocated by run_plan when empty) survives across
43	// every leg so memory threads through.
44	struct Plan {
45	  std::string elf;          // path to the ELF every leg launches
46	  long long mem_size = 0;   // shared-mmap size in bytes
47	  std::string mmap_path;    // "" => run_plan allocates one (F5) and owns it
48	  std::vector<Step> steps;
49	};
50	
51	// What one drain step measured (read back from its state file), plus the
52	// leg's captured stdout -- the guest program's own output (UART/semihosting)
53	// rides the engine's stdout and must flow through to the user. `st` is the
54	// full drained record (verify_oracle F4: run --verify diffs the vsim drain
55	// against the oracle leg's in-process, after run_plan removed the files).
56	struct PhaseResult {
57	  unsigned long long mcycle = 0;
58	  unsigned long long minstret = 0;
59	  std::string out;
60	  hybrid_state_v1 st{};
61	  // cosim_roi F4: in-ROI checkpoint drains (`<state_out>.ckpt<k>`, k from 1),
62	  // read back in order before run_plan removes the workdir. Empty unless the
63	  // leg ran with checkpointing enabled.
64	  std::vector<hybrid_state_v1> checkpoints{};
65	};
66	
67	// Aggregate outcome. `error` empty => every step matched its expected exit and
68	// drained a valid state file; `phases` then holds one entry per step in order.
69	struct PlanResult {
70	  std::string error;
71	  std::vector<PhaseResult> phases;
72	  bool ok() const { return error.empty(); }
73	};
74	
75	}  // namespace andes_sim
76	
77	#endif  // ANDESIM_PLAN_HPP

1	// The phase-plan executor (F6) -- the C++ analog of runner.run_session, minus
2	// the dropped QEMU2 handback. run_plan spawns each leg of a Plan in order,
3	// threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward (leg N's --handoff-out is
4	// leg N+1's --resume-from-qemu), and reports each leg's mcycle/minstret.
5	//
6	// plan_argvs is the pure core (no spawn, no mmap): it resolves each Step's
7	// engine + role against the registry and fills the invoke template with the
8	// threaded state paths, so the argv construction is unit-testable in isolation.
9	#ifndef ANDESIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
10	#define ANDESIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
11	
12	#include <string>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	#include "engine_descriptor.hpp"
16	#include "plan.hpp"
17	
18	namespace andes_sim {
19	
20	// The framework-owned values shared by every leg of a run: the resolved
21	// shared-mmap path/size/base and the QEMU plugin path. Per-leg values
22	// (bin/state_in/state_out) are derived by plan_argvs from this + the threading.
23	struct RuntimeCtx {
24	  std::string mmap_path;
25	  long long mem_size = 0;
26	  std::string mmap_base = "0x0";
27	  std::string plugin_path;
28	};
29	
30	// hw-config sync: the QEMU fast leg models the hardware the accurate-leg
31	// engine measures, so its -cpu vlen follows that engine's descriptor. 512 is
32	// the fallback for engines that report none. One definition, used by both the
33	// plan executor ({vlen} fill) and the hybrid banner.
34	inline long synced_vlen(long engine_vlen) {
35	  return engine_vlen > 0 ? engine_vlen : 512;
36	}
37	
38	// A trigger's per-leg argv contribution, dispatched by the leg's role. The
39	// QEMU plugin takes its trigger as a comma-suffix folded INTO the one `-plugin`
40	// token (so it rides the `{trigger}` placeholder); vsim takes separate tokens
41	// appended to its argv. marker contributes nothing (plugin/vsim detect the markers
42	// themselves).
43	struct LegTriggerArgs {
44	  std::string plugin_suffix;        // qemu fast-leg: appended to {trigger}
45	  std::vector<std::string> extra;   // vsim accurate-leg: appended tokens
46	};
47	
48	// Map `t` onto `role`'s argv contribution. marker -> empty. pc -> qemu
49	// `,enter_pc=<enter_pc>` / vsim `--hybrid-exit-pc <exit_pc>`. icount -> qemu
50	// `,icount=<qemu_icount>` / vsim `--hybrid-icount <vsim_icount>`. Roles other
51	// than fast-leg/accurate-leg get nothing. A missing required param or an
52	// unknown trigger kind sets `err` (and returns an empty contribution).
53	//
54	// NOTE (altitude debt): these flag spellings are framework-side per-engine
55	// knowledge -- the one place F9 hardcodes a fast/accurate engine's CLI, unlike
56	// the base argv which comes from each engine's `--describe` invoke template.
57	// This is a deliberate scope cut: the principled form (per-(trigger,role) argv
58	// templates carried in `--describe`, filled by build_argv like `invoke`) would
59	// extend the F2 engine contract and is left for a later feature.
60	LegTriggerArgs leg_trigger_args(const Trigger& t, const std::string& role,
61	                                std::string& err);
62	
63	// Build every step's concrete argv, threading state files under `workdir`:
64	//   state_in[0]  = ""                       (cold start; no resume)
65	//   state_in[i]  = state_out[i-1]           (prior leg's drain)
66	//   state_out[i] = workdir/"state-<i>.bin"  (this leg's drain)
67	// Each step's engine is looked up in `engines` by id and its `role` template is
68	// filled via build_argv. Pure (no spawn). Returns one argv per step; on any
69	// error (unknown engine/role, unresolved placeholder) returns {} and sets `err`.
70	std::vector<std::vector<std::string>> plan_argvs(
71	    const Plan& plan, const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
72	    const std::string& workdir, const RuntimeCtx& ctx, std::string& err);
73	
74	struct PlanOptions {
75	  int timeout_ms = 90000;     // per-leg spawn timeout
76	  int expect_rc = 200;        // drain success code (kExitHandoffToQemu)
77	  std::string plugin_path;    // "" => $VSIM_PLUGIN else repo default
78	};
79	
80	// Execute `plan`: resolve the plugin, acquire the shared mmap (allocate one
81	// under /dev/shm when plan.mmap_path is empty, and own it), spawn each leg with
82	// a timeout, require exit == expect_rc, and read back each leg's mcycle/minstret
83	// from its drained state file. Returns the per-leg results; on the first failure
84	// `error` describes it and `phases` holds whatever completed before it.
85	PlanResult run_plan(const Plan& plan,
86	                    const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
87	                    const PlanOptions& opts = {});
88	
89	}  // namespace andes_sim
90	
91	#endif  // ANDESIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP

=== release-surface contract (current assertions) ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-surface contract: the andesim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
# user-facing commands (run, list, doctor) and never the third-party simulator
# name "verilator". The former developer commands build/test/state-diff have
# moved OUT of the binary (build -> scripts/build_all.sh, test ->
# scripts/test_all.sh, state-diff -> the diff_states core behind `run --verify`):
# they are not listed in any help and are not dispatchable. The unfinished
# ROADMAP commands (profile, cluster, archive, replay, estimate) appear in no
# help at all. The cycle-accurate engine is presented as "vsim" everywhere --
# proven end to end with a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator" and
# must come back out as vsim:.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)

# ROADMAP: Andes HybridSim v1.0 (complete-all-features)

Single source of truth for everything required to ship Andes HybridSim
v1.0. Every feature traces to a functional requirement in `docs/FRS.md`,
which in turn traces to a market requirement in `docs/MRD.md`. Covering
all FRs therefore covers all MRs (FRS section 13 has no orphan).

This file **supersedes** two earlier engineering breakdowns, now in
`docs/archive/`:

- `docs/archive/commercial_v1_roadmap.md` - Waves 0-6 closing L1-L21
- `docs/archive/TODO.md` - failure-mode backlog F-T1.1..F-T3.8

Their content is absorbed below as full feature entries. `docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb`
stays as the plain-English "do not do this" envelope and the L-id source.

House rules (from `CLAUDE.md`): one session completes one feature. Update
the feature's Status when starting (in-progress) and on completion (done).
Each code feature carries a TDD RED line: the failing test you write first.

## Status legend

- not-started: no work yet
- in-progress: being implemented in a session
- partial: shipped for the M-mode envelope, incomplete for the full FR
- done: behavioural + structural commits landed, tests pass
- business: not a code task; a sign-off / process / legal deliverable

## Feature ID scheme

- `F-ENG-*` - engineering: ROI-envelope and correctness of the cycle engine
- `F-PROD-*` - productization: interfaces, trace, observability, encryption,
  licensing, packaging
- `F-BIZ-*` - business / legal / process: tagged `business`, no TDD RED

## Track and wave ordering (dependency DAG)

```

        (E01..E04)      |        P-b trace export (needs E18)    legal,

           v            |        P-d ENCRYPTION  *ship gate*     parallel,
Wave 1  wire v2 (E05) --+----->  P-e licensing (needs P-d)       no code
           |                     P-f packaging (needs all)       dep
     +-----+-----+
     v           v
Wave 2 envelope  Wave 3 Andes
(E06..E11)       parity (E12,E13)
     |           |
     +-----+-----+
           v
Wave 4 scale (E14..E17)

           v

           |
           v
Wave 6 portability (deferred, see Out of scope)
```

Hard dependencies:

- **F-ENG-05 (wire format v2)** gates Waves 2-4: every new state block
  (trap, S-mode, Andes, per-hart) needs feature-bitted fields.
- **F-PROD-12 (encryption)** is the commercial ship gate (MR-D). Nothing
  goes to a paying customer without it. It is also the longest pole
  (24-48 weeks, possibly an external partner - see MRD open questions).
- **P-e licensing** assumes the encrypted binary exists (P-d) to bind to.
- **P-f packaging** closes last; it bundles every shipped component.

Tracks E, P, and B run in parallel across sessions. Within Track E the
waves are sequential after Wave 1.

---

## Baseline: already shipped

These FRs are closed by the gem5-parity core roadmap (CSR / PC / icount /
SimPoint switching + warmup window) and `docs/archive/driver_ROADMAP.md`
(the `./hsim` driver F1-F14). They are the starting line, not open work.

- FR-101 handoff (`./hsim run`, M-mode envelope; 2-phase since the QEMU2 leg was removed).
- FR-102/103/104/105 all four trigger modes.
- FR-106 state transport for the M-mode subset (FR-107 handback removed): 32 GPRs,
  32 FPRs, V-state, and 4 restored CSRs (mstatus, mtvec, mcycle, minstret).
- FR-108 M-mode workloads (asm + C-runtime fixtures).
- FR-114 checkpoint / replay (`./hsim archive` + `./hsim replay`).
- FR-205 iterative re-measure (replay a checkpoint against a rebuilt vsim).
- FR-301 (partial) subcommands present: list, build, run, test, doctor,
  profile, cluster, archive, replay, estimate.

"partial" elsewhere means the M-mode happy path works but the full FR
acceptance (S/U-mode, full CSR set, JSON, RTL-correlated accuracy) is open.

---

# Track E - Engineering

> NOTE 2026-06-09: the vsim -> QEMU2 handback was removed repo-wide. Any F-ENG item below that proposes work on the QEMU2 leg, `qemu_handback`, the orchestrator's `gdbstub.py` / `qemu-resume`, a post-handback readback, or a QEMU2 watchdog is OBSOLETE -- the simulator is now 2-phase (QEMU1 drain -> vsim drain). The vsim-side items remain valid.

## Wave 0 - Truth in advertising

Goal: stop silent wrongness before fixing big things. Highest ROI per
week. (Absorbs commercial_v1_roadmap Wave 0; L11/L15/L16/L20.)

### F-ENG-01 - Value-level handoff checker

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-106, FR-K(601), MR-A, MR-I
- L-id: L15 (F-T3.1)
- Description: [OBSOLETE 2026-06-09: the QEMU2 handback and
  `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py` were removed, so there is no post-handback
  readback to add; the drain itself is now the only state sink.] The icount
  and simpoint paths assert only exit code and PC range; a wrong register
  value passes silently. Add a post-handback `g`-packet read in the
  orchestrator and compare it field-by-field against the drained
  `hybrid_state_v1`. Wire it as a CI gate.
- Key files: `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py` (post-handback readback),
  `tests/hsim/test_handoff_value_check.sh` (new)
- Dependencies: none
- TDD RED: a fixture mutates a GPR mid-ROI; the checker fails when the
  drained struct disagrees with the QEMU2 post-handback readback. Today
  nothing compares them.

### F-ENG-02 - Fail-loud on missing CSR name

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-106, FR-305 (exit 4), MR-K
- L-id: L16
- Description: GPR/PC writes hard-fail when the stub omits the name, but
  every CSR/PMP/V write goes through `_try_write_u64`, which returns
  quietly on a missing feature-XML name. The asymmetry is the hazard.
  Make a missing CSR name raise the same way a missing GPR does, mapped
  to exit code 4 (state-transport corruption).
- Key files: `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py:251-258` (`_try_write_u64`
  returns status), `apply_state` (caller asserts)
- Dependencies: none
- TDD RED: a mock stub that drops `mtvec`; the orchestrator must raise,
  not skip.

### F-ENG-03 - VLEN runtime check

- Status: mostly superseded by L11 (2026-06-12); residual below
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-106, MR-A, MR-I
- L-id: L11 (F-T3.4)
- Description: L11 closed the main hazards: the wire format now carries
  VLEN up to 1024 (`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=128`, state version 2), the
  plugin ABORTS on an over-ceiling vlenb instead of clamping
  (`hybrid_v_drain_policy`), vsim's `load_state` rejects an over-ceiling
  file, and inside `andesim run` the two legs cannot disagree because
  the fast leg's `-cpu vlen=` is copied from the engine descriptor.
  `LIVE_VLEN_BYTES=64` in `checkpoint.py` is NOT the wire ceiling: it is
  the live engine's vlenb used by the replay-archive validator, so it
  stays 64 for the VLEN-512 build.
- Residual: hand-driven legs (raw QEMU + raw vsim, both under the ceiling
  but different from each other, e.g. 1024 vs 512) are still only caught
  by the fixture's own self-check, not by a vsim-side compare of the
  live hart `vlenb` against `state.vlenb` at resume.
- Key files: `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` (read live vlenb,
  compare against `state.vlenb`)
- Dependencies: none
- TDD RED: a vlenb=128 state file against a VLEN-512 sim aborts at resume
  instead of silently corrupting the V regfile.

### F-ENG-04 - fcsr / frm / fflags round-trip

- Status: DONE (2026-06-12)
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-106, FR-202, MR-A
- L-id: L20 (F-T1.2)
- Description: `fcsr` (packs `frm[7:5]` + `fflags[4:0]`) was in no
  transport surface. Now: `uint64_t fcsr` carved from `reserved[]`,
  drained alongside the FPRs, restored after `mstatus.FS` is enabled,
  re-read at vsim exit, and compared by `--verify`/`state-diff`. Gated
  on `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`; old state files read back 0 (= the previous
  reset-value behavior), so no version bump.
- Key files: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` + `state_abi_check.h` (field +
  offset lock), `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (handle + drain),
  `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` (restore),
  `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp` (drain),
  `driver/state_diff.cpp` (oracle compare). (The planned
  `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py` handback work died with the QEMU2 leg.)
- Tests: `tests/fixtures/rt_c_fcsr.c` (frm=RTZ + sticky NX before the
  enter marker, in-ROI self-check, sentinel 0x45 at the exit drain) via
  `tests/hybrid/e2e_fcsr_roundtrip.sh` + the marker/pc e2e suite; unit
  coverage in `state_abi.test.cpp`, `resume_driver.test.cpp`,
  `state_drain.test.cpp`, `driver/state_diff_test.cpp`.

## Wave 1 - Wire format v2

Goal: structural foundation. v1 has ~216 reserved bytes and no growth
path; every Wave 2-3 fix needs feature-bitted fields. (Absorbs
commercial_v1_roadmap Wave 1.)

### F-ENG-05 - hybrid_state_v2 with feature bits

- Status: not-started
- Type: structural
- Traces: FR-106, FR-801 (ABI versioning), MR-A, MR-E, MR-I
- L-id: structural foundation (andes_sim_limitations.ipynb "transport ceiling")
- Description: New `include/hybrid/state_abi_v2.h`. Magic + version + size
  header; reader rejects unknown version. Feature bits extend the three
  existing (`RV64/FP/V`) with `PRIV`, `TRAP_CSR`, `S_MODE_CSR`,
  `ANDES_CSR`. Base block: GPRs, FPRs, fcsr, M-mode CSRs, PC, priv. Trap
  block: mepc, mcause, mtval, dpc. S-mode block (behind bit): stvec, sepc,
  scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip, scounteren, senvcfg, satp. V block
  unchanged. Keep a v1 reader (zero-extend) for one release; drop the v1
  writer after one release. Update all 4 transports (plugin drain, vsim
  resume, vsim drain, orchestrator parse). Mirror in `abi.py`.
- Key files: `include/hybrid/state_abi_v2.h` (new),
  `include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h`, `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`,
  `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`,
  `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`,
  `tools/orchestrator/abi.py`, `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py`,
  `tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp`, `docs/wire_format_v2.md` (new)
- Dependencies: F-ENG-04 (fcsr lands in the v2 base block)
- TDD RED: `state_abi.test.cpp` asserts the v2 magic/version header and a
  feature-bit gate (e.g. S-mode block absent when `S_MODE_CSR` clear); a
  v1 blob still reads via the shim. An ABI-hash check fails CI on an
  unreviewed layout change.

## Wave 2 - ROI envelope expansion

Goal: real OS-bearing workloads run inside vsim. Removes the "M-mode only,
trap-free, PMP-static, no syscalls" core rule. (Absorbs commercial_v1
Wave 2; L1-L6.)

### F-ENG-06 - Paging (satp) restore + TLB flush

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-109, MR-B
- L-id: L3
- Description: `satp` is drained but never written into vsim, so the ROI
  runs bare-mode and every virtual address hits wrong memory. Restore
  `satp` on resume, then `sfence.vma` via the Program Buffer to flush
  stale TLB.
- Key files: `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`
- Dependencies: F-ENG-05
- TDD RED: a fixture with `satp != 0` runs a Sv39-mapped load inside the
  ROI and reads the correct mapped value.

### F-ENG-07 - Trap / exception state round-trip

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-109, MR-B
- L-id: L4 (F-T1.4)
- Description: `mcause`, `mtval`, `mepc` are not re-read at drain (stale
  QEMU1 values pass through) and trap-delegation CSRs are not restored, so
  a trap inside the ROI starts from reset. Restore the trap block on
  entry; re-read it at drain.
- Key files: `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp` (re-read
  mcause/mtval/mepc), `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` (restore)
- Dependencies: F-ENG-05
- TDD RED: a fixture that triggers an illegal-instruction trap inside the
  ROI; the trap handler runs to completion under vsim.

### F-ENG-08 - Privilege restore (S/U-mode)

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-109, MR-B
- L-id: L6 (F-T2.1)
- Description: Both sides hardcode `priv=3`. vsim never writes `dcsr.prv`
  (so `dret` always resumes M-mode); `apply_state` never writes `priv`.
  Stop hardcoding; write `dcsr.prv` so `dret` resumes in the drained mode;
  add `priv` to the handback.
- Key files: `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp:51`,
  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:264`,
  `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` (dcsr.prv),
  `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py` (apply_state priv)
- Dependencies: F-ENG-05
- TDD RED: a fixture that triggers from S-mode and resumes to S-mode.

### F-ENG-09 - PMP restore into vsim

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-106, FR-109, MR-A
- L-id: L2 (F-T1.3)
- Description: All 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr` are drained but none are
  written into vsim, so the ROI runs with zeroed PMP and any protection
  silently disappears. Write all PMP via abstract command; respect
  locked-bit semantics.
- Key files: `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`
- Dependencies: F-ENG-05
- TDD RED: a fixture with a write-protect PMP region; a write inside the
  ROI traps.

### F-ENG-10 - LR/SC reservation policy

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-106, MR-A
- L-id: L5 (F-T1.5)
- Description: A reservation held across the trigger never round-trips, so
  the `sc` always fails and a CAS loop spins forever. v1.0: the plugin
  REJECTS the handoff with a clear error if a reservation is pending at
  the trigger (no silent miscompare). Carrying the reservation in the wire
  format is deferred post-v1.
- Key files: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (reservation check),
  `include/hybrid/state_abi_v2.h` (reservation field behind a feature bit,
  post-v1)
- Dependencies: F-ENG-05
- TDD RED: a fixture with `lr` before and `sc` after the trigger; the
  plugin aborts at the trigger with a clear message, not a spin.

### F-ENG-11 - Syscalls / semihosting inside ROI

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-109, MR-B
- L-id: L1 (F-T1.1) - the blocker
- Description: libgloss inside the ROI emits the semihosting magic triple;
  vsim has no handler, so the ebreak trap-loops to timeout. Policy
  (decide before implementation): (a) passthrough - vsim catches the
  semihosting ebreak and proxies to a host syscall trampoline (heavy,

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F9 contract: `run --mode hybrid` -- orchestrate a QEMU1 -> vsim handoff (no
# QEMU2) and print the one-line window-cycle figure for the marker | pc
# triggers. Three layers:
#
#   1. unit (fast, no spawn): the elf-syms boundary resolver, hybrid_trigger
#      (CLI -> Trigger, incl. pc symbol resolution), the trigger->argv mapping
#      (plan-test), and the new CLI flags (cli-test).
#   2. validation error paths via the real binary, all exiting BEFORE any spawn:
#      missing ELF, pc without boundaries, an undefined pc symbol, simpoint
#      (F11, not yet), and an unknown trigger.
#   3. real handoff + golden parity (guarded): run marker/pc through both
#      ./hsim.py (the Python golden) and andesim and assert identical window
#      cycle numbers, plus the new output format. Skipped when the qemu/vsim/
#      plugin artifacts or the golden driver are not built.
#
# pc uses handoff_roundtrip.elf's own markers as the boundaries (_start =
# the enter marker 0x100000, 0x10000c = the exit marker), so pc reproduces marker's
# switch points exactly -- and exercises BOTH symbol and 0x resolution.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"  # asm fixture
CELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_matmul.elf"       # C fixture (needs shared mmap)
ENG=vsim:ax45mpv_premium  # the engine ./hsim.py resolves by default

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit tests (the F9 pure cores)
for t in elf-syms hybrid plan cli; do
  "$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-$t-test" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || fail "unit test andesim-$t-test failed"
done
echo "[ok] unit: elf-syms, hybrid_trigger, trigger->argv (plan), CLI flags"

# 2. validation error paths -- real binary, but every case errors before a spawn
# (expect: assert rc + output regex; shared helper from tests/lib/log.sh)
expect 2 'ELF not found'        "$BIN" run --mode hybrid /no/such.elf
expect 2 'engine args go after' "$BIN" run --mode hybrid a.elf b.elf
expect 2 'requires --pc-start'  "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger pc "$ELF"
expect 2 'not defined' "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger pc \
  --pc-start nope_xyz --pc-end _start "$ELF"
expect 2 'F11'              "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger simpoint "$ELF"
expect 2 'unknown trigger'  "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger bogus "$ELF"
expect 2 'requires --kanata' "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
  --objdump /tmp/o "$ELF"
echo "[ok] validation: missing ELF, pc boundaries, bad symbol, simpoint/unknown trigger, kanata/objdump"

# 3. real handoff + golden parity (guarded on built artifacts)
QEMU="$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64"
SIM="$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
PLUGIN="$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so"
if [ -x "$QEMU" ] && [ -x "$SIM" ] && [ -f "$PLUGIN" ] && [ -x "$ROOT/hsim.py" ]; then
  # Pull the window/kernel cycle integer from either driver's "] N  (vsim..."
  # line (golden marker/pc say "kernel_cycles", andes says "window_cycles";
  # the number's position is identical).
  cyc() { grep -oE '\] [0-9]+  \(' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | head -1; }
  check_parity() {  # LABEL GOLDEN_NUM ANDES_NUM
    [ -n "$2" ] || fail "$1: golden produced no cycle number"
    [ -n "$3" ] || fail "$1: andesim produced no cycle number"
    [ "$2" = "$3" ] || fail "$1: cycle mismatch golden=$2 andes=$3"
    echo "[ok] $1 parity: $3 cycles (golden == andesim)"
  }

  # marker -- also assert the new output format (window_cycles + PASS line)
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim.py run --mode marker "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" "$ELF" 2>&1)
  printf '%s\n' "$AO" | grep -Eq '^\[marker window_cycles\] [0-9]+  \(vsim mcycle=' \
    || fail "marker: missing window_cycles line: $AO"
  printf '%s\n' "$AO" | grep -Eq '^PASS: --mode hybrid --trigger marker ' \
    || fail "marker: missing PASS line: $AO"
  check_parity marker "$GO" "$(printf '%s\n' "$AO" | cyc)"

  # marker on a C fixture -- the stack/heap + main()'s frame must survive the
  # handoff through the shared mmap (asm fixtures are self-contained; this is
  # the "+ C fixtures" half of the done-when).
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim.py run --mode marker "$CELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" "$CELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  check_parity marker-c "$GO" "$AO"

  # pc -- symbol start (_start) + 0x end (the exit marker)
  GO=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 180 ./hsim.py run --mode pc \
        --pc-start _start --pc-end 0x10000c "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  AO=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENG" \
        --pc-start _start --pc-end 0x10000c "$ELF" 2>&1 | cyc)
  check_parity pc "$GO" "$AO"

  # kanata ROI trace forwards onto the vsim leg and writes a non-empty file.
  KAN=$(mktemp); rm -f "$KAN"
  timeout 180 "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" \
    --kanata "$KAN" "$ELF" >/dev/null 2>&1
  [ -s "$KAN" ] || fail "kanata: trace file empty/missing after marker run"
  echo "[ok] kanata: marker run wrote a non-empty ROI trace ($(wc -l <"$KAN") lines)"
  rm -f "$KAN"
else
  echo "[skip] real handoff parity: need built qemu+vsim+plugin and ./hsim"
fi

ok "F9 run --mode hybrid (marker|pc)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F7 contract: `run --mode fast` -- QEMU-only, transparent passthrough.
# Three layers:
#
#   1. run-test (unit, fast): passthrough_argv fills the qemu `standalone`
#      invoke template ({bin}/{elf}) and appends the post-`--` engine args
#      verbatim -- including a `-gdb tcp::N -S` gdbstub. Pure, no spawn.
#   2. CLI error paths (no engine needed): missing --mode, unknown model,
#      missing ELF, an extra positional, and engine!=qemu each exit 2 with a
#      clear message.
#   3. real passthrough (needs built qemu + a fixture): launch
#      `run --mode fast ELF -- -gdb tcp::PORT -S`; the gdbstub port opens and
#      qemu halts at reset -- the done-when "port opens, halts, debugger
#      connects". exec_passthrough's exit-code propagation is already covered
#      by the F5 infra test (and observed here only indirectly).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
RUNTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-run-test"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit: the argv-assembly contract carries the passthrough behavior
[ -x "$RUNTEST" ] || fail "missing unit-test binary: $RUNTEST"
"$RUNTEST" || fail "run unit tests (passthrough_argv) failed"

# assert `$BIN run ...` exits with $1 and its combined output matches regex $2
expect_rc_match() {
  local want_rc="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want_rc" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want_rc for [$*]: $out"
  echo "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "output missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# 2. CLI error paths (deterministic; no qemu)
expect_rc_match 2 'mode .* is required'      "$BIN" run
expect_rc_match 2 "unknown model 'bogus'"    "$BIN" run --mode bogus p.elf
expect_rc_match 2 'missing ELF'              "$BIN" run --mode fast
expect_rc_match 2 'engine args go after --'  "$BIN" run --mode fast a.elf b.elf
expect_rc_match 2 "engine must be 'qemu'"    "$BIN" run --mode fast --engine vsim:x p.elf

# 3. real passthrough: a frozen-at-reset gdbstub port opens (guarded on artifacts)
QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"
if [ -x "$QEMU" ] && [ -f "$ELF" ]; then
  PORT=$(( 40000 + (RANDOM % 20000) ))
  BG=""
  cleanup() { [ -n "${BG:-}" ] && kill "$BG" 2>/dev/null; pkill -f "tcp::$PORT" 2>/dev/null; true; }
  trap cleanup EXIT
  # -S halts the cpu at reset, so the stub listens regardless of the ELF body.
  "$BIN" run --mode fast "$ELF" -- -gdb "tcp::$PORT" -S </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
  BG=$!
  opened=0
  for _ in $(seq 1 40); do
    if timeout 1 bash -c ">/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/$PORT" 2>/dev/null; then opened=1; break; fi
    sleep 0.25
  done
  cleanup; trap - EXIT; wait "$BG" 2>/dev/null
  [ "$opened" -eq 1 ] || fail "fast passthrough: gdbstub port $PORT never opened"
  echo "[ok] real fast passthrough: qemu gdbstub halted + listening on :$PORT"
else
  echo "[skip] real fast run: qemu and/or fixture not built ($QEMU / $ELF)"
fi

# F9 contract: `run --mode hybrid` -- orchestrate a QEMU1 -> vsim handoff (no
# QEMU2) and print the one-line window-cycle figure for the marker | pc
# triggers. Three layers:
#
#   1. unit (fast, no spawn): the elf-syms boundary resolver, hybrid_trigger
#      (CLI -> Trigger, incl. pc symbol resolution), the trigger->argv mapping
#      (plan-test), and the new CLI flags (cli-test).
#   2. validation error paths via the real binary, all exiting BEFORE any spawn:
#      missing ELF, pc without boundaries, an undefined pc symbol, simpoint
#      (F11, not yet), and an unknown trigger.
#   3. real handoff + golden parity (guarded): run marker/pc through both
#      ./hsim.py (the Python golden) and andesim and assert identical window
#      cycle numbers, plus the new output format. Skipped when the qemu/vsim/
#      plugin artifacts or the golden driver are not built.
#
# pc uses handoff_roundtrip.elf's own markers as the boundaries (_start =
# the enter marker 0x100000, 0x10000c = the exit marker), so pc reproduces marker's
# switch points exactly -- and exercises BOTH symbol and 0x resolution.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit tests (the F9 pure cores)
for t in elf-syms hybrid plan cli; do
  "$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-$t-test" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || fail "unit test andesim-$t-test failed"
done
echo "[ok] unit: elf-syms, hybrid_trigger, trigger->argv (plan), CLI flags"

# 2. validation error paths -- real binary, but every case errors before a spawn
# (expect: assert rc + output regex; shared helper from tests/lib/log.sh)
expect 2 'ELF not found'        "$BIN" run --mode hybrid /no/such.elf
expect 2 'engine args go after' "$BIN" run --mode hybrid a.elf b.elf
expect 2 'is required for --mode hybrid' "$BIN" run --mode hybrid "$ELF"

  echo "[ok] kanata: marker run wrote a non-empty ROI trace ($(wc -l <"$KAN") lines)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-surface contract: the andesim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
# user-facing commands (run, list, doctor) and never the third-party simulator
# name "verilator". The former developer commands build/test/state-diff have
# moved OUT of the binary (build -> scripts/build_all.sh, test ->
# scripts/test_all.sh, state-diff -> the diff_states core behind `run --verify`):
# they are not listed in any help and are not dispatchable. The unfinished
# ROADMAP commands (profile, cluster, archive, replay, estimate) appear in no
# help at all. The cycle-accurate engine is presented as "vsim" everywhere --
# proven end to end with a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator" and
# must come back out as vsim:.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }

# 1. release --help: run + list + doctor only. No developer-commands section
# (build/test/state-diff moved to scripts/), and no "verilator".
H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
has '^  run '    "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'run'"
has '^  list '   "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'list'"
has '^  doctor ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'doctor'"
for c in build test state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
done
no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'developer command' "$H" && fail "release --help: developer commands moved to scripts/; drop the section:"$'\n'"$H"
ok "release --help: run/list/doctor only, no developer-commands section, no verilator"

# 2. The developer commands left the binary entirely: ANDESIM_DEV=1 --help adds
# NO commands (run/list/doctor only), and build/test/state-diff are no longer
# dispatchable (unknown command, rc 2).
D=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
for c in run list doctor; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing release command '$c'"
done
for c in build test state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" && fail "dev --help: leaked removed/hidden command '$c'"
done
no_word "$D" || fail "dev --help: leaked 'verilator'"
for c in build test state-diff; do
  expect 2 "unknown command '$c'" "$BIN" "$c"
done
ok "dev --help: no developer commands; build/test/state-diff gone (rc 2)"

# 3. run --help: the --engine example reads vsim:, never verilator:; the
# --trigger menu offers only the supported triggers (marker|pc -- icount was
# removed, simpoint is unfinished).
RH=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
has 'vsim:' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing vsim: example"
no_word "$RH" || fail "run --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'simpoint' "$RH" && fail "run --help: leaked unfinished trigger 'simpoint':"$'\n'"$RH"
has 'trigger.*icount' "$RH" && fail "run --help: --trigger should not list removed 'icount':"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mem-size' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --mem-size:"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mmap-size' "$RH" && fail "run --help: retired --mmap-size alias should stay hidden:"$'\n'"$RH"
# Interactive-debug + oracle knobs are user-facing: documented in the release help.
has '^  --verify '   "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --verify:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb '      "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb-port ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb-port:"$'\n'"$RH"
ok "run --help: vsim: example, no verilator/simpoint, --mem-size/--verify/--gdb documented"

# 4. list models: composition cells read vsim (never verilator), and NOTES show
# user-facing model traits only -- no implementation detail, no unfinished trigger.
LM=$("$BIN" list models 2>&1)
has 'vsim' "$LM" || fail "list models: missing vsim"
no_word "$LM" || fail "list models: leaked 'verilator'"
for d in 'transparent passthrough' 'pure from reset' 'simpoint' 'icount'; do
  has "$d" "$LM" && fail "list models: leaked implementation detail/removed-or-unfinished trigger '$d':"$'\n'"$LM"
done
ok "list models: vsim, no verilator, no implementation detail, no simpoint/icount"

# 5. list engines end to end: a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator"
# must surface as vsim: (the single normalization point), proving --engine /
# errors / list all speak the product name with no real sim_* needed.
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat >"$TMP/sim_fake" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"verilator:fakecfg","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc","icount"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
EOF
chmod +x "$TMP/sim_fake"
LE=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" list engines 2>&1)
has 'vsim:fakecfg' "$LE" || fail "list engines: fake not renamed to vsim:fakecfg:"$'\n'"$LE"
no_word "$LE" || fail "list engines: leaked 'verilator':"$'\n'"$LE"
# Triggers are a hybrid-MODEL option, not an engine attribute: `list engines`
# carries no TRIGGERS column (and so never leaks the unfinished simpoint trigger
# that the built-in qemu row used to advertise).
has 'TRIGGERS' "$LE" && fail "list engines: TRIGGERS is a hybrid-model option, not an engine column:"$'\n'"$LE"
has 'simpoint'  "$LE" && fail "list engines: leaked unfinished trigger 'simpoint':"$'\n'"$LE"
ok "list engines: a verilator-self-describing engine is shown as vsim:, no TRIGGERS column"

# 6. `list fixtures` is a developer target (internal test ELFs, not user
# workloads): release hides it; ANDESIM_DEV reveals it.
printf '%s\n' "$H" | grep -qw fixtures && fail "release --help: leaked 'fixtures' target"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-surface contract: the andesim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
# user-facing commands (run, list, doctor) and never the third-party simulator
# name "verilator". The former developer commands build/test/state-diff have
# moved OUT of the binary (build -> scripts/build_all.sh, test ->
# scripts/test_all.sh, state-diff -> the diff_states core behind `run --verify`):
# they are not listed in any help and are not dispatchable. The unfinished
# ROADMAP commands (profile, cluster, archive, replay, estimate) appear in no
# help at all. The cycle-accurate engine is presented as "vsim" everywhere --
# proven end to end with a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator" and
# must come back out as vsim:.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }

# 1. release --help: run + list + doctor only. No developer-commands section
# (build/test/state-diff moved to scripts/), and no "verilator".
H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
has '^  run '    "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'run'"
has '^  list '   "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'list'"
has '^  doctor ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing 'doctor'"
for c in build test state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
done
no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'developer command' "$H" && fail "release --help: developer commands moved to scripts/; drop the section:"$'\n'"$H"
ok "release --help: run/list/doctor only, no developer-commands section, no verilator"

# 2. The developer commands left the binary entirely: ANDESIM_DEV=1 --help adds
# NO commands (run/list/doctor only), and build/test/state-diff are no longer
# dispatchable (unknown command, rc 2).
D=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
for c in run list doctor; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing release command '$c'"
done
for c in build test state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "^  $c " "$D" && fail "dev --help: leaked removed/hidden command '$c'"
done
no_word "$D" || fail "dev --help: leaked 'verilator'"
for c in build test state-diff; do
  expect 2 "unknown command '$c'" "$BIN" "$c"
done
ok "dev --help: no developer commands; build/test/state-diff gone (rc 2)"

# 3. run --help: the --engine example reads vsim:, never verilator:; the
# --trigger menu offers only the supported triggers (marker|pc -- icount was
# removed, simpoint is unfinished).
RH=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
has 'vsim:' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing vsim: example"
no_word "$RH" || fail "run --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'simpoint' "$RH" && fail "run --help: leaked unfinished trigger 'simpoint':"$'\n'"$RH"
has 'trigger.*icount' "$RH" && fail "run --help: --trigger should not list removed 'icount':"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mem-size' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --mem-size:"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mmap-size' "$RH" && fail "run --help: retired --mmap-size alias should stay hidden:"$'\n'"$RH"

has '^  --verify '   "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --verify:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb '      "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb-port ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb-port:"$'\n'"$RH"
ok "run --help: vsim: example, no verilator/simpoint, --mem-size/--verify/--gdb documented"

# 4. list models: composition cells read vsim (never verilator), and NOTES show
# user-facing model traits only -- no implementation detail, no unfinished trigger.
LM=$("$BIN" list models 2>&1)
has 'vsim' "$LM" || fail "list models: missing vsim"
no_word "$LM" || fail "list models: leaked 'verilator'"
for d in 'transparent passthrough' 'pure from reset' 'simpoint' 'icount'; do
  has "$d" "$LM" && fail "list models: leaked implementation detail/removed-or-unfinished trigger '$d':"$'\n'"$LM"
done
ok "list models: vsim, no verilator, no implementation detail, no simpoint/icount"

# 5. list engines end to end: a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator"
# must surface as vsim: (the single normalization point), proving --engine /
# errors / list all speak the product name with no real sim_* needed.
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat >"$TMP/sim_fake" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"verilator:fakecfg","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc","icount"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
EOF
chmod +x "$TMP/sim_fake"
LE=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" list engines 2>&1)
has 'vsim:fakecfg' "$LE" || fail "list engines: fake not renamed to vsim:fakecfg:"$'\n'"$LE"
no_word "$LE" || fail "list engines: leaked 'verilator':"$'\n'"$LE"
# Triggers are a hybrid-MODEL option, not an engine attribute: `list engines`
# carries no TRIGGERS column (and so never leaks the unfinished simpoint trigger
# that the built-in qemu row used to advertise).
has 'TRIGGERS' "$LE" && fail "list engines: TRIGGERS is a hybrid-model option, not an engine column:"$'\n'"$LE"
has 'simpoint'  "$LE" && fail "list engines: leaked unfinished trigger 'simpoint':"$'\n'"$LE"
ok "list engines: a verilator-self-describing engine is shown as vsim:, no TRIGGERS column"

# 6. `list fixtures` is a developer target (internal test ELFs, not user
# workloads): release hides it; ANDESIM_DEV reveals it.
printf '%s\n' "$H" | grep -qw fixtures && fail "release --help: leaked 'fixtures' target"

printf '%s\n' "$LH" | grep -qw fixtures && fail "release list --help: leaked 'fixtures':"$'\n'"$LH"
has 'models' "$LH" || fail "release list --help: missing 'models' target:"$'\n'"$LH"
expect 2 "unknown target 'fixtures'" "$BIN" list fixtures
DLH=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$DLH" | grep -qw fixtures || fail "dev list --help: missing 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$DLH"
ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list fixtures >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "dev: list fixtures should succeed"
ok "list: fixtures is dev-only (release hides it; ANDESIM_DEV reveals it)"

# 7. The removed `build` command must not survive in user-facing hints: a
# missing artifact in `doctor` now points at scripts/build_all.sh.
DOC=$(VSIM_BIN=/no/such/vsim "$BIN" doctor 2>&1 || true)
printf '%s\n' "$DOC" | grep -q 'andesim build' && fail "doctor hint still names the removed 'andesim build':"$'\n'"$DOC"
printf '%s\n' "$DOC" | grep -q 'scripts/build_all.sh' || fail "doctor hint should point at scripts/build_all.sh:"$'\n'"$DOC"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-surface contract: the andesim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
# user-facing commands (run, list, doctor) and never the third-party simulator
# name "verilator". The former developer commands build/test/state-diff have
# moved OUT of the binary (build -> scripts/build_all.sh, test ->
# scripts/test_all.sh, state-diff -> the diff_states core behind `run --verify`):
# they are not listed in any help and are not dispatchable. The unfinished
# ROADMAP commands (profile, cluster, archive, replay, estimate) appear in no
# help at all. The cycle-accurate engine is presented as "vsim" everywhere --
# proven end to end with a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator" and
# must come back out as vsim:.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }

H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
has '^run '    "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'run':"$'\n'"$H"
has '^list '   "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'list':"$'\n'"$H"
has '^doctor ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'doctor':"$'\n'"$H"
for s in fast cycle hybrid; do
  has "^  $s " "$H" || fail "release --help: run missing subcommand '$s':"$'\n'"$H"
done
for t in models engines; do
  has "^  $t " "$H" || fail "release --help: list missing target '$t':"$'\n'"$H"
done
has 'REQUIRED for hybrid' "$H" || fail "release --help: --trigger not marked REQUIRED for hybrid:"$'\n'"$H"
for c in build test state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "(^|  )$c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
done
no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'developer command' "$H" && fail "release --help: developer commands moved to scripts/; drop the section:"$'\n'"$H"
has '^  fixtures ' "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked dev-only 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$H"

has '^  fixtures ' "$D" || fail "dev --help: should reveal the dev 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$D"
no_word "$D" || fail "dev --help: leaked 'verilator'"
for c in build test state-diff; do

done

has '^  --gdb-port ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb-port:"$'\n'"$RH"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# run --cosim contract (cosim_roi F4): opt-in checkpoint co-simulation.
#   1. hybrid marker --cosim --cosim-interval 500 -> >=1 checkpoint,
#      "[cosim] PASS", rc 0 (rt_c_v_matmul: ~1.7k ROI retires -> 3 ckpts)
#   2. hybrid pc --cosim                          -> same through cosim_pc
#   3. default (no --cosim)                       -> no cosim output
#   4. usage errors: model, trigger, interval, --verify exclusivity
#   5. dev-only help surface
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/roi.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_v_matmul}"
hybrid_resolve_paths
ENGINE="${ENGINE:-vsim:ax45mpv_premium}"

# 1. marker mode with a sub-ROI interval -> real checkpoints.
OUT=$("$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" \
      --cosim --cosim-interval 500 "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "marker --cosim rc=$RC: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q '\[cosim\] PASS' || fail "marker: no [cosim] PASS: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -Eq '\[cosim\] PASS: [1-9][0-9]* checkpoint' \
  || fail "marker: expected at least one checkpoint: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'window_cycles' \
  && fail "marker: window_cycles printed under --cosim (the checkpoints pollute it; mutually exclusive): $OUT"
ok "hybrid marker --cosim: checkpoints + final match the oracle, no cycle figure"

# 2. pc mode (boundaries = the fixture's own marker PCs, like docs 4.2).
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")") \
  || fail "no ROI markers in $VSIM_ELF"
OUT=$("$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENGINE" \
      --pc-start "0x${MARKERS%% *}" --pc-end "0x${MARKERS##* }" \
      --cosim --cosim-interval 500 "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "pc --cosim rc=$RC: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q '\[cosim\] PASS' || fail "pc: no [cosim] PASS: $OUT"
ok "hybrid pc --cosim: checkpoints + final match the oracle"

# 3. default off: no cosim leg, no cosim output, cycle figure intact.
OUT=$("$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" \
      "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "default hybrid rc=$RC: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -qi 'cosim' && fail "default run leaked cosim output: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'window_cycles' || fail "default: cycle figure missing: $OUT"
ok "default: co-simulation stays off, window_cycles stays on"

# 4. usage errors. (cycle --cosim is now valid: lock-step DV, see
#    test_andes_sim_cosim_lockstep.sh. Only fast is rejected here.)
expect 2 'cosim requires --mode hybrid or cycle' \
  "$BIN" run --mode fast --cosim "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'cosim-interval requires --cosim' \
  "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --cosim-interval 500 --engine "$ENGINE" "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'positive integer' \
  "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --cosim --cosim-interval 0 --engine "$ENGINE" "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'exclusive' \
  "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --cosim --verify --engine "$ENGINE" "$VSIM_ELF"
ok "--cosim usage errors (model/interval/--verify)"

# 5. dev-only help surface.
expect 0 ' --cosim ' env ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" run --help
OUT=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q -- '--cosim' && fail "release run --help leaks --cosim"
ok "--cosim help is dev-only"

ok "run --cosim checkpoint co-simulation"

537	Profiling ONE region you can name (a kernel)?

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# test_all.sh -- run the full andesim test surface. This is the entry point that
# replaced the former `andesim test` subcommand (which moved out of the binary).
#
# Phases (all run, in order, unless named explicitly):
#   unit      build/driver/andesim-*-test   the C++ driver unit tests
#   contract  tests/andes_sim/*.sh          driver feature + parity contracts
#   e2e       scripts/run_e2e.sh            hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]
#
# --dry-run prints the plan without executing (and without building). The
# contract and e2e phases need built artifacts -- run scripts/build_all.sh
# first. FILTER / MODE / JOBS pass through to scripts/run_e2e.sh unchanged.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

DRY_RUN=0
PHASES=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    unit|contract|e2e) PHASES+=("$arg") ;;
    *)
      echo "test_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
      echo "usage: test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done
[ "${#PHASES[@]}" -eq 0 ] && PHASES=(unit contract e2e)

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

pass=0
failed=0
declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()

# run_case NAME CMD...  -- execute one case, tally it, dump its log on failure.
run_case() {
  local name="$1"; shift
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "$name"; return; fi
  local log rc; log=$(mktemp)
  "$@" >"$log" 2>&1; rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
    ok "$name"; pass=$((pass + 1))
  else
    fail "$name (rc=$rc)"; failed=$((failed + 1)); FAILED_NAMES+=("$name")
    cat "$log"
  fi
  rm -f "$log"
}

run_unit() {
  step "[unit] C++ driver unit tests"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
    printf '  %s\n' "scripts/build_driver.sh" "build/driver/andesim-*-test (each)"
    return
  fi
  if ! bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null; then
    fail "[unit] build_driver.sh failed"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
  fi
  shopt -s nullglob
  local bins=("$ROOT"/build/driver/andesim-*-test)
  shopt -u nullglob
  if [ "${#bins[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
    fail "[unit] no unit-test binaries under build/driver"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
  fi
  local t
  for t in "${bins[@]}"; do run_case "[unit] $(basename "$t")" "$t"; done
}

run_contract() {
  step "[contract] driver feature + parity contracts"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
    printf '  %s\n' "tests/andes_sim/parity.sh" "tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh (each)"
    return
  fi
  local s
  for s in "$ROOT"/tests/andes_sim/parity.sh "$ROOT"/tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh; do
    [ -f "$s" ] || continue
    run_case "[contract] $(basename "$s")" bash "$s"
  done
}

run_e2e() {
  step "[e2e] hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "scripts/run_e2e.sh"; return; fi
  run_case "[e2e] run_e2e.sh" bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_e2e.sh"
}

for p in "${PHASES[@]}"; do
  case "$p" in
    unit)     run_unit ;;
    contract) run_contract ;;
    e2e)      run_e2e ;;
  esac
done

if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
  echo
  echo "(dry-run: nothing executed)"
  exit 0
fi

echo
step "summary: $pass passed, $failed failed"
if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
  fail "failed: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
  exit 1
fi

skills.name: simplify
skills.content:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).
