############ b9bd2be745 ############
contrib/plugins: add hotloops tool for hot inner-loop detection

A TCG plugin plus a wrapper script and docs for finding hot inner
loops in RISC-V workloads.

Plugin (contrib/plugins/hotloops.c):
- Detects loops by observing backward TB transitions: when the next
  executed translation block starts at a PC <= the last instruction
  PC of the previously executed TB, that pair (start_pc, end_pc) is
  a loop edge whose iteration count we tally.
- Args: limit=N (top-N rows, default 50), min_iters=N (drop loops
  below threshold). Output is sorted by iterations descending.

Wrapper (scripts/hotloops.sh):
- Takes a RISC-V ELF, auto-detects rv32/rv64, runs the baremetal
  qemu-system-<arch> with -bios <elf> and the plugin, then formats the
  result. Symbols are resolved via objdump and, when the ELF carries
  DWARF, source file:line via addr2line.
- Baremetal knobs: --machine (default andes_ae350), --cpu (default
  andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=1024), --qemu-config (-readconfig),
---- files ----
 contrib/plugins/hotloops.c  | 178 ++++++++++++++
 contrib/plugins/meson.build |   3 +-
 docs/hotloops.md            | 267 +++++++++++++++++++++
 scripts/hotloops.sh         | 550 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 4 files changed, 997 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

############ c17e6fc3f3 ############
hw/riscv/andes_ae350: honor -object memory-backend-file for DRAM

Adopt the modern machine->ram idiom used by virt.c and most other QEMU
machines: set mc->default_ram_id and let the machine framework either
auto-create an anonymous memory-backend (the existing behavior) or
consume a user-supplied -object memory-backend-file,id=mem (the new
capability). Replace the local memory_region_init_ram(main_mem, ...)
+ add_subregion(..., main_mem) pair with a single add_subregion that
binds the DRAM range to machine->ram.

Behavior is unchanged for users who do not pass -object memory-backend:
the framework auto-creates an anonymous backend with the default_ram_id,
identical to the prior init_ram call. Users who pass
-machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem now get DRAM backed by a shared
file - required for the hybrid-sim QEMU<->vsim shared-RAM round-trip on
this board.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---- files ----
 hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c | 11 ++++++-----
 1 file changed, 6 insertions(+), 5 deletions(-)

############ 9ff162fe19 ############
riscv/andes_ae350: add SimControl exit device at 0xe0080000

The vplat runtime exits via writes to 0xe0080000 (SimControl), but this
device was absent from the ae350 machine, causing all vplat ELFs to hang
indefinitely under QEMU.

Add an inline MemoryRegionOps handler at that address. Write semantics
match the vsim SimControl device: value < 256 is a raw exit code; the
magic values 0x01234567/68/71 exit 0 (pass/finish/skip) and
0x01234569/70 exit 1 (fail/warn).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---- files ----
 hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c         | 40 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 include/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.h |  1 +
 2 files changed, 41 insertions(+)

############ 9de79ec5aa ############
riscv/andes_ae350: rename andes_sim_ctrl_ops -> andesim_ctrl_ops

Follows the andes-sim -> andesim product rename in the parent repo. The
SimControl exit device's MemoryRegionOps is the only andes_sim-named
symbol; the real Andes hardware models (andes_ae350 board, andes_plic,
andes_atcsmu, andes_plmt) are intentionally untouched.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

/*
     * Register system main memory. machine->ram is the framework-owned
     * backend (mc->default_ram_id, set in class_init): passing
     * -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=<id> maps it onto a user backend
     * (e.g. memory-backend-file) for the hybrid-sim QEMU<->vsim shared-RAM
     * round-trip; otherwise an anonymous backend is auto-created (identical
     * to the previous init_ram behavior). The single backend spans both DRAM
     * windows through aliases -- its low main_size bytes map to DRAM, the
     * remaining ext_size bytes to DRAM_EXT.
     */
    MemoryRegion *main_mem = g_new(MemoryRegion, 1);
    memory_region_init_alias(main_mem, NULL, "riscv.andes.ae350.ram.main",
                             machine->ram, 0, main_size);
    memory_region_add_subregion(system_memory, memmap[ANDES_AE350_DRAM].base,
                                main_mem);

=== build_all.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# build_all.sh -- build the andesim artifacts. This is the entry point that
# replaced the former `andesim build` subcommand (which moved out of the driver
# binary). It only orchestrates the existing build scripts / Makefiles; the
# build logic itself lives in setup.sh, scripts/build_*.sh, and the Makefiles.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/build_all.sh [TARGET] [--dry-run]
#
# TARGET (default: all):
#   all       setup.sh (qemu + vsim + plugin + simpoint) then fixtures
#             (the fixtures Makefile also builds the runtime lib transitively)
#   qemu      build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64
#   vsim      verilator/build/sim_*
#   plugin    qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
#   simpoint  tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint
#   fixtures  tests/fixtures/*.elf (+ runtime lib)
#   runtime   build/runtime/ (libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o, andesim.ld, andesim.specs)
#
# --dry-run prints the underlying commands without running them.
#
# The andesim driver itself is NOT built here: ./andesim self-bootstraps via
# scripts/build_driver.sh on first use.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

TARGET=all
DRY_RUN=0
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    all|qemu|vsim|plugin|simpoint|fixtures|runtime) TARGET="$arg" ;;
    *)
      echo "build_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
      echo "usage: build_all.sh [all|qemu|vsim|plugin|simpoint|fixtures|runtime] [--dry-run]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done

# run one step: print it under --dry-run, otherwise banner + execute (inheriting
# stdio so the user watches the build live). set -e aborts on the first failure.
run() {
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$*"
    return
  fi
  printf '[build_all] %s\n' "$*"
  "$@"
}

# plugin needs an ABSOLUTE QEMU_ROOT: `make -C qemu_plugin` chdirs first, so a
# relative ./QEMU would resolve under qemu_plugin/ and miss the headers.
case "$TARGET" in
  all)      run bash "$ROOT/setup.sh"; run make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" ;;
  qemu)     run bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_qemu.sh" ;;
  vsim)     run bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_vsim.sh" ;;
  plugin)   run make -C "$ROOT/qemu_plugin" "QEMU_ROOT=$ROOT/QEMU" ;;
  simpoint) run bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_simpoint.sh" ;;
  fixtures) run make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" ;;
  runtime)  run make -C "$ROOT/runtime" ;;
esac

#

#   libhotloops.so        -- hot inner-loop detector (developer profiling tool)

QEMU_ROOT ?= /local/nick/qemu_v5
CC        ?= gcc

GLIB_CFLAGS := $(shell pkg-config --cflags glib-2.0)
GLIB_LIBS   := $(shell pkg-config --libs   glib-2.0)

CFLAGS  := -O2 -fPIC -Wall -Wextra -std=c11

LDFLAGS := -shared
